term_table.english_sentence_A: But if something is neither already hot in the way we are nor becomes such in approaching us, this is colder than the mixture of a human being, even if in some way or other the hot predominates in it.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But if something neither is already hot in the way we are nor becomes such on being brought near us, this is colder than the mixture of a human being, even if the hot predominates in it to whatever degree.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὥσπερ γὰρ εἰ δυοῖν μὲν ὑδάτοιν ἀμφοῖν μὲν θερμοῖν, ἀλλὰ τοῦ μὲν μᾶλλον, τοῦ δ’ ἧττον, ἐπιμίξαις τῷ μᾶλλον θερμῷ τὸ ἧττον, ἐκλύσεις αὐτοῦ τὴν θερμασίαν, οὕτως εἰ εἰς τὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ ῥοδίνου [554] θερμότητα χλιαρὰν ὑπάρχουσαν καὶ πρὸς τὴν ἀνθρώπου κρᾶσιν ἀναμίξαις ἀνθρωπείαν θερμότητα, καθαιρήσεις τι πάντως αὐτῆς καὶ καταψύξεις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For just as, if of two waters, both hot, but the one more and the other less, you were to mix the less hot into the more hot, you would slacken its warmth, so if into the heat from rose oil, which is lukewarm even in relation to the mixture of a human being, you were to mix in human heat, you would in every case take away something of it and cool it down.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For just as, if of two waters both are hot, but the one more so and the other less, and you mix the less hot into the more hot, you will slacken its warmth, so, if into the heat from rose oil, [554] which is lukewarm even relative to the mixture of a human being, you mix human heat, you will certainly take away something of it and cool it down.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὥσπερ γὰρ εἰ δυοῖν μὲν ὑδάτοιν ἀμφοῖν μὲν θερμοῖν, ἀλλὰ τοῦ μὲν μᾶλλον, τοῦ δ’ ἧττον, ἐπιμίξαις τῷ μᾶλλον θερμῷ τὸ ἧττον, ἐκλύσεις αὐτοῦ τὴν θερμασίαν, οὕτως εἰ εἰς τὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ ῥοδίνου [554] θερμότητα χλιαρὰν ὑπάρχουσαν καὶ πρὸς τὴν ἀνθρώπου κρᾶσιν ἀναμίξαις ἀνθρωπείαν θερμότητα, καθαιρήσεις τι πάντως αὐτῆς καὶ καταψύξεις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For just as, if of two waters, both hot, but the one more and the other less, you were to mix the less hot into the more hot, you would slacken its warmth, so if into the heat from rose oil, which is lukewarm even in relation to the mixture of a human being, you were to mix in human heat, you would in every case take away something of it and cool it down.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For just as, if of two waters both are hot, but the one more so and the other less, and you mix the less hot into the more hot, you will slacken its warmth, so, if into the heat from rose oil, [554] which is lukewarm even relative to the mixture of a human being, you mix human heat, you will certainly take away something of it and cool it down.

term_table.greek_sentence: Μὴ τοίνυν θαυμάζειν, εἴ τι τῶν ἰδίᾳ τε καὶ καθ’ αὑτὰ θερμῶν ἑτέρῳ θερμοτέρῳ προσαγόμενον ἐμψύχειν αὐτὸ δύναται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: One should not, then, be surprised if something that is hot in its own right and in itself, when brought to another hotter thing, is able to cool it.
term_table.english_sentence_B: One should not wonder, then, if one of the things that are hot individually and in themselves, when applied to another, hotter thing, is able to cool it.

term_table.english_sentence_A: For to it the same things often appear now hot, now cold: cold when it has become hotter, and hot when it has become colder.

term_table.english_sentence_A: And someone recently put to us the problem why we urinate cold in the baths but hot outside, not following that the urine itself is lukewarm in the same way both in the baths and outside, whereas we are not in the same condition with respect to the surface of the body while bathing and before it.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὅρος, Corc. ὄρvος IG 9(1).698.1 (written ὄρβος 700.1 ); Cret. and Arg. ὦρος SIG 685.59 , Mnemos. 42.332 ; Heracl. ὄρος Tab.Heracl. 1.53 , al., cf. ἄντορος; Ion. οὖρος GDI 5518 and 5493b25 , Democr. 4 , Hdt. (v. infr.) (also Theraean IG 12(3).436 ); Megarian ὄρρος (?) Berl.Sitzb. 1888.885 , cf. ὁμορέω: ὁ:—boundary, landmark, ἀμφ' οὔροισι δύ' ἀνέρε δηριάασθον Il. 12.421 ; λίθον . . , τόν ῥ' ἄνδρες πρότεροι θέσαν ἔμμεναι οὖρον ἀρούρης 21.405 ; ἐγὼ δὲ τούτων ὥσπερ ἐν μεταιχμίῳ ὅ. κατέστην Sol. ap. Arist. Ath. 12.5 : the regions separated by the boundary are usu. in gen., οὖρος τῆς Μηδικῆς ἀρχῆς καὶ τῆς Λυδικῆς Hdt. 1.72 , etc.: in dat., οὐδεὶς ὅρος ἐκ θεῶν χρηστοῖς οὐδὲ κακοῖς E. HF 669 (lyr.): with a single gen., ῥεῖθρον ἠπείροιν ὅρον A. Pr. 790 ; γάμου ὅ. the time within which one may marry, Pl. Lg. 785b ; οἱ ὅ. τῶν διαστημάτων the notes which limit the intervals in the musical scale, Id. Phlb. 17d , cf. Aristox. Harm. pp.49,56 M. ; ὅροι τρεῖς ἁρμονίας . . , νεάτης τε καὶ ὑπάτης καὶ μέσης Pl. R. 443d ; ἐς ἑβδομήκοντα ἔτεα οὖρον τῆς ζόης ἀνθρώπῳ προτίθημι I set the limit of human life at seventy years, Hdt. 1.32 , cf. 74 , 216 ; ζωᾶς ὅρον ἡμετέρας B. 5.144 : abs., εἰς τὸν τόπον . . , ἐν οἷς ἂν . . ὅρους θῶνται τῶν ὠνίων wherever (they) appoint fixed places for trading, Pl. Lg. 849e ; decision of a magistrate, ὅρον δώσω PThead. 15.20 (iii A.D.); so ὅρον προσγράψαι D. 23.40 ; ὅρους τοῖς βαρβάροις πήξαντες Lycurg. 73 ; εἷς ὅρος παγήσεται Th. 4.92 ; τὸν ὅρον ὑπερβάντες Pl. R. 373d , etc.: also in pl., bounds, boundaries, ἐν οὔροισι χώρης Hdt. 4.52 , cf. 125 ; τοὺς Αἰγυπτίων οὔρους Id. 2.17 ; ὑπὸ Κυλλάνας ὅροις Pi. O. 6.77 ; γῆς ἐπ' ἐσχάτοις ὅροις A. Pr. 666 ; τὸ ἀκόντιον ἔξω τῶν ὅ. τῆς αὑτοῦ πορείας . . ἐξενεχθὲν ἔτρωσεν αὐτόν Antipho 3.2.4 ; ἐντὸς ὅρων Ἡρακλείων Pl. Ti. 25c . metaph., ὅροι θεσπεσίας ὁδοῦ A. Ag. 1154 (lyr.); θῆλυς ὅ. the boundary of a woman's mind, v. ἐπινέμω 11.3 . memorial stone or pillar, Hdt. 1.93 : esp. pillar (whether inscribed or not, cf. Harp. ) set up on mortgaged property, to serve as a bond or register of the debt, Sol. 36 ; ὅπως . . ὅροι τεθεῖεν Is. 6.36 : with gen. of the amount, τίθησιν ὅρους ἐπὶ μὲν τὴν οἰκίαν δισχιλίων (sc. δραχμῶν), ἐπὶ δὲ τὸ χωρίον ταλάντου D. 31.1 , cf. 25.69 ; δανείζειν τοὺς ἱερέας . . ἐπὶ χωρίῳ . . καὶ ὅρον ἐφιστάναι IG 22.1183.29 , cf. D. 41.6 , Thphr. Char. 10.9 : specimens are IG 12(7).412 (Amorgos), 22.2642 ,al. boundary-stone marking the limits of temple-lands, ὅ. τοῦ ἱεροῦ ib. 12.858 , cf. 860 , 22.2597 , al.; ὅρος· μὴ τοιχοδομεῖν ἐντὸς τῶν ὅρων ἰδιώτην ib. 7.422 (Orop.), cf. 1785 (Thesp.), etc. ; ὅ. κρήνης, λεσχέων δημοσίων, ὁδοῦ, etc., ib. 12.874 , 888 , 877 , etc. ; similarly, ὅ. σήματος ib. 903 , al., 22.2568 , al.; ὅ. μνημάτων ib. 12.906 ; ὅ. μνήματος ib. 22.2527 , al.; ὅ. θήκης ib. 2586 , al. standard, measure, ἢν δ' ἄγαν δοκῶ χρονίζειν . . Answ. τοῦδ' ὅ. τίς ἐστί μοι; E. IT 1219 ; ὅροι τῶν ἀγαθῶν καὶ κανόνες D. 18.296 ; rule, canon, εἷς ὅρος, μία βροτοῖσίν ἐστιν εὐτυχίας ὁδός B. Fr. 7 ; ὅρον πολιτείας ὁλιγαρχικῆς ταξάμενοι πλῆθος χρημάτων Pl. R. 551a ; ἀριστοκρατίας ὅρος ἀρετή, ὀλιγαρχίας πλοῦτος Arist. Pol. 1294a10 ; ὁμολογίᾳ θέμενοι ὅρον, εἰς τοῦτο ἀποβλέποντες καὶ ἀναφέροντες τὴν σκέψιν ποιώμεθα Pl. Phdr. 237d : hence, end, aim, ἕν' ὅ. θέμενος παντὶ τρόπῳ μ' ἀνελεῖν D. 21.105 . in Logic, term of a proposition (whether subject or predicate), Arist. APr. 24b16 , Cael. 282a1 , al. ; ὅ. μέσος the middle term, Id. EN 1142b24 , cf. APr. 25b33 sq. : hence, definition, ἔστι ὅ. λόγος ὁ τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι σημαίνων Id. Top. 101b39 , cf. 139a24 , al. ; defined as ἡ τοῦ ἰδίου ἀπόδοσις Chrysipp.Stoic. 2.75 : in pl., title of pseudo-Platonic work. premiss of a syllogism, ὅ. κατηγορικοί, στερητικοί, Arist. APr. 29a21 , cf. 31b33 , al. Math., term of a ratio or proportion, Archyt. 2 , Arist. EN 1131b5 sqq., Euc. 5 Def. 8 , Nicom. Ar. 1.8 . pl., terms, conditions, συνθέσθαι πρός τινα ἐπὶ ὅροις, ὥστε . . CPR 19.8 (iv A.D.). Astrol., οἱ τρεῖς ὅ. the three terms, used in various calculations, Vett. Val. 304.1 , al. (Spir. lenis in some dialects which have not lost spir. asper is inferred from absence of a sign for h in Corc. ὄρvος, Arg.ὦρος, Heracl. ὄρος, cf. ἄντορος.)

term_table.english_sentence_B: For the water will appear to you not lukewarm but considerably cold.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἥσσων, ἧσσον, gen. ονος; Att. ἥττων, Ion. ἥσσων (not ἕσσων) Hdt. (v. infr.), Democr. 50 , Hp. VC 2 : formed from ἦκα (prop. ἠσσ-, cf. ἤκιστος), but in sense Comp. of κακός, μικρός: c. gen. pers., inferior; esp. in force, weaker, αἴθ' ὅσον ἥ. εἰμὶ τόσον σέο φέρτερος εἴην Il. 16.722 ; of horses, 23.322 , al.; ῥώμῃ ἥσσονες τῶν Περσέων Hdt. 8 113 , cf. 9.62 ; γυναικῶν ἥσσονες S. Ant. 680 ; Κύπριδος E. Andr. 631 ; ἔς τι in a thing, Hdt. 3.102 : c. inf. modi, ἥσς. τινὸς θέειν not so good at running, ib. 105 ; οὐδενὸς ἥσς. γνῶναι second to none in judging, Th. 2.60 ; ἱππεύειν ἥττ. τῶν ἡλίκων inferior to them in riding, X. Cyr. 1.3.15 . abs., οἱ ἥσς. the weaker party, A. Supp. 203 , 489 ; οὐχ ἥσσους γενέσθαι to have the best of it, Th. 4.72 ; τὸ λαμβάνειν τὰ τῶν ἡττ. X. An. 5.6.32 : c. dat. modi, ἥσσονες ναυμαχίῃ Hdt. 5.86 : c. acc. modi, τὸν νοῦν ἥσς. S. El. 1023 , cf. X. Cyr. 1.4.4 ; of things, τὸν ἥττω λόγον κρείττω ποιεῖν 'to make the worse appear the better cause', Pl. Ap. 18b , cf. Ar. Nu. 114 : pl., οἱ ἥττους λόγοι ib. 1042 , Isoc. 15.15 ; τὸ ἧσς. ἀδικία νέμεις E. Supp. 379 (lyr.). less, fewer, ἵνα πλείω μὲν ἀκούωμεν, ἥττονα δὲ λέγωμεν Zeno Stoic. 1.68 . c. gen. rei, giving way or yielding to a thing, a slave to . . , τοῦ τῆσδ' ἔρωτος εἰς ἅπανθ' ἥσς. S. Tr. 489 ; τῶν αἰσχρῶν Id. Ant. 747 ; ὀργῆς Id. Fr. 929 ; γάμων E. IA 1354 ; κέρδους Ar. Pl. 363 ; ἡδονῶν Pl. Prt. 353c ; γαστρὸς ἢ οἴνου ἢ ἀφροδισίων ἢ πόνου ἢ ὕπνου X. Mem. 1.5.1 ; χρημάτων Democr. l.c., Theopomp.Hist. 121 : generally, unable to resist, τοῦ πεπρωμένου E. Hel. 1660 ; νόσων καὶ γήρως Lys. 2.78 ; οἱ ἥττους τῶν πόνων [ἵπποι] X. Eq.Mag. 1.3 , 2.78 . neut. ἧσσον, ἧττον, as Adv., less, ὀλίγον δέ τί μ' ἧσς. ἐτίμα Od. 15.365 , cf. E. Hipp. 264 (anap.); ἧσσόν τι Th. 3.75 ; ἧσς. ἑτέρων Id. 1.84 ; ὁμοίως τε τρωθεὶς καὶ ἧσς. Hp.l.c.: mostly with Verbs, but also with Adjs., ἀριστοκρατίαι . . αἱ μὲν ἧττ., αἱ δὲ μᾶλλον μόνιμοι Arist. Pol. 1307a14 , cf. Mete. 340b8 : with a Comp. , ἧττ. ἀκριβέστερον Id. Pr. 957b8 ; ἧττ. εὐληπτοτέραν D.H. 3.43 codd.: with neg., οὐχ ἧσς., οὐδ' ἧσς., not a whit less, just as much, A. Ch. 181 , 708 , Th. 1.8 ; οὐδὲν ἧσς., μηδὲν ἧσς., S. Aj. 276 , 1329 ; for τὸ μᾶλλον καὶ ἧττ., v. μάλα .
term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δὲ εὐθὺς εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ βαλανεῖον ἅπτοιο τοῦ κατὰ τὸν καδίσκον ὕδατος, ἧττόν σοι φανεῖται ψυχρόν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But if, immediately upon entering the bath, you were to touch the water in the pail, it will appear less cold to you.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But if immediately upon entering the bath you touch the water in the tub, it will appear less cold to you.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ οὐδὲν θαυμαστὸν, εἴ γε καὶ τὰ πολλὰ τῶν φρεατιαίων ὑδάτων, ὅσα βαθείας ἔχει τὰς πηγὰς ἐν τῷ χειμῶνι ψαυόμενα, χλιαρὰ φαίνεται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And there is nothing surprising in this, if indeed also most well waters, those that have deep springs, appear lukewarm when touched in winter.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And there is nothing surprising in this, since most well waters too, those that have deep sources, when touched in winter appear lukewarm.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὅρος, Corc. ὄρvος IG 9(1).698.1 (written ὄρβος 700.1 ); Cret. and Arg. ὦρος SIG 685.59 , Mnemos. 42.332 ; Heracl. ὄρος Tab.Heracl. 1.53 , al., cf. ἄντορος; Ion. οὖρος GDI 5518 and 5493b25 , Democr. 4 , Hdt. (v. infr.) (also Theraean IG 12(3).436 ); Megarian ὄρρος (?) Berl.Sitzb. 1888.885 , cf. ὁμορέω: ὁ:—boundary, landmark, ἀμφ' οὔροισι δύ' ἀνέρε δηριάασθον Il. 12.421 ; λίθον . . , τόν ῥ' ἄνδρες πρότεροι θέσαν ἔμμεναι οὖρον ἀρούρης 21.405 ; ἐγὼ δὲ τούτων ὥσπερ ἐν μεταιχμίῳ ὅ. κατέστην Sol. ap. Arist. Ath. 12.5 : the regions separated by the boundary are usu. in gen., οὖρος τῆς Μηδικῆς ἀρχῆς καὶ τῆς Λυδικῆς Hdt. 1.72 , etc.: in dat., οὐδεὶς ὅρος ἐκ θεῶν χρηστοῖς οὐδὲ κακοῖς E. HF 669 (lyr.): with a single gen., ῥεῖθρον ἠπείροιν ὅρον A. Pr. 790 ; γάμου ὅ. the time within which one may marry, Pl. Lg. 785b ; οἱ ὅ. τῶν διαστημάτων the notes which limit the intervals in the musical scale, Id. Phlb. 17d , cf. Aristox. Harm. pp.49,56 M. ; ὅροι τρεῖς ἁρμονίας . . , νεάτης τε καὶ ὑπάτης καὶ μέσης Pl. R. 443d ; ἐς ἑβδομήκοντα ἔτεα οὖρον τῆς ζόης ἀνθρώπῳ προτίθημι I set the limit of human life at seventy years, Hdt. 1.32 , cf. 74 , 216 ; ζωᾶς ὅρον ἡμετέρας B. 5.144 : abs., εἰς τὸν τόπον . . , ἐν οἷς ἂν . . ὅρους θῶνται τῶν ὠνίων wherever (they) appoint fixed places for trading, Pl. Lg. 849e ; decision of a magistrate, ὅρον δώσω PThead. 15.20 (iii A.D.); so ὅρον προσγράψαι D. 23.40 ; ὅρους τοῖς βαρβάροις πήξαντες Lycurg. 73 ; εἷς ὅρος παγήσεται Th. 4.92 ; τὸν ὅρον ὑπερβάντες Pl. R. 373d , etc.: also in pl., bounds, boundaries, ἐν οὔροισι χώρης Hdt. 4.52 , cf. 125 ; τοὺς Αἰγυπτίων οὔρους Id. 2.17 ; ὑπὸ Κυλλάνας ὅροις Pi. O. 6.77 ; γῆς ἐπ' ἐσχάτοις ὅροις A. Pr. 666 ; τὸ ἀκόντιον ἔξω τῶν ὅ. τῆς αὑτοῦ πορείας . . ἐξενεχθὲν ἔτρωσεν αὐτόν Antipho 3.2.4 ; ἐντὸς ὅρων Ἡρακλείων Pl. Ti. 25c . metaph., ὅροι θεσπεσίας ὁδοῦ A. Ag. 1154 (lyr.); θῆλυς ὅ. the boundary of a woman's mind, v. ἐπινέμω 11.3 . memorial stone or pillar, Hdt. 1.93 : esp. pillar (whether inscribed or not, cf. Harp. ) set up on mortgaged property, to serve as a bond or register of the debt, Sol. 36 ; ὅπως . . ὅροι τεθεῖεν Is. 6.36 : with gen. of the amount, τίθησιν ὅρους ἐπὶ μὲν τὴν οἰκίαν δισχιλίων (sc. δραχμῶν), ἐπὶ δὲ τὸ χωρίον ταλάντου D. 31.1 , cf. 25.69 ; δανείζειν τοὺς ἱερέας . . ἐπὶ χωρίῳ . . καὶ ὅρον ἐφιστάναι IG 22.1183.29 , cf. D. 41.6 , Thphr. Char. 10.9 : specimens are IG 12(7).412 (Amorgos), 22.2642 ,al. boundary-stone marking the limits of temple-lands, ὅ. τοῦ ἱεροῦ ib. 12.858 , cf. 860 , 22.2597 , al.; ὅρος· μὴ τοιχοδομεῖν ἐντὸς τῶν ὅρων ἰδιώτην ib. 7.422 (Orop.), cf. 1785 (Thesp.), etc. ; ὅ. κρήνης, λεσχέων δημοσίων, ὁδοῦ, etc., ib. 12.874 , 888 , 877 , etc. ; similarly, ὅ. σήματος ib. 903 , al., 22.2568 , al.; ὅ. μνημάτων ib. 12.906 ; ὅ. μνήματος ib. 22.2527 , al.; ὅ. θήκης ib. 2586 , al. standard, measure, ἢν δ' ἄγαν δοκῶ χρονίζειν . . Answ. τοῦδ' ὅ. τίς ἐστί μοι; E. IT 1219 ; ὅροι τῶν ἀγαθῶν καὶ κανόνες D. 18.296 ; rule, canon, εἷς ὅρος, μία βροτοῖσίν ἐστιν εὐτυχίας ὁδός B. Fr. 7 ; ὅρον πολιτείας ὁλιγαρχικῆς ταξάμενοι πλῆθος χρημάτων Pl. R. 551a ; ἀριστοκρατίας ὅρος ἀρετή, ὀλιγαρχίας πλοῦτος Arist. Pol. 1294a10 ; ὁμολογίᾳ θέμενοι ὅρον, εἰς τοῦτο ἀποβλέποντες καὶ ἀναφέροντες τὴν σκέψιν ποιώμεθα Pl. Phdr. 237d : hence, end, aim, ἕν' ὅ. θέμενος παντὶ τρόπῳ μ' ἀνελεῖν D. 21.105 . in Logic, term of a proposition (whether subject or predicate), Arist. APr. 24b16 , Cael. 282a1 , al. ; ὅ. μέσος the middle term, Id. EN 1142b24 , cf. APr. 25b33 sq. : hence, definition, ἔστι ὅ. λόγος ὁ τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι σημαίνων Id. Top. 101b39 , cf. 139a24 , al. ; defined as ἡ τοῦ ἰδίου ἀπόδοσις Chrysipp.Stoic. 2.75 : in pl., title of pseudo-Platonic work. premiss of a syllogism, ὅ. κατηγορικοί, στερητικοί, Arist. APr. 29a21 , cf. 31b33 , al. Math., term of a ratio or proportion, Archyt. 2 , Arist. EN 1131b5 sqq., Euc. 5 Def. 8 , Nicom. Ar. 1.8 . pl., terms, conditions, συνθέσθαι πρός τινα ἐπὶ ὅροις, ὥστε . . CPR 19.8 (iv A.D.). Astrol., οἱ τρεῖς ὅ. the three terms, used in various calculations, Vett. Val. 304.1 , al. (Spir. lenis in some dialects which have not lost spir. asper is inferred from absence of a sign for h in Corc. ὄρvος, Arg.ὦρος, Heracl. ὄρος, cf. ἄντορος.)
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο λουόμενοι μὲν ψυχρὸν τὸ οὖρον, ἐῤῥιγωκότες δ’ ἐν κρύει, τὸ φρεατιαῖον ὕδωρ θερμὸν εἶναι νομίζομεν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And for this reason, when bathing we think the urine cold, but when we have been shivering in the frost we think the well water hot.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For this reason, when bathing we think the urine cold, and when we have been chilled in frost we think well-water hot.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: διάθεσις, εως, ἡ, (διατίθημι) placing in order, arrangement ( ἡ τοῦ ἔχοντος μέρη τάξις Arist. Metaph. 1022b1 ), Antipho Soph. 24a ; πολιτείας Pl. Lg. 710b ; τῶν ξενίων Id. Ti. 27a . disposition or composition in a work of art (opp.εὕρεσις), Id. Phdr. 236a ; opp.ἱστορία, μῦθος, Plb. 34.4.1 , Plu. Arat. 32 , etc.; δ. ᾠδῆς Eup. 303 ; τῶν ἐπῶν Phryn.Com. 55 ; plan of a building, Plu. Per. 13 ; subject of a picture, etc., Polem. ap. Ath. 5.210b ; δ. μυθολογίας Plu. 2.16b ; representation in a play, Hero Aut. 20.2 : in pl., word-painting, Plu. 2.17b ; of geographical description, Str. 1.1.16 ; rhetorical art, μετ' αὐξήσεως καὶ διαθέσεως Plb. 2.61.1 . in oratory, delivery, Plu. Rh. 1372a33 (possibly, inventive disposition). δ. ἔγγραφος written report, POxy. 52.13 (iv A.D.). = διάθεμα , Procl. inCra. p.10P. (pl.). (from Pass. ) bodily state, condition, Hp. VM 7 , Arist. GA 778b34 ; δ. τοῦ σώματος Philem. 95.4 ; δ. ὑγιεινή, νοσώδης, Gal. 5.826 , 17(2).238 ; ἕξις defined as δ. μόνιμος Id. 5.826 ; νευρικὴ δ. OGI 331.11 (Pergam.); of the mind, Antipho Soph. 24a ; ἕξις ψυχῆς καὶ δ. Pl. Phlb. 11d ; distd. from ἕξις, Arist. Cat. 8b28 , de An. 417b15 , Zeno and Chrysipp.Stoic. 1.50 , 3.111 ; δ. ἁμαρτωλός Phld. Lib. p.560 ., al.; δ. σωματική, ψυχική, A.D. Synt. 278.10 : pl., Diotog. ap. Stob. 4.7.62 . disposition towards persons, Pl. R. 489a ; propensity, Cic. Att. 14.3.2 ; πρός τινα Sch. E. Hec. 8 . generally, state, condition, τὴν βασιγείαν εἰς τὴν ἀρχαίαν δ. κατέστησεν OGI 219.11 (Sigeum, iv/iii B.C.). Gramm., force, function, τοῦ ὀνόματος δ. εἰσὶ δύο, ἐνέργεια καὶ πάθος (e.g. κριτής, κριτός) D.T. 637.29 ; esp. of the voices of the verb, δ. εἰσὶ τρεῖς, ἐνέργεια, πάθος, μεσότης Id. 638.8 ; δ. παθητική, μέση, A.D. Synt. 210.19 , 226.10 ; also of tense, χρονικὴ δ. ib. 251.1 (s.v.l.); διαβατικὴ δ. transitive force, ib. 43.18 .
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ εἴπερ τῶν διαθέσεων ἐν αἷς ὄντες ἀμφοτέρων ἐψαύσαμεν ἐπιλαθοίμεθα, μόνης τῆς γεγενημένης ἡμῖν αἰσθήσεως μεμνημένοι, τάχ’ ἀποφηναίμεθα ἄν ποτε τὸ μὲν ὕδωρ ἁπλῶς θερμὸν εἶναι, τὸ δ’ οὖρον ψυχρόν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And if we should forget the conditions in which we were when we touched both, remembering only the sensation that came to us, we might perhaps at some point declare that the water is simply hot and the urine simply cold.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And if we were to forget the conditions we were in when we touched each of them, remembering only the sensation that arose in us, we might perhaps at some time declare the water to be hot simply and the urine cold.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: οὐδέτερ-ος, α, ον, not either, neither of the two, Hdt. 1.51 , Ar. Ra. 1412 , Pl. Phlb. 21e : in pl., when each party is pl., first in Hes. Th. 638 , Sc. 171 , cf. Hdt. 1.76 , etc.: divisim, v. ἕτερος 1 . Adv. οὐδετέρως in neither of two ways, Pl. Lg. 902c : also neut. pl. as Adv., = οὐδετέρως , Id. Plt. 258a , Tht. 184a , etc. neutral, τῶν μὲν αἱρετῶν οὐσῶν, τῶν δὲ φευκτῶν, τῶν δ' οὐ. Arist. EN 1175b26 : so in Medic., of a state which is neither illness nor health, διάθεσις Herophil. ap. Gal. 6.388 ; σῶμα Gal. 1.307 , 311 . in Gramm., neuter, ἀρσενικῶν καὶ θηλυκῶν καὶ οὐ. D.H. Amm. 2.10 ; τὸ οὐ. (sc. γένος) the neuter gender, A.D. Pron. 6.19 . Adv. -ρως in the neuter, Id. Synt. 199.20 , Gal. 9.458 , Ath. 15.701a ; also of Verbs, οὐδετέρα διάθεσις Sch.D.T. p.246 H.
term_table.greek_sentence: ἔστι δ’ οὐδέτερον ἁπλῶς οὔτε θερμὸν οὔτε ψυχρὸν, ἀλλ’ ὡς πρὸς ἡμᾶς· καὶ οὐδὲ πρὸς ἡμᾶς αὖ πάλιν ἁπλῶς, ἀλλ’ ὡδί πως ἔχοντας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But neither of them is simply either hot or cold, but only in relation to us; and not even in relation to us simply, again, but to us as being in a certain condition.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But neither is either hot or cold simply; each is so relative to us. And again, it is not even relative to us simply, but relative to us when we are in some particular state.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἁπλῶς δ’ ἂν πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὁποῖόν ἐστιν ἑκάτερον λέγοιτο πρὸς τὴν μέσην καὶ ἁρίστην ἡμῶν κρᾶσιν ἐξεταζόμενον, ὥσπερ εἰ καὶ πρὸς ἄνθρωπον ἁπλῶς ἐδοκιμάζετο, πάντως ἄν που πρός τε τὸν εὔκρατον ἡ ἐξέτασις ἐγίγνετο.
term_table.english_sentence_A: What each of them is simply in relation to us would be stated when it is examined in relation to our middle and best mixture, just as, if it were being tested in relation to man simply, the examination would surely in any case be made in relation to the well-mixed man.
term_table.english_sentence_B: What each of them is simply relative to us would be stated when it is examined against our middle and best mixture; just as, if it were being tested against man simply, the examination would surely be made against the well-mixed man.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἤρτηται τοίνυν καὶ ταῦτα πάντα τὰ σφάλματα τῆς τῶν ὀνομάτων διαιρέσεως, ἧς ὀλίγου δεῖν ἅπαντες καταφρονοῦσιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: All these errors too, then, depend on the division of names, which almost everyone despises.
term_table.english_sentence_B: All these errors, then, depend on the division of names, which almost everyone despises.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: διαίρ-εσις, εως, ἡ, divisibility, Arist. Metaph. 1016b4 , al. Medic., dissection, ζῴων Gal. 4.664 . venesection, Antyll. ap. Orib. 7.9.2 . surgical operation, Phld. term_table.greek_sentence: [557] ἐπεὶ γὰρ ψυχρὸν καὶ θερμὸν τὸ μὲν ἁπλῶς λέγεται, τὸ δ’ ἐπικρατείᾳ, τὸ δὲ τῇ πρὸς τὸ σύμμετρον ὁμογενὲς παραβολῇ, τὸ δὲ πρὸς ὁτιοῦν τὸ ἐπιτυχὸν εὐλόγως ἐν ταῖς ὁμωνυμίαις σφαλλόμεθα πολλάκις, ἐπιλανθανόμενοι μὲν ὁποῖόν τι θερμὸν κρίνομεν, ἐφ’ ἕτερον δὲ μεταβαίνοντες.

term_table.greek_sentence: Οὔτε γὰρ ἁπλῶς θερμὸν ἕκαστον αὐτῶν ἐστιν, ὥσπερ τὸ πῦρ· τοῦτο μὲν γὰρ ἂν καὶ ἀδύνατον· οὔτ’ εἰ κατ’ ἐπικράτησιν, ὥσπερ τὸ αἷμα, πρόκειται σκοπεῖν· ἀλλ’ οὐδ’ εἰ πρὸς τὸ σύμμετρον ὁμογενὲς ἢ ὁμοειδὲς λέγεται θερμὸν, ὥσπερ λέων μὲν ἐν ζώοις, τὸ δ’ ἀκμάζον ἐν ἑκάστῳ τῶν εἰδῶν πρὸς τὸ γεγηρακός.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For neither is each of them hot simply, as fire is—for that would indeed be impossible—nor is it proposed to examine whether it is hot by predominance, as blood is; nor yet whether it is called hot in relation to the well-proportioned thing of the same genus or of the same species, as a lion is among animals, and as that which is in its prime, within each of the species, is in relation to that which has grown old.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For neither is each of them hot simply, as fire is (that would indeed be impossible), nor is the proposed inquiry whether it is hot by predominance, as blood is; nor yet whether it is called hot in relation to what is well-proportioned of the same genus or of the same species, as a lion is among animals, and, in each of the species, what is in its prime relative to what has grown old.

Sens. 51 . Geom., δύο εἴδη τῷ εἴδει δεδομένα two figures given in species, Euc. Dat. 53 , etc.; esp. in central conics, rectangle formed by a transverse diameter and the corresponding parameter, Apollon.Perg. Con. 1.14 , 21 , al.; also, species of numbers, of the terms in an algebraical expression involving different powers of the unknown quantity, Dioph. Def. 11 . form, kind, or nature, τῶν ἀλλέων παιγνιέων τὰ εἴδεα Hdt. 1.94 ; τὸ εἶ. τῆς νόσου Th. 2.50 , etc.; ἐν ἁρμονίας εἴδει εἶναι, γενέσθαι, to be or become like . . , Pl. Phd. 91d , cf. Cra. 394d ; ὡς ἐν φαρμάκου εἴδει by way of medicine, Id. R. 389b ; νόμων ἔχει εἶδος is in the province of law, Arist. Pol. 1286a3 ; situation, state of things, σκέψασθε ἐν οἵῳ εἴδει . . τοῦτο ἔπραξαν Th. 3.62 ; plan of action, policy, ἐπὶ εἶδος τρέπεσθαι Id. 6.77 , 8.56 ; ἐπ' ἄλλ' εἶδος τρέπεσθαι take up another line, Ar. term_table.english_sentence_A: For neither is each of them hot simply, as fire is—for that would indeed be impossible—nor is it proposed to examine whether it is hot by predominance, as blood is; nor yet whether it is called hot in relation to the well-proportioned thing of the same genus or of the same species, as a lion is among animals, and as that which is in its prime, within each of the species, is in relation to that which has grown old.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For neither is each of them hot simply, as fire is (that would indeed be impossible), nor is the proposed inquiry whether it is hot by predominance, as blood is; nor yet whether it is called hot in relation to what is well-proportioned of the same genus or of the same species, as a lion is among animals, and, in each of the species, what is in its prime relative to what has grown old.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὥστε ἐν τῇ πείρᾳ καὶ τὰ τῆς κρίσεως ἔσται καὶ τὰ τῆς διαγνώσεως, ἣν ἀφέντες οἱ πολλοὶ τῶν ἰατρῶν εἰ ἐρυθρόν ἐστιν τὸ ῥόδον ἢ εὐῶδες ἐπισκοποῦνται, παρέντες ὅταν ἐγκαυθῶσι τὴν κεφαλὴν, ἐπιτιθέντες αὐτῇ ῥόδων στεφάνους, ἢ τὸν χυλὸν αὐτῶν, ἢ ῥόδινον ἔλαιον, οὕτω τῇ πείρᾳ μαθεῖν τὸ γιγνόμενον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So that both the matter of judgement and that of discrimination will lie in experience, which most physicians abandon, inquiring instead whether the rose is red or fragrant, and neglecting, when they have been overheated in the head, to put on it garlands of roses, or their juice, or rose oil, and so to learn by experience what happens.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν ἴσῳ τὸ ψυκτικὸν εἶναι ἀνθρώπου φύσεως, ἀεὶ γὰρ τούτου χρὴ μεμνῆσθαι, καίτοι μυριάκις μὲν ἐγὼ διατελῶ λέγων αὐτὸ, παρακούουσι δ’ οἱ πολλοὶ καὶ συγγινώσκειν αὐτοῖς χρὴ διεστραμμένοις ὑπὸ τῶν σοφιστῶν ληρούντων μακρά.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For if they are heated up, it would rather be hot; but if they are cooled, cold — which is the same as saying that it is cooling in relation to human nature; for one must always keep this in mind, although I never cease saying it countless times, while most people mishear it, and one must pardon them, perverted as they are by sophists who talk nonsense at length.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Here 'cold' is equivalent to being cooling of the nature of man, for one must always remember this. Yet although I keep saying it countless times, most people mishear it, and one must forgive them, perverted as they have been by the sophists who drivel at length.

Vect. 4.1 : generally, function, faculty, δύναμις φυσική, ζωική, ψυχική, Gal. 10.635 ; περὶ φυσικῶν δ., title of work by Galen. in pl., agencies, ὑπάρχειν ἐν τῇ φύσει τὰς τοιαύτας δυνάμεις (sc. the gods) Polystr. p.10 W. function, meaning, of part in whole, Id. p.17 W. in Music, function, value, of a note in the scale, δ. ἐστι τάξις φθόγγου ἐν συστήματι Cleonid. Harm. 14 , cf. Aristox. Harm. p.69M. ; μέση κατὰ δύναμιν, opp. κατὰ θέσιν, Ptol. Harm. 2.5 . faculty, art, or craft, Pl. R. 532d , Arist. Metaph. 1018a30 , EN 1094a10 , Arr. Epict. 1.1.1 ; δ. σκεπτική the doctrine of the Sceptics, S.E. M. 7.1 . a medicine, Timostr. 7 , etc.; δ. ἁπλαῖ Hp. Decent. 9 , Aret. CD 1.4 , etc.; δ. πολυφάρμακοι Plu. 2.403c , Gal. 13.365 : in pl., collection of formulae or prescriptions, Orib. 10.33 . action of medicines, περὶ τῆς ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων δ., title of work by Galen; also, potency, δυνάμει θερμά, ψυχρά, Id. 1.672 , al. magically potent substance or object, PMag.Leid.V. 8.12 : in pl., magical powers, Hld. 4.7 . force or meaning of a word, Lys. 10.7 , Pl. Cra. 394b , Diog.Oen. 12 , Phld. Sign. 31 , etc. phonetic value of sounds or letters, Plb. 10.47.8 , D.H. Comp. 12 , Luc. Jud.Voc. 5 , etc. worth or value of money, Th. 6.46 , 2.97 , Plu. Lyc. 9 , Sol. 15 . capability of existing or acting, potentiality, opp. actuality (ἐνέργεια), Arist. Metaph. 1047b31 , 1051a5 , etc.: hence δυνάμει as Adv., virtually, ὕστερον ὂν τῇ τάξει, πρότερον τῇ δυνάμει . . ἐστί D. 3.15 ; opp. ἐνεργείᾳ, Arist. APo. 86a28 , al.; opp. ἐντελεχείᾳ, Id. Ph. 193b8 , al. Math., power, κατὰ μεταφορὰν ἡ ἐν γεωμετρίᾳ λέγεται δ. Id. Metaph. 1019b33 ; usu. second power, square, κατὰ δύναμιν in square, Pl. Ti. 54b , cf. Theol.Ar. 11 , etc.: chiefly in dat., [εὐθεῖα] δυνάμει ἴση a line the square on which is equal to an area, ἡ BA ἐλάσσων ἐστὶν ἢ διπλασίων δυνάμει τῆς AK the square on BA is less than double of the square on AK, Archim. Sph.Cyl. 2.9 : εὐθεῖαι δ. σύμμετροι commensurable in square, Euc. 10 Def. 2 ; ἡ δυνάμει δεκάς the series 12 + 22 . . . + 102 , Theol.Ar. 64 . square number, Pl. Ti. 32a . square of an unknown quantity ( x2 ), Dioph. Def. 2 , al. square root of a number which is not a perfect square, surd, opp. μῆκος, Pl. Tht. 147d . product of two numbers, ἡ ἀμφοῖν (sc. τριάδος καὶ δυάδος) δ. ἑξάς Ph. 1.3 , cf. Iamb. in Nic. p.108 P.; δυνάμει in product, Hero Metr. 1.15 , Theol.Ar. 33 . concrete, powers, esp. of divine beings, αἱ δ. τῶν οὐρανῶν LXX Is. 34.4 , cf. 1 Ep.Pet. 3.22 , al., Ph. 1.587 , Corp.Herm. 1.26 , Porph. Abst. 2.34 : sg., Act.Ap. 8.10 , PMag.Par. 1.1275 ; πολυώνυμος δ., of God, Secund. Sent. 3 . manifestation of divine power, miracle, Ev.Matt. 11.21 , al., Buresch Aus Lydien 113 , etc.

term_table.english_sentence_A: The matters of experience, then, are thus easy, both concerning the power of roses and concerning all the other drugs.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἔξεστι γὰρ δήπου καὶ στεφανώσασθαι ῥόδοις καὶ τρίψαντί ποτε καταπλάσαι τὸ στόμα τῆς κοιλίας ἀνθρώπου καυσουμένου καὶ [559] ἀποθλίψαντι τὸν χυλὸν αὐτῶν ἐκροφῆσαι καὶ μίξαντι μεθ’ ὕδατος, ἢ ἐλαίου, τῶν τοῦ σώματός τι μορίων ἀνατρῖψαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For it is surely possible both to crown oneself with roses, and, having at some time pounded them, to apply them as a plaster to the mouth of the stomach of a person burning with fever, and [559] having pressed out their juice, to gulp it down, and having mixed it with water or with oil, to rub some one of the parts of the body with it.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For it is surely possible both to crown oneself with roses, and at some time, having pounded them, to apply them as a poultice to the mouth of the stomach of a person suffering from burning fever, and, [559] having squeezed out their juice, to sip it down, and, having mixed it with water or oil, to rub some one of the parts of the body with it.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὀπο-βάλσαμον, τό, the juice of the balsam-tree, balsam of Mecca, Thphr. HP 4.4.14 , CP 6.18.2 , J. AJ 14.4.1 , Gal. 12.554 , Edict.Diocl.in BCH 22.403 (written ὀποπ-, as also in PMed.Strassb. p.4 K., Gloss.); the tree itself, Balsamodendron Opobalsamum, J. AJ 8.6.6 , al.
term_table.greek_sentence: καίτοι τί λέγω τούτοις, ὅπου γε ὀποβαλσάμῳ μιγνύντες ἔνιοι ῥόδων χυλὸν ἐν τοῖς ὑπὸ κύνα καύμασιν ἀνατρίβονται τὰ σώματα χάριν ἐμψύξεως, αὐτῇ τῇ πείρᾳ μεμαθηκότες ὡς ἱκανῶς ἀναψύχουσιν;
term_table.english_sentence_A: And yet why do I say this to these people, when in fact some people, mixing rose juice with opobalsam, rub their bodies with it in the burning heats under the Dog-star for the sake of cooling, having learned by experience itself that they cool sufficiently?
term_table.english_sentence_B: And yet why do I speak of these things, when some people, mixing juice of roses with balsam sap, rub down their bodies during the heats under the Dog-star for the sake of cooling, having learned by experience itself that they cool sufficiently?

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ῥόδινος, η, ον, (ῥόδον) made of or from roses, στέφανος Anacr. 83 ; ἄλειφα Hippon. 58 ; μύρον Cephisod. 3 ; μύρον is understood in Thphr. term_table.greek_sentence: ἀλλ’ ὑπὸ περιττῆς σοφίας Ἡρόδοτος ὁ ἰατρὸς οὐδὲ τὸ ξὺν ὄξει ῥόδινον, ὃ δὴ καλοῦσιν ἰδίως ὀξυρόδινον, ὁμολογεῖ ψύχειν ἡμᾶς· εἶτ’ ἀναμνησθεὶς τό γε τοσοῦτον, ὡς ἐν ταῖς ἀρχαῖς τῶν φρενιτικῶν νοσημάτων αὐτὸς αὐτῷ χρῆται καὶ συνεὶς τῆς ἐναντιολογίας, ὡμολόγηται γὰρ ὑπὸ πάντων σχεδὸν τῶν ἰατρῶν ἄχρι καὶ τῶν ἀμφὶ τὸν ἀναισθητότατον Θεσσαλὸν, ὡς ἀποκρούεσθαι χρὴ καὶ ψύχειν ἐν ἀρχῇ μᾶλλον ἢ θερμαίνειν καὶ χαλᾷν, οὐ ψύχειν φησὶν, ἀλλὰ στύφειν αὐτό.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But out of excessive wisdom Herodotus the physician does not even admit that rose oil with vinegar, which they specifically call oxyrhodinon, cools us; then, having recalled at least this much, that he himself uses it in the beginnings of phrenitic diseases, and being aware of the contradiction—for it is agreed by almost all physicians, even down to the followers of the most senseless Thessalus, that at the beginning one must repel and cool rather than warm and relax—he says that it does not cool but is astringent.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But out of excessive cleverness Herodotus the physician does not even admit that rose oil with vinegar, which they call specifically oxyrhodinon, cools us. Then, remembering at least this much, that he himself uses it at the beginnings of phrenitic diseases, and perceiving the contradiction (for it is agreed by nearly all physicians, down even to the followers of the most insensate Thessalus, that at the beginning one must repel and cool rather than heat and relax), he says that it does not cool but is astringent.

term_table.greek_sentence: οὕτω γάρ σοι κρίνοντι τὸ μὲν ἔλαιον οὔτε θερμὸν οὔτε ψυχρὸν ὡς πρὸς ἄνθρωπον εὔκρατον ἑρεθήσεται, τὸ δὲ ῥόδινον ἤδη μέν πω ψυχρότερον, οὐ μὴν ἰσχυρῶς γε ψυχρὸν, ἀλλ’ ὡς ὀνομάζειν εἴωθα τῆς πρώτης τῶν ψυχόντων ἀποστάσεώς τε καὶ τάξεως.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For if you judge in this way, olive oil will be found neither hot nor cold relative to a well-tempered human being, while rose oil will be found already somewhat colder, yet certainly not strongly cold, but, as I am accustomed to name it, of the first distance and order of the cooling things.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For if you judge in this way, oil will be said to be neither hot nor cold in relation to a well-tempered human being, while rose oil is already somewhat colder, yet not strongly cold, but, as I am accustomed to name it, of the first distance and order of cooling things.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: φάρμακον [v. sub fin.], τό, drug, whether healing or noxious: in Hom. the sense is freq. determined by an epith., φάρμακα, πολλὰ μὲν ἐσθλὰ . . , πολλὰ δὲ λυγρά Od. 4.230 ; τόδε φ. ἐσθλόν 10.287 , cf. 292 ; φ. ἤπια, ὀδυνήφατα (v. infr. 2 ); κακὰ φ. ib. 213 ; φ. λυγρά ib. 236 ; φ. οὐλόμενον ib. 394 ; ἀνδροφόνον 1.261 ; θυμοφθόρα φ. 2.329 ; so, after Hom. , προσανέα φ. term_table.greek_sentence: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὕδωρ, εἰ τύχοι, τὸ μὲν ἀκριβῶς ἐστιν εὔκρατον, τὸ δ’ ἤτοι θερμότερον ἢ ψυχρότερον, οὐ μὴν ἤδη γέ πως θερμὸν ἢ ψυ χρὸν ἀπολελυμένως εἰπεῖν, οὕτω κᾀν τοῖς φαρμάκοις ἔλαιον μὲν ἐκ τῆς μέσης ὑπάρχει κράσεως, ὁ δὲ τῶν ῥόδων χυλὸς ἐκ τῆς ψυχροτέρας μὲν, ἀλλ’ οὐ πολλῷ τινι κατὰ τὴν χλιαρὰν, ὡς εἴρηταί μοι καὶ πρόσθεν, ὑπάρχων θερμασίαν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For just as water, for instance, is in one case precisely well-tempered, in another either warmer or colder, yet not thereby in any way hot or cold, to speak absolutely, so too among drugs olive oil belongs to the middle mixture, whereas the juice of roses belongs to the colder one, though not by any great amount, being, as I have also said before, at lukewarm warmth.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For just as with water, say, one is exactly well-tempered while another is either warmer or colder, yet not such that one could already call it hot or cold absolutely, so too among drugs oil is of the middle mixture, whereas the juice of roses is of the colder, though not by any great amount, being, as I have also said before, of lukewarm warmth.

term_table.english_sentence_A: For just as water, for instance, is in one case precisely well-tempered, in another either warmer or colder, yet not thereby in any way hot or cold, to speak absolutely, so too among drugs olive oil belongs to the middle mixture, whereas the juice of roses belongs to the colder one, though not by any great amount, being, as I have also said before, at lukewarm warmth.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: χαμαί-μηλον, τό, earth-apple, camomile, Orph. A. 921 . = ἀνθεμὶς λευκή , Dsc. 3.137 , Plin. HN 22.53 . = παρθένιον , Ps.- Dsc. 3.138 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἔστι δὲ καὶ τὸ χαμαίμηλον, ὅσον μὲν ἐπὶ λεπτομερείᾳ, ῥόδῳ παραπλήσιον, ὅσον δ’ ἐπὶ θερμότητι, τῆς ἐλαίου μᾶλλον δυνάμεως, οἰκείας τε τῷ ζώῳ καὶ συμμέτρου, διὸ καὶ κόπου ἀρωγόν ἐστιν εἴπερ τι καὶ ἄλλο καὶ ἀλγημάτων πραϋντικὸν, ἀνίησί τε καὶ χαλᾷ τὰ τεταμένα καὶ μαλάττει τὰ μετρίως σκληρὰ καὶ ἀραιοῖ τὰ πεπυκνωμένα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Chamomile too is, as regards fineness of parts, similar to the rose, but as regards heat it is rather of the power of olive oil, which is proper to the animal and well-proportioned; wherefore it is also a help against fatigue, if anything is, and soothing of pains, and it relaxes and slackens what is tense, softens what is moderately hard, and rarefies what has been condensed.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For this reason it is a help against fatigue if anything else is, and soothing of pains; it relaxes and loosens what is tensed, softens what is moderately hard, and rarefies what has been condensed.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ γὰρ καὶ τούτων ἴαμα γενναιότατόν ἐστιν τὸ χαμαίμηλον, ὅταν ἤδη πεττομένοις προσφέρηται, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὑποχονδρίοις εὐμενὲς εἴπερ τι ἄλλο.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For chamomile is a most noble remedy of these too, whenever it is applied to them once they are already being concocted, and on this account it is also kindly to the hypochondria if anything is.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For chamomile is a most excellent (γενναιότατον) remedy for these too, when it is administered to them when they are already being concocted; and for this reason it is also kindly to the hypochondria, if anything else is. term_table.english_sentence_A: And linseed too, at any rate, the ancient account says is of this sort.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And indeed that too really is kindly to the internal organs in the region of the hypochondria, but less so than chamomile.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: χαμαί-μηλον, τό, earth-apple, camomile, Orph. A. 921 . = ἀνθεμὶς λευκή , Dsc. 3.137 , Plin. HN 22.53 . = παρθένιον , Ps.- Dsc. 3.138 .
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ γάρ ἐστιν ὄντως κᾀκεῖνο τοῖς καθ’ ὑποχόνδρια σπλάγχνοις εὐμενὲς, ἀλλ’ ἧττον χαμαιμήλου.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And indeed that too is really kindly to the viscera in the hypochondria, but less so than chamomile.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For it is both less hot, as has been said, and in addition to this it is coarse-particled. The rose, however, does not come near them for these purposes.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ γὰρ καὶ θερμὸν ἧττόν ἐστιν, ὡς εἴρηται, καὶ πρὸς τούτῳ καὶ παχυμερὲς ὑπάρχει, οὐ μὴν τό γε ῥόδον ἐγγὺς αὐτοῖς εἰς ταῦτα, καίτοι γ’ ὅσον ἐπί τε τὸ χλιαρὸν τῆς θερμότητος καὶ τῷ λεπτομερεῖ, χρήσιμον ἂν ἦν ἱκανῶς καὶ τοῦτο ταῖς καθ’ ὑποχόνδρια φλεγμοναῖς, ἀλλ’ ἡ συνοῦσα στύψις αὐτῷ πολλαχῆ παραβλάπτει καὶ μάλιστ’ ἐν οἷς εὐδόκιμόν ἐστι χαμαίμηλον, ἢ τὰ πεπυκνωμένα τῶν σωμάτων ἀραιοῦν, ἢ τὰ κατεσκληρυμμένα μαλάττον, ἢ τὰ τεταμένα χαλῶν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For it is both less hot, as has been said, and in addition to this it is coarse-particled; the rose, however, does not come close to them in these respects, although, as far as concerns the lukewarmness of its heat and its fine-particled quality, this too would have been sufficiently useful for inflammations in the hypochondria; but the astringency that accompanies it does harm in many ways, and especially in those cases in which chamomile is of good repute, either rarefying the condensed parts of bodies, or softening the hardened, or relaxing the tense.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And yet, as far as the lukewarm character of its heat and its fine-particled nature are concerned, it too would be quite useful for inflammations in the region of the hypochondria; but the astringency present in it does harm in many ways. It does so especially in those things in which chamomile is highly esteemed: either rarefying the condensed parts of bodies, or softening those that have been hardened, or relaxing those that are stretched tight.

term_table.greek_sentence: Τὰ γάρ τοι τῆς μέσης κράσεως καὶ τὰ ἐφ’ ἑκάτερα βραχὺ παραλλάττοντα φάρμακα καὶ θερμαίνειν ἂν δόξειέ ποτε καὶ ψύχειν αὖθις, ἐνίοτε δὲ μήτε θερμαίνειν μήτε ψύχειν, ἀλλ’ οἷα παρέλαβε τὰ σώματα διαφυλάττειν, καὶ τοῦτο εὐλόγως πέπονθεν, εἴ γε τὸ χλιαρὸν ὕδωρ καὶ τὸ οὖρον ἐν μὲν τοῖς βαλανείοις ψυχρὰ, τοῖς δ’ ἐψυγμένοις θερμὰ φαίνεται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For indeed the drugs of the middle mixture, and those which deviate slightly toward either side, may seem at one time to warm and at another in turn to cool, and sometimes neither to warm nor to cool but to preserve the bodies in the condition in which they received them; and this happens to them with good reason, if indeed lukewarm water and urine appear cold in the baths, but warm to those who have been chilled.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For drugs of the middle mixture, and those that deviate slightly to either side, might seem at one time to warm and at another, again, to cool, and sometimes neither to warm nor to cool but to preserve the bodies in the condition in which they received them. And this happens to them with good reason, since lukewarm water and urine appear cold in the baths, but warm to those who have been chilled.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἴπερ οὖν παρὰ τό πως ἔχειν τὰ διατιθέμενα καὶ τὸ διατιθὲν οὐχ ὁμοίως ἐνεργεῖν φαίνεται, δῆλον ὡς οὔτε τὸ ῥόδον οὔτε τοὔλαιον οὔτε τὸ χαμαίμηλον ﻿ [565] οὔτε τὸ λινόσπερμον, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ τὸ ἄνηθον οὔτε τὸ τήλινον ἄλευρον, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ τὸ πύρινον οὐδ’ ἄλλα μυρία, τά τε ἀκριβῶς μέσα ταῖς κράσεσιν, τά τε βραχὺ παραλλάττοντα, τὴν αὐτὴν ἐνέργειαν ἐπιδείξεται διὰ παντός.
term_table.english_sentence_A: If, then, in accordance with the condition of the things being affected, the agent too appears not to act in the same way, it is clear that neither the rose nor the oil nor chamomile [565] nor linseed, nor indeed dill nor fenugreek flour, nor wheat flour either, nor countless others—both those that are exactly intermediate in their mixtures and those that depart slightly from it—will display the same activity throughout.
term_table.english_sentence_B: If, then, it is evident that the agent which affects, too, does not act in the same way according to the condition of the things being affected, it is clear that neither the rose nor olive oil nor chamomile [565] nor linseed, nor yet dill nor fenugreek meal, nor yet wheaten meal nor countless others, both those exactly intermediate in their mixtures and those that deviate slightly, will display the same activity in every case.

term_table.greek_sentence: αὐτίκα γέ τοι τὸ ῥόδινον ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ τὴν κρᾶσιν κεκραμένον ἐλαίου τε καὶ τοῦ τῶν ῥόδων χυλοῦ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: To take an immediate example, rose oil is, in its mixture, mixed intermediately between oil and the juice of roses; for it is less hot than the one and more so than the other.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Rose oil, for instance, is mixed with a mixture intermediate between olive oil and the juice of roses: for it is less hot than the former and hotter than the latter.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἀναψύχει μὲν γὰρ τοὺς ἐγκεκαυμένους τῷ χλιαρῷ δηλονότι τῆς θερμότητος, ὀλίγον δέ τι καὶ τοὺς κατεψυγμένους θερμαίνει.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For it cools those who are burning, obviously by the lukewarmness of its heat, while it also warms a little those who have been chilled, since this too is a work of lukewarm warmth, just as baths too both warm those who are shivering and cool those who are burning.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It cools again those who are overheated, evidently by the lukewarm character of its heat, and it also warms to some small degree those who are chilled.

term_table.greek_sentence: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο κᾀν τοῖς ψύχειν ἢ θερμαίνειν πεφυκόσι φαρμάκοις, ἐὰν ἀναμίξῃς τὸ ῥόδινον, οὐδὲν ἐργάσῃ μέγα κακὸν, ὥσπερ δ’ ἀξιόλογον ἀγαθὸν οὐδέν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And for this reason, even if you mix rose oil into drugs whose nature it is to cool or to heat, you will do no great harm, just as you will do no notable good either.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And for this reason, if you mix rose oil into drugs that are naturally disposed to cool or to warm, you will do no great harm, just as you will do no noteworthy good either.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀμετρ-ία, ἡ, excess, disproportion, opp. συμμετρία, Pl. Ti. 87d , cf. R. 486d , Heraclit. All. 8 , Alex.Aphr. Pr. 1.112 , etc. want of moderation, Arist. VV 1251b15 . infinity, countless number, κακῶν Pl. Ax. 367a (in pl.).
term_table.greek_sentence: δεῖται γὰρ τὸ [566] θεραπευόμενον ἅπαν, ὡς ἂν ἐξ ἀμετρίας τινὸς εἰς συμμετρίαν ἀγόμενον, οὐκ αὐτοῦ τοῦ συμμέτρου τὴν κρᾶσιν, ἀλλὰ τῆς ἐναντίας ἀμετρίας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For everything that is being treated, [566] inasmuch as it is being brought from some excess into due proportion, needs not what is itself moderate in its mixture, but the opposite excess.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For everything that is [566] being treated, inasmuch as it is being brought from some immoderation into due proportion, needs not the mixture of the moderate itself but that of the opposite immoderation.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ γοῦν τὸ ψυχρὸν ὕδωρ βουληθείης εὔκρατον ποιῆσαι, τὸ μὲν εὔκρατον ἤδη μιγνύειν οὐ χρὴ χλιαρὸν γὰρ οὕτως ἔσται τὸ μικτὸν ἐξ ἀμφοῖν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: At any rate, if you should wish to make cold water well-tempered, you must not mix in what is already well-tempered; for in that way the mixture of both will be lukewarm.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So if you should wish to make cold water well-tempered, you must not mix in water that is already well-tempered, for in that way the mixture made from both will be lukewarm.

Eup. 244 ; ψ. καὶ ἀηδὴς [Μοῦσα] Pl. Lg. 802d ; ἕωλα καὶ ψ. D. 21.112 ; πρᾶγμα . . φρέατος . . ψυχρότερον Ἀραρότος Alex. 179 , cf. Arist. Rh. 1405b34 , Demetr. Eloc. 114 , etc.: hence jokes in Ar. Th. 170 ; σκώψαντι ψ. ἐπιγελάσαι to laugh at a feeble joke, Thphr. Char. 2.4 ; τοὺς γοῦν ψυχροὺς ψ. λέγουσι διαλέγεσθαι Pl. Euthd. 284e . silly, γραϊδίοις ψυχροῖς ὁμιλοῦντες Jul. Ep. 89b . term_table.greek_sentence: ἀλλ’ εἴτε πολλῷ ψυχρότερόν ἐστι τὸ τῆς θεραπείας δεόμενον, ἀνάγκη καὶ τὸ θεραπεῦσον αὐτὸ πολλῷ θερμότερον ὑπάρχειν, εἴτ’ ὀλίγῳ ψυχρότερον, ὀλίγῳ χρὴ καὶ τὸ θεραπεῦον εἶναι θερμότερον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But if what needs treatment is much colder, it is necessary that what is to treat it also be much hotter; and if it is slightly colder, what treats it must also be slightly hotter.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But if what needs treatment is much colder, then what is to treat it must necessarily also be much hotter; and if it is a little colder, then what treats it must also be a little hotter.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὅμοιος or (as in Hom. , Ion. , and old Att. ) ὁμοῖος, α, ον (cf. ἐρῆμος, ἑτοῖμος) : later Ep. also ὁμοίιος (B, q.v.) ; Aeol. ὔμοιος Theoc. 29.20 (Adv. -ως IG 12(2).69a6 ) ; Arc. ὑμοῖος Schwyzer 665 A 15 (Orchom., iv B.C.) : (ὁμός) :—like, resembling, ὡς αἰεὶ τὸν ὁ. ἄγει θεὸς ὡς τὸν ὁ. 'birds of a feather flock together', Od. 17.218 ; ὁ ὅ. τῷ ὁ. Pl. Grg. 510b ; ὁ ὅ. ὡς τὸν ὅ. Arist. EN 1155a34 ; τὸ ὅ. τῷ ὁ. φίλον ib. 1165b17 , v. infr. 6 ; ὡς ἐπὶ τῶν ὁ. as in similar cases (of persons), BGU 79.18 (ii A.D.), etc. : Comp. -ότερος more like, Pl. Phd. 79b : Sup. -ότατος most like, Hdt. 2.92 , S. Ant. 833 (lyr.), etc. the same, ἄμφω γὰρ πέπρωται ὁμοίην γαῖαν ἐρεῦσαι Il. 18.329 ; χρὼς οὐκέθ' ὁ. Od. 16.182 ; hence (sc. ἑαυτῷ), always the same, unchanging, αἰεὶ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ὁμοῖοι Hes. Op. 114 ; ὅ. τὴν γνώμην the same as ever, Antipho 5.76 ; γνῶμαι πρὸς τοὺς αὐτοὺς κινδύνους ὁμοῖαι Th. 2.89 ; ἀεὶ ὅ. εἶ, ὦ Ἀπολλόδωρε Pl. Smp. 173d ; ἓν καὶ ὅ. one and the same, Id. Phdr. 271a . equal in force, a match for one, Il. 23.632 , Hdt. 9.96 . of things, suiting, according with, πολλά τε καὶ ὅ. ἑαυταῖς Id. R. 549e ; ὅ. τῇ φύσει Ar. Th. 167 . ὁμοῖον ἡμῖν ἔσται it will be all the same, all one to us, Hdt. 8.80 ; σὺ δ' αἰνεῖν εἴτε με ψέγειν θέλεις, ὁμοῖον A. Ag. 1404 , cf. 1239 , E. Supp. 1069 ; ἐν τῷ ὁ. καθειστήκει Th. 2.49 . τὸ ὅ. ἀνταποδιδόναι give 'tit for tat', Hdt. 1.18 ; so τὴν ὁμοίην (sc. δίκην, χάριν) ἀποδιδόναι τινί Id. 4.119 , 6.21 , 62 ; τὴν ὁ. φέρεσθαι παρά τινος to have a like return made one, ibid. ; ἐπ' ἴσῃ καὶ ὁμοίᾳ, v. ἴσος 11.2 . ἐν ὁμοίῳ ποιεῖσθαί τι hold a thing in like esteem, Id. 7.138 , 8.109 . ἐκ τοῦ ὁ. in like fashion, likewise, Th. 6.78 , 87 ; ἐκ τῶν ὁ. ceteris paribus, Pl. Phdr. 243d ; on equal terms, in fair fight, A. Ag. 1423 ; so ἐν τῷ ὁ. στρατεύεσθαι καὶ ὅτε . . as when . . , Th. 6.21 , etc. of the same rank or station, Hdt. 1.134 ; γαμεῖν ἐκ τῶν ὁ. Cleobul. ap. Stob. 3.1.172 , POxy. 124.2 (iii A.D.), PSI 2.120.33 (iv A.D.?) : hence οἱ ὅμοιοι, in aristocratic states, peers, all citizens who had equal right to hold state-offices, esp. at Sparta, X. HG 3.3.5 , Lac. 13.1 , 7 , Arist. Pol. 1306b30 ; Περσέων ὁμοίους τοῖσι πρώτοισι δυώδεκα Hdt. 3.35 . Geom., of figures, similar, Euc. 6 Def. 1 , 3 Def. 11 , al. ; of angles, similar, i.e. equal, Arist. Cael. 296b20 , 297b19 , 311b34 , cf. Thalesap. Procl. in Euc. 1p.251F. of Numbers, square, the product of two equal factors, Plot. 6.2.21 ; cf. ἀνόμοιος 2 . Construction : abs., freq. in Hom. , etc. (v. supr.). c. dat. of the person or thing which another resembles : so always in Hom. , Hes. , and usu. in Hdt. and Att. (v. supr.) : but sts. c. gen., τοῖσι τούτων ὁμοίοις χύμασι v.l. in Hp. Art. 12 (DielsZtschr.f.vergl. Sprachf. 47.200 ), v. l. in Hdt. 3.37 and Pl. R. 472d ; τουτέων οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλο ἔθνος ὁμοίας τὰς κεφαλὰς ἔχον οὐδέν (ellipt. as in b. infr.) Hp. Aër. 14 ; ὁ λεκτικὸς πῇ μὲν ὅμοιος Ἡροδότου, πῇ δὲ ἐνδεέστερος D.H. Pomp. 4 ; ὁμοία ἀνδριάντος Dion.Byz. 53 ; ὅμοιον ἱέρακος Cyran. 22 , cf. 12 . ellipt. phrases, κόμαι Χαρίτεσσιν ὁμοῖαι, for κόμαι ταῖς τῶν Χαρίτων ὁμοῖαι, Il. 17.51 ; οὔ τις ὁμοῖα νοήματα Πηνελοπείῃ ᾔδη, for τοῖς τῆς Πηνελοπείης, Od. 2.121 : also in Prose, ἅρματα ὅ. ἐκείνῳ, for τοῖς ἐκείνου, X. Cyr. 6.1.50 ; ὁμοίαν ταῖς δούλαις ἐσθῆτα, for τῇ τῶν δουλῶν, ib. 5.1.4 ; cf. ἴσος 1.1 , συγγενής 111.2 . c. acc. of that in which a person or thing resembles another, ἀθανάτῃσι φυὴν καὶ εἶδος ὁμοίη Od. 6.16 , cf. 3.468 , Il. 5.778 ; ὀργὴν ὁ. τῷ κάκιστ' αὐδωμένῳ A. Th. 678 , cf. S. Aj. 1153 , etc. : also with Preps., ὁμοῖοι ἐν πολέμῳ Il. 12.270 ; ἐς φύσιν οὐδὲν ὁ. Batr. 32 ; ὅ. τινὶ πρός τι X. Cyn. 5.29 ; but οὐδὲν ὁμοῖον ἦν μοι πρὸς τοῦτον I had nothing in common with him, Is. 8.26 . c. inf., θείειν ἀνέμοισιν ὁμοῖοι like the winds in running, Il. 10.437 ; τῷ οὔ πώ τις ὁμοῖος κοσμῆσαι ἵππους like him to marshal or in marshalling horses, 2.553 , cf. 14.521 ; ὅμοιοι ἦσαν θαυμάζειν (s. v.l., θαυμάζοντες codd. dett.) X. An. 3.5.13 . ὅμοιον εἰπεῖν approximately, Men. Epit. 548 . folld. by a Relat., ὁμοίη, οἵην με τὸ πρῶτον ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖσι νόησας like as when thou saw'st me first, h.Ven. 178 ; ὅμοιον . . , οἷόνπερ τὸ τῶν ποταμῶν X. HG 4.2.11 , cf. Hier. 7.5 , Cyr. 6.1.37 : folld. by ὅσπερ, Id. An. 5.4.34 ; by ὥσπερ, ὁ. ἀτμὸς ὥσπερ ἐκ τάφου πρέπει A. Ag. 1311 , cf. X. Smp. 4.37 ; by ὥστε, E. Or. 697 ; v. infr. c. folld. by καί (='as'), γνώμῃσι ἐχρέωντο ὁμοίῃσι καὶ σύ Hdt. 7.50 , cf. Th. 1.120 , Pl. Cri. 48b , Tht. 154a ; οὐδέν τι γενόμενος ἐς Ἀχαιοὺς ὅμοιος [ἢ] καὶ Καλλίστρατος . . Paus. 7.16.4 ; v. καί A. 111 . Adv., freq. in the neut. sg. and pl. ὅμοιον, ὅμοια (older ὁμοῖον, ὁμοῖα) in like manner with, c. dat., ὁμοῖα τοῖσι μάλιστα 'second to none', Hdt. 3.8 , cf. Th. 7.29 ; ὁμοῖα τοῖσι πλουσιωτάτοισι Hdt. 3.57 ; ὅμοιον μουσίσδει . . ταῖσιν ἀηδονίσι Theoc. 8.37 : folld. by a relat. Partic., ὁμοῖον ὥστε . . even as, S. Ant. 587 (lyr.) ; ὁ. ὡς εἰ . . Pl. Lg. 628d ; ὁμοῖα καὶ βοῦς ἐργάτης S. Fr. 563 . alike, ὅμοια χέρσον καὶ θάλασσαν ἐκπερῶν A. Eu. 240 . regul. Adv. ὁμοίως in like manner with, c. dat., Hdt. 1.32 , al. ; τοῖς μάλισθ' ὁ. D. Ep. 2.24 : folld. by a relat. Partic., ὁ. ὡς εἰ . . Hdt. 1.155 ; ὁ. ὥσπερ . . X. Cyr. 1.4.6 ; ὁ. καὶ . . Hdt. 7.86 , 8.60 .β' : abs., ὁ. δέ and in like manner, PEleph. 15.1 (iii B. C.), etc. alike, equally, Pi. P. 9.78 , Hdt. 7.100 ; Δαναοῖσι Τρωσί θ' ὁ. A. Ag. 67 (anap.) ; λέγειν . . σιγᾶν θ' ὁ. Id. Eu. 278 , etc. ; τῷ νῷ θ' ὁ. κἀπὸ τῆς γλώσσης S. OC 936 ; ὁ. μὲν . . , ὁ. δὲ . . Pl. Prt. 319d ; ὁ. ἀμφοῖν ἀκροάσασθαι D. 18.2 ; ὁ. ἔχειν to be uniform, Arist. Ph. 261b25 : prov., οὐδ' ὅκου χώρης οἱ μῦς ὁ. τὸν σίδηρον τρώγουσιν like any other food, Herod. 3.76 (but perh. all alike, cf. Ar. Eq. 1296 cod. R, Th. 5.15 (s. v.l.), Plu. 2.763c ) : Comp. -ότερον AP 11.233 ( Lucill. ) : Sup. -ότατα Ar. Fr. 281 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τὸ γὰρ ἐπὶ τὰ αὐτὰ παραπλησίως [567] ἀφεστηκὸς, ὅμοιον τῇ κράσει τῷ θεραπευομένῳ καθεστηκὸς, οὐδεμίαν ἀλλοίωσιν ἐπιφέρειν ἱκανὸν, ὥστε οὔτε βλάψει τι παθὸν οὔτ’ ὠφελήσει.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For that which stands at a similar distance in the same direction, being similar in mixture to what is being treated, is capable of bringing about no alteration, so that it will neither harm anything affected nor benefit it.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For what is, to a comparable degree, [567] removed in the same direction, being similar in mixture to what is being treated, is capable of bringing about no alteration, so that it will neither harm anything that has been affected (τι παθὸν) nor benefit it.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σύμμετρ-ος, ον, (μέτρον) commensurate with, of like measure or size with, σύμμετρος σῷ ποδί (sc. ἡ βάσις) E. El. 533 ; χαμεύνῃ Id. Fr. 676 ; βόστρυχον . . σύμμετρον τῷ σῷ κάρᾳ exactly like it, A. Ch. 230 : esp. of Time, commensurate with, keeping even with, δαλὸν ἥλικα ξύμμετρόν τε διαὶ βίου ib. 610 (lyr.); τῷδε τἀνδρὶ ς. being of like age with him, S. OT 1113 ; ποίᾳ ξύμμετρος προὔβην τύχῃ; coincident with what chance have I come? i.e. in the very nick of time, Id. Ant. 387 , cf. E. Alc. 26 (infr. 111 ). in Mathematics, having a common measure, σύμμετροι αἱ τῷ αὐτῷ μέτρῳ μετρούμεναι (sc. γραμμαί) Arist. LI 968b6 ; freq. denied of the relation between the diagonal of a square and its side, Id. APo. 71b27 , APr. 41a26 , Ph. 221b25 , Rh. 1392a18 ; [τὸ νόμισμα] πάντα ποιεῖ σύμμετρα commensurable, Id. EN 1133b22 ; μήκει οὐ σύμμετροι τῇ ποδιαίᾳ not lineally commensurate with the one-foot side, Pl. Tht. 147d , cf. 148b : Comp. , of musical intervals, ταῖς αἰσθήσεσιν εὐληπτότερα τὰ -ότερα Ptol. Harm. 1.10 . in accord with the metre, S. Eleg. 1 ; σύμμετροι ἐπεκτύπεον ποδῶν χορείαις in time, Tim. Pers. 213 . in measure with, proportionable, exactly suitable, λόγοι ἀνδράσι ς. Isoc. 4.83 , cf. 5.110 , 12.135 ; γῆ θηρίοις μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις ς. Str. 15.1.26 ; ς. πρός τι Pl. Lg. 625d , Metrod. Fr. 1 , etc.; c. dat., Pl. Men. 76d , Ti. 67c , Epicur. Fr. 81 ( Comp. ). abs., in right measure, in due proportion, symmetrical, opp. ὑπερβάλλων and ἐλλείπων, Arist. EN 1104a18 , al.; τὸ ς. καὶ καλόν Pl. Phlb. 66b ; τῶν φύσει ξηροτέρων . . ὡς πρὸς τὸν ς. παραβάλλειν Gal. 6.360 , cf. 27 , al. generally, fitting, meet, due, ξύμμετρον δ' ἔπος λέγω A. Eu. 532 (lyr.); δένδρον πολυκαρπότερον τοῦ συμμέτρου Pl. Ti. 86c , cf. Phld. Rh. 1.288S. , al.; ξύμμετρος ὡς κλύειν within fit distance for hearing, S. OT 84 . moderate, πόνοι Isoc. 1.12 ; ὥστε σύμμετρον . . τὸ πνεῦμα . . ποιεῖν Antiph. 202.16 ; ς. τροφαί Sor. 1.26 , cf. 49 , al.; ς. στέγη moderate in size, X. Oec. 8.13 ; of suitable size, σκῆπτρον OGI 56.62 (Canopus, iii B.C.). Adv. -τρως in moderation, Isoc. 1.32 , etc.; in due time, ἀφίκετο E. Alc. 26 ; ς. πρὸς ἑωυτόν conveniently, Hp. Off. 3 ; ς. ἔχειν πρός τι to be in proportion to . ., X. Eq. 1.16 ; εἴς τι Arist. Mir. 834a15 ; ς. ἴσχειν λεπτότητος καὶ πάχους Pl. Ti. 85c ; τὸ μετὰ νοῦ καὶ τὸ ς. Nicom.Com. 1.36 ; = μετρίως, φέρειν IG 12(7).396.31 (Amorgos, ii B.C.), cf. Aristid.Quint. 2.5 . Comp. -ότερον more fittingly, D. 61.27 ( v.l. -ώτερον ).
term_table.greek_sentence: πάλιν δὲ εἰ μὲν τὸ πάθος εἴη μικρὸν, ὡς ἂν ἀπὸ τῆς συμμέτρου θερμασίας τῆς κατὰ φύσιν εἰς οἷον χλιαράν τινα μεταπεπτωκέναι, τὸ δὲ φάρμακον εἴη ψυχρὸν, ἀνάγκη ἐπιψυγῆναί τε καὶ βλαβῆναι τὸ πάθος ὑπὸ τοῦ ψυχροῦ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Again, if the affection should be small, such that it has shifted from the moderate warmth that is according to nature to, as it were, a kind of lukewarm warmth, while the drug is cold, the affection must necessarily be chilled and harmed by the cold.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Again, if the affection is small, so as to have shifted from the moderate natural warmth to a sort of lukewarm one, and the drug is cold, the affection must necessarily be further chilled and harmed by the cold.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: βαλαν-εῖον, τό, bath, bathing-room, Ar. Nu. 837 , 1054 , etc.; β. δημόσιον BGU 1130.9 (i B. C.): more freq. in pl., Ar. Nu. 991 , Eq. 1401 , etc. bath taken, Aristo Stoic. 1.88 , Gal. 11.46 .—Prose word for poet. λουτρά.
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ γὰρ τὸ συμμέτρως [568] κεκραμένον ὀνομάζομεν ἐνίοτε θερμὸν, ὥσπερ καὶ τὸ βαλανεῖον τὸ τοιοῦτον καὶ τὸ πόμα καὶ τὸ τούτου λειπόμενον οὐ πολλῷ, καὶ πρὸς τούτοις ἔτι τὸ θερμότερον ἅπαν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For indeed we sometimes call what is mixed in due proportion [568] "hot", as for instance a bath of that sort and a drink, and also what falls short of this by not much, and in addition to these everything hotter still.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For we sometimes call what is mixed in due proportion [568] 'hot': so, for example, we call such a bath hot, and such a drink, and also whatever falls short of it by not much, and, besides these, everything that is hotter still.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δέ γε τοῖς ὀνόμασιν ἀκριβῶς ἐχρώ μεθα, τὸ μὲν σύμμετρον οὐ θερμὸν, ἀλλ’ εὔκρατον ἂν ἐκαλοῦμεν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But if we were using the names precisely, we would call the well-proportioned not "hot" but "well-tempered"; and whatever is more immoderate than this, that which is immoderate in the direction of the hotter we would call hot to a lesser and to a greater degree, and that which is in the direction of the colder cold to a lesser and to a greater degree.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But if we used names precisely, we would call what is in due proportion not 'hot' but 'well-tempered'.

term_table.english_sentence_A: And so too, I think, in the case of drugs, if we were naming precisely, we would have called something well-tempered and intermediate, like olive oil; and if something is hotter than it, hot, like fenugreek; and if something is colder than it, cold, like the rose.
term_table.english_sentence_B: In the same way, I think, if we named drugs precisely, we would have called a drug 'well-tempered' and 'intermediate', as olive oil is. If a drug were hotter than this, we would have called it 'hot', as fenugreek is.

term_table.greek_sentence: δόξειεν ἂν οὖν ἄλογον ὑπάρχειν, εἴ τι θερμαίνειν ὁμολογοῦντες εἶτα ψυχρὸν προσαγορεύομεν, [569] ὥσπερ εἰ καὶ τὸ φρεατιαῖον ὕδωρ ἐν χειμῶνι, τὸ ταῖς κατεψυγμέναις χερσὶ χλιαρὸν φαινόμενον, ὀνομάζοι τις ψυχρόν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It would seem, then, to be unreasonable if, while agreeing that something heats, we then call it cold, [569] just as if one were also to call well-water in winter cold, the water which appears lukewarm to chilled hands.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It might seem, then, to be unreasonable if, while agreeing that something heats, we then call it cold, [569] just as if someone were to call cold the well-water in winter, which appears lukewarm to chilled hands.

term_table.english_sentence_A: For indeed not much of the distinctions belonging to it seems still to be lacking, once at least it has clearly been shown that it is nothing to wonder at that, under the action of a single drug, differing bodies are some of them heated, others cooled, and others undergo neither of these.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For not much of the distinctions belonging to it seems still to be lacking, now that it has once been clearly shown that it is nothing surprising if, by one drug, different bodies are in some cases heated, in others cooled, and in others undergo neither of these.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ῥᾴδιος (ῥαιδ- correctly in early texts, PCair.Zen. 367.20 (iii B.C.), etc., later ῥαδ-, Diog.Oen. 10 , etc.), α, ον: Ep. and Ion. ῥηΐδιος [ιδ], η, ον , as always in Hom. ; ῥῄδιος, η, ον, Thgn. 574 , 577 (v. infr. B):—Degrees of Comparison: ῥᾳδιώτερος is cited from Hyp. by Poll. 5.107 , perhaps by error for ῥᾳδιέστερος, which occurs in Hyp. Fr. 86 , Arist. Pr. 870b37 (as Adv.), Plb. 11.1.1 , 16.20.4 . Adv. -έστατα Ph. Bel. 96.33 :—but the form ῥᾴων, ῥᾷον is more common, Th. 5.36 , etc.; Ion. ῥηΐων, ῥήϊον, (v. infr. B); Ep. ῥηΐτερος Il. 18.258 , 24.243 , etc.; contr. ῥῄτερος Thgn. 1370 ; Dor. ῥᾴτερος Pi. O. 8.60 (ῥαΐτερον codd.); a form ῥᾴσσων in EM 158.15 : ῥᾳότερον, gloss on εὐπετέστερον , Erot. p.35 N.: Sup. , Att. ῥᾷστος, η, ον ; Dor. ῥάϊστος Theoc. 11.7 (Adv.); Ion. and Ep. ῥήϊστος Od. 4.565 ; contr. ῥῇστος Timo 67.2 (Adv.); Ep. ῥηΐτατος, v. infr. B. 111 fin.: (v. ῥᾶ, ῥέα, ῥεῖα):—easy, ready, and so easy to make or do, opp. χαλεπός ( Arist. Rh. 1363a23 ); ῥηΐδιόν τι ἔπος a word easy to understand and follow, Od. 11.146 , cf. h.Ap. 534 ; οἶμος ῥηϊδίη an easy road, Hes. Op. 292 ; ταχὺς γὰρ Ἅιδης ῥᾷστος ἀνδρὶ δυστυχεῖ, i. e. least painful, E. Hipp. 1047 : c. inf., τάφρος περῆσαι ῥηϊδίη easy to pass over, Il. 12.54 ; ῥηΐτεροι πολεμίζειν ἦσαν Ἀχαιοί easier to fight with, 18.258 ; ῥηΐτεροι . . Ἀχαιοῖσιν ἐναιρέμεν easier for them to slay, 24.243 ; οὐ ῥηΐδι' ἐστὶ θεῶν ἐρικυδέα δῶρα ἀνδράσι γε θνητοῖσι δαμήμεναι 20.265 ; ῥᾴονι ἂν ἐχρώμεθα τῷ Φιλίππῳ we should have found P. easier to resist, D. 1.9 . ῥᾴδιόν ἐστι it is easy, c. inf., ῥᾴδιον πόλιν σεῖσαι καὶ ἀφαυροτέροις Pi. P. 4.272 ; τοῖς γὰρ δικαίοις ἀντέχειν οὐ ῥᾴδιον S. Fr. 78 , cf. Ph. 1395 , Ar. Th. 68 , Th. 6.21 , etc.: c. acc. et inf., τύραννον εὐσεβεῖν οὐ ῥᾴδιον S. Aj. 1350 , cf. X. HG 6.2.10 ; χαλεπὸν τὸ ποιεῖν, τὸ δὲ κελεῦσαι ῥ. Philem. 27 ; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν ῥ. καὶ παντὸς εἶναι D. 1.16 ; ῥᾷον παραινεῖν ἢ παθόντα καρτερεῖν Men. Mon. 471 , etc.: ῥᾷστοί εἰσιν ἀμύνεσθαι,= ῥᾴδιόν ἐστιν αὐτοὺς ἀμύνεσθαι, Th. 4.10 ; ῥᾷσται ἐς τὸ βλάπτεσθαι (sc. αἱ νῆες) Id. 7.67 . also ῥᾴδιόν ἐστι it is a light matter, you think little of doing, παρ' ὑμῖν ῥ. ξενοκτονεῖν E. Hec. 1247 . Adv. phrase, ἐκ ῥᾳδίας easily, Plot. 4.8.1 . easy-going, adaptable, ῥ. ἤθεα E. Hipp. 1116 (lyr.); in bad sense, reckless, unscrupulous, ῥ. τὸν τρόπον Luc. Merc.Cond. 40 , cf. Alex. 4 ; ῥ. τὼ ὀφθαλμώ having a roving eye, Alciphr. 1.6 ; cf. B. 1.2 , ῥᾳδιουργός. ῥᾴων γενέσθαι to be easier, get better, of a sick person, Hp. Loc.Hom. 34 ; ὡσπερεὶ ῥ. ἔσομαι shall feel easier, better, D. 45.57 ; ταῦτ' ἢν ποιῇς, ῥ. ἔσει Theopomp.Com. 62 ; Εὐριπίδου μνήσθητι, καὶ ῥ. ἔσει Philippid. 18 . Adv. ῥᾳδίως, Aeol. βραϊδίως Theoc. 30.27 ; Ep. and Ion. ῥηϊδίως, as always in Hom. ; ῥηδίως Herod. 7.69 :—easily, readily, Il. 4.390 , al., Hes. Op. 43 , Hdt. 9.2 , etc.; in Trag. and Att. freq. ῥᾳδίως φέρειν bear lightly or with equanimity, make light of a thing, E. Andr. 744 , etc.; ῥ. προσίσταται ib. 232 ; ῥ. ἀπολείπειν to leave not unwillingly, Th. 1.2 ; ῥᾳδίως ἀπαλλάττοιντο αὐτῶν Pl. Phd. 63a . in bad sense, lightly, recklessly, ῥ. περὶ μεγάλων βουλεύεσθαι Th. 1.73 , cf. Pl. Lg. 917b ; ῥᾳδίως οὕτως in this easy, thoughtless way, Id. R. 377b , 378a ; ῥ. τολμῶσι λέγειν Lys. 19.49 . of things, ταλάντου ῥᾳδίως ἄξιος easily, fully worth a talent, Is. 8.35 ; οὐ ῥ. hardly, scarcely, Plu. Lyc. 31 , cf. 2.39b . Comp. , ῥᾷον φέρειν Th. 8.89 ; ῥ. ὀμνύναι κἀπιορκεῖν ἢ ὁτιοῦν nothing so easy, D. 54.39 ; Ion. ῥήϊον Hp. Int. 12 ; also ῥηϊτέρως, Id. Mul. 1.1 , 26 . Sup. ῥᾷστα, esp. in phrases, ῥᾷστα φέρειν S. term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν μὲν γὰρ τῷ πρός τι ῥᾷστον ἐπὶ τὰ κατὰ μέρος ἐλθόντα λέγειν ὡς τοιούτῳ μὲν σώματι προσαγόμενον ῥόδινον, ἐν ᾗ παρέλαβεν αὐτὸ κράσει φυλάττειν πέφυκε, ἑτέρῳ δέ τινι τοιῷδε θερμαίνει ﻿ [570] προσφερόμενον, ἄλλῳ δὲ ψύχει.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in the relative sense it is very easy, when one comes to the particular cases, to say that rose oil, when applied to such-and-such a body, is of a nature to preserve it in the mixture in which it found it, whereas when brought to another body of such-and-such a kind it heats [570] and another it cools.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in the relative sense it is very easy, when one comes to particulars, to say that rose oil, when applied to a body of such a kind, is naturally apt to preserve it in the mixture in which it found it, while when applied to some other body of a certain kind it heats [570], and to another it cools.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἴη δ’ ἂν ὅ τε διορισμὸς ἥ τε συνθήκη τοιήδε, ἐπειδὴ τὰ σώματα τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ ταῖς ἐξ ἀρχῆς κράσεσιν καὶ ταῖς κατὰ τὰς ἡλικίας αὐτοῖς προσγινομέναις καὶ ταῖς κατὰ τοὺς ἐθισμοὺς τοῦ βίου πάμπολυ διενήνοχε, ἀνάγκη δήπου πρὸς τῶν αὐτῶν φαρμάκων αὐτὰ διαφόρως ἀλλοιοῦσθαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: The distinction and the agreement would be as follows: since the bodies of human beings differ very greatly both in their mixtures from the beginning and in those that accrue to them according to their ages and in those according to the habits of their way of life, it is surely necessary that they be altered in different ways by the same drugs.
term_table.english_sentence_B: The distinction and the convention would be of the following kind. Since the bodies of human beings differ very greatly, both in their original mixtures and in those that accrue to them according to their ages and according to the habits of their life, it is surely necessary that they are altered differently by the same drugs.

term_table.greek_sentence: νέον γοῦν τινα φύσιν θερμὸν, ἐργάτην τῷ βίῳ, πρεσβύτιδι γυναικὶ καὶ φύσει ψυχροτέρᾳ παραβάλλων οὐκ ἂν ἐλάττονα τὴν ὑπεροχὴν εὕροις ἤ τινος τῶν θερμαινόντων ἱκανῶς φαρμάκων πρὸς τὰ ψύχοντα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: At any rate, if you compare a young man, hot by nature, a labourer by way of life, with an old woman who is also colder by nature, you would find the excess no smaller than that of one of the drugs that heat considerably in relation to those that cool.
term_table.english_sentence_B: At any rate, if you compare a young man who is hot by nature and a labourer in his way of life with an old woman who is also colder by nature, you would find the excess to be no less than that of one of the strongly heating drugs over the cooling ones.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μικρός and σμικρός, ά, όν, Dor. , Ion. μικκός (q.v.): σμικρός is corroborated by metre in Il. 17.757 , Hes. Op. 361 , and might be restored in Il. 5.801 , Od. 3.296 (μικρός codd.); it is prob. the only form in Hdt. ( μικρός Hdt. 2.74 codd.): freq. in Lyr. and prob. always in Trag. (exc. where metre requires μικρός, as S. Aj. 161 (anap., Comp. )); most freq. in Pl. ; but in Th. , also Ar. and other Com., μικρός prevails, σμικρός being found Th. 4.13 , 7.75 , 8.81 , Ar. Ach. 523 , V. 5 ; Att. Inscrr. have σμικρός IG 12.313.111 , al., μικρός ib. 369.10 , al.:—small, little, in Size, μ. ἔην δέμας Il. 5.801 ; μ. λίθος Od. 3.296 ; κίρκον, ὅ τε σμικρῇσι φόνον φέρει ὀρνίθεσσιν Il. 17.757 ; σμ. ἄστεα Hdt. 1.5 ; μεγάθεϊ σμικροί Id. 2.74 : with Dims., μ. πολίχνιον, γῄδιον, παιδάρια, Isoc. 5.145 , X. Cyr. 8.3.38 , Ages. 1.21 : as a Com. exaggeration, δικαστηρίδιον μ. πάνυ Ar. V. 803 ; σκαλαθυρμάτι' ἄττα μ. Id. Nu. 630 , etc.: c. inf., μικροὶ δ' ὁρᾶν Id. Pax 821 : as a term of reproach, Κλειγενὴς ὁ μικρός Id. Ra. 709 , cf. Pl. Prt. 323d , Arist. EN 1123b7 , Alex. 98.7 ; Ἀμύντας ὁ μ. Arist. Pol. 1311b3 ; οἱ ἐν μικρῷ μεγάλοι short but stoutly built, Philostr. Gym. 36 ; ὁ μ. δάκτυλος SIG 1172.4 (Lebena). in Quantity, σμικρὸν ἐπὶ σμικρῷ καταθεῖναι Hes. Op. 361 ; μέλιτος μικρόν Ar. V. 878 ; μ. ὄψον, ἀργυρίδιον, X. Mem. 3.14.1 , Ar. Pl. 240 , cf. Antiph. 44 . in Amount or Importance, petty, trivial, slight, σμ. πρόφασις Thgn. 323 ; ἔπος, ἔγκλημα, ῥοπή, etc., S. OC 443 , Tr. 361 , OT 961 , etc.; ἐκ σμικροῦ λόγου on some slight pretext, Id. OC 620 ; ἐν σμικρῷ λόγῳ παρῆκεν as of small account, ib. 569 ; αἰτίας μικρᾶς πέρι E. Andr. 387 , etc.; οὐδὲ μικρόν, = οὐδὲ γρῦ , D. 19.37 ; of persons, of small account, opp. μέγας, σμ. ἐν σμικροῖς, μέγας ἐν μεγάλοις Pi. P. 3.107 ; ἄριστ' ἂν καὶ μέγας ὀρθοῖθ' ὑπὸ μικροτέρων S. Aj. 161 (anap.), etc.; σμ. τίθησί με Id. OC 958 ; βίος ὁ μ., = μέτριος , E. Fr. 504 ; τίνος σμικροτάτου μεταβαλόντος, σμικρότατος τὴν δύναμιν, Pl. R. 473b ; of the mind, οὐ σμικρὸν φρονεῖ S. Aj. 1120 ; of style, mean, [ Φίλιστοσ] μικρὸς ταῖς ἐκφράσεσιν D.H. Vett.Cens. 3.2 ; of festivals, of lesser importance, Ἁλίεια τὰ μεγάλα καὶ τὰ μ. SIG 1067.14 (Cedreae). of Time, short, Pi. O. 12.12 , Ar. Pl. 126 , etc.; εἰς μ. χρόνον Pl. R. 498d ; ἐν μικρῷ (sc. χρόνῳ) shortly, X. Cyn. 5.32 , Eq. 8.7 ; πρὸ μικροῦ Poll. 1.72 ; ἔτι μικρὸν καὶ καταλιθοβολήσουσί με LXX Ex. 17.4 . of Age, young, Ostr.Bodl. i237 (ii B.C.), etc. Adverbial usages, regul. Adv. σμικρῶς, but little, Pl. Criti. 107d ; μικρῶς by a little, prob. in Archim. Stom. 1 : Sup. σμικρότατα X. Mem. 3.11.12 . σμικροῦ or μικροῦ within a little, almost, Id. Cyr. 1.4.8 , D. 18.151 , etc.; in full, μικροῦ δεῖν, v. δεῖ 11 , δέω (B) 1 ; μικροῦ τινος ἀπελείφθη τοῦ μή . . Ach.Tat. 7.13 ; but μικροῦ πρίασθαι for a little, cheap, X. Mem. 2.10.4 . σμικρῷ by a little, with Comp. , Pl. Plt. 262c , etc.; also σμικρῷ πρόσθεν a little before, Id. Lg. 719b , etc.; μικρῷ ἄνωθεν D. 44.6 . μικρόν a little, σμικρὸν ὑπολείπεσθαι, σμ. τι παρακλίνειν, X. An. 5.4.22 , Pl. Cra. 410a ; of Time, X. An. 3.1.11 , etc.; repeated, μικρὸν μικρόν Antiph. 10 : pl., of Degree, σμικρὰ γεωμετρίας ἔμπειροι Pl. R. 527a , etc.; σμίκρ' ἄττα διατρίψαντες Id. Prt. 316a ; μικρὰ διακινήσω σε περὶ τοῦ πράγματος Sosip. 1.22 ; περιπάτησον μικρὰ μετ' ἐμοῦ Men. Sam. 243 , cf. Plu. Luc. 31 . with Preps., ἐπὶ σμικρόν but a little, S. El. 414 , Antipho 6.18 , Hdt. 4.129 . κατὰ μικρόν into small pieces, X. An. 7.3.22 ; so κατὰ μικρὰ γενομένης τῆς δυνάμεως ib. 5.6.32 ; also, little by little, κατὰ μικρὸν ἀεί Ar. V. 702 , cf. Nu. 741 ; opp. συλλήβδην, Pl. R. 344a ; καὶ κατὰ σμ. or μ. ever so little, Id. Sph. 241c , Isoc. 3.10 , D. 2.22 . παρὰ μικρόν within a little, παρὰ μ. ἐλθεῖν c. inf., to be within an ace of doing, E. Heracl. 295 (anap.), cf. Isoc. 7.6 , etc.; παρὰ μ. ἦλθον ἀποθανεῖν Id. 17.42 ; τὸ παρὰ μ. ὥσπερ οὐδὲν ἀπέχειν δοκεῖ Arist. Ph. 197a30 ; but τὸ παρὰ μ. σῴζεσθαι to be only just saved, Id. Rh. 1371b11 , cf. Simp. in Ph. 344.10 ; gradual, imperceptible change, Arist. Pol. 1303a20 ; οὐδὲ παρὰ μ. ἦν κρεῖττον c. inf., Plb. 12.20.7 ; [ ἡ τύχη] παρὰ μ. εἰς ἑκάτερα ποιεῖ μεγάλας ῥοπάς Id. 15.6.8 , cf. Isoc. 4.59 ; but also παρὰ μ. ποιεῖσθαι, ἡγεῖσθαι, to think little of . . , D. 61.51 , Isoc. 5.79 . μετὰ μικρόν a little after, Ev.Matt. 26.73 . besides regul. Comp. and Sup. μικρότερος, -ότατος ( Ar. Eq. 789 , D. Prooem. 48 , etc.), there are the irreg. ἐλάσσων, ἐλάχιστος, from ἐλαχύς, and μείων, μεῖστος, also μειότερος; v. μείων. [ι by nature; ι only in late Poetry, Epigr. ap. Phleg. Fr. 36.17 J. ] (Perh. cf. Lat. mīca, mīcidus, OHG. smāhi, ONorse smár 'little'.)
term_table.greek_sentence: νέον γοῦν τινα φύσιν θερμὸν, ἐργάτην τῷ βίῳ, πρεσβύτιδι γυναικὶ καὶ φύσει ψυχροτέρᾳ παραβάλλων οὐκ ἂν ἐλάττονα τὴν ὑπεροχὴν εὕροις ἤ τινος τῶν θερμαινόντων ἱκανῶς φαρμάκων πρὸς τὰ ψύχοντα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: At any rate, if you compare a young man, hot by nature, a labourer by way of life, with an old woman who is also colder by nature, you would find the excess no smaller than that of one of the drugs that heat considerably in relation to those that cool.
term_table.english_sentence_B: At any rate, if you compare a young man who is hot by nature and a labourer in his way of life with an old woman who is also colder by nature, you would find the excess to be no less than that of one of the strongly heating drugs over the cooling ones.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὑπεροχ-ή, ἡ, ( ὑπερέχω 11 ) projection, prominence, οὐ κνῖσα κρούει πʽινὸς ὑπεροχὰς ἄκρας; Ephipp. 3 , cf. Gp. 9.10.4 ; αἱ ὑ. τῶν βουνῶν, τῶν ὀρῶν, their prominent points, Plb. 10.10.10 , Plu. 2.936a ; top of an upright beam, Ath.Mech. 17.4 ; ὑ. λιθοειδεῖς, of the mastoid processes of the skull, Ruf. Onom. 139 ; τὰς ὑ. αὐτῶν (sc. τῶν μαστῶν) Sor. 1.55 : abs., an eminence, Plb. 3.104.3 . rising of a star, ἀνατολὴν εἶναι . . ὑ. ἄστρου ὑπὲρ γῆς Chrysipp.Stoic. 2.200 ; raising, τῆς ἑαυτῶν κεφαλῆς Plot. 5.8.3 . metaph., pre-eminence, superiority, ὑπεροχῆς ἐπιθυμεῖ ἡ νεότης, ἡ δὲ νίκη ὑ. τις Arist. Rh. 1389a13 ; ἡ ἰσχὺς καὶ ἡ ὑ. Id. Pol. 1297b18 ; τὴν ὑ. ἀπονέμειν τοῖς ἀρίστοις ib. 1293b41 ; τὴν ὑ. τῆς πολιτείας λαμβάνειν superiority in the government, ib. 1296a31 ; διὰ τὴν ὑ. τοῦ πλήθους because of superiority in multitude, ib. 1293a4 ; ἡ ἐν τῷ ἐπιτηδεύματι ὑ. IG 22.3800 : pl., πρὸς τὰς ὑ. οὕτω διακεῖσθαι Isoc. 12.16 ; διαφέρεσθαι ἐν τῷ ποσῷ καὶ ταις ὑ. Arist. Pol. 1323a35 . like ὑπερβολή , excess, opp. ἔλλειψις (defect), in many senses, as in Arithm., one of the ἀριθμοῦ ᾗ ἀριθμὸς πάθη, Id. Metaph. 1004b12 , cf. Archim. Spir. 11 , Aequil. 1.2 , Dioph. 1.6 , al.; ἐν ἴσῃ ὑ., of an arithmetical progression, Papp. 76.21 , al., cf. Archyt. 2 , Porph. in Harm. p.266 W.; excess, of a sum of money, SIG 976.66 (Samos, ii B.C.); in Physics, Arist. Ph. 187a16 , 189b10 , HA 486b8 , al.; διαφέρειν καθ' ὑπεροχήν Id. PA 644a17 , al.; τάχος τὸ ὑ. [ἔχον] κινήσεως Id. Metaph. 1052b30 ; ἡ κατὰ τὴν ἀρετὴν ὑ. Id. EN 1098a11 , cf. Rh. 1368a25 ; τῶν ἠθῶν (sc. τοῦ ʼΕπικούρου) IG 22.1099.27 (Epist. Plotinae), cf. 42(1).86.18 (Epid., prob.); φιλίας εἶδος τὸ καθ' ὑ., where one exceeds the other in rank, etc., Arist. EN 1158b12 , cf. 1161a20 : pl., κατὰ πλούτων ὑπεροχάς Pl. Lg. 711d ; οἱ ἐν ὑπεροχαῖς εὐτυχημάτων ὄντες Arist. Pol. 1295b14 . alone, supremacy, authority, dignity, Plb. 1.64.1 ; τὴν Σελεύκου τοῦ βασιλέως ὑ. Antiph. 187.4 ; δαιμόνων ὑ. OGI 383.75 (Nemrud Dagh, i B.C.); οἱ ἐν ὑπεροχαῖς νεανίσκοι D.S. 4.41 ; οἱ ἐν ὑπεροχῇ ὄντες PTeb. 734.24 (ii B.C.), 1 Ep.Ti. 2.2 ; ἀνὴρ ἐν ὑ. κείμενος LXX 2 Ma. 3.11 . of language, periphrasis. prolixity, opp. ἔλλειψις, Pl. Plt. 283c . as a title, Excellency, Just. Nov. 25.5 ; ἡ ὑμετέρα Ὑ. POxy. 130.20 (vi A.D.).

term_table.lsj_entry_text: εὐκρασία (late εὐκοσμ-κρασίη Man. 5.59 ), ἡ, good temperature, mildness, τῶν ὡρῶν Pl. Ti. 24c ; τοῦ ἀέρος Plb. 34.8.4 : abs., Arist. Pr. 860b12 ; ἐν ταῖς εὐκρασίαις in good climates, Thphr. CP 3.21.1 . of persons, εὐ. τοῦ σώματος good temperament, Arist. PA 673b25 , cf. GA 744a30 , Zeno Stoic. 1.37 , Gal. 6.31 , etc.
term_table.greek_sentence: Μέσον οὖν τινα νόησόν μοι τῶνδε, τήν τε φύσιν εὐθὺς ἐξ ἀρχῆς εὔκρατον, ἔθεσί τε προσήκουσιν τὴν εὐκρασίαν ταύτην διαφυλάττοντα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Conceive for me, then, someone intermediate between these, both well-mixed in nature right from the beginning and preserving this good mixture by appropriate habits.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Conceive for me, then, someone midway between these, who is well-mixed in nature right from the start and who preserves this good mixture by suitable habits.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: τρεῖς, οἱ, αἱ,
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ τρεῖς τούτους ὥσπερ σκοποὺς κράσεως ἐν τῇ διανοίᾳ παραθέμενος ἐπίσκεψαι τὸ καθόλου θερμὸν, ἢ ψυχρὸν, ἢ ξηρὸν, ἢ ὑγρὸν φάρμακον, ὡς πρὸς ποίαν ἐξ αὐτῶν κρᾶσιν ἀποβλέποντα [571] προσαγορεύειν ἐστὶ βέλτιον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And having set these three before your mind as, so to speak, the targets of temperament, consider the drug that is hot, or cold, or dry, or moist in general, and ask with reference to which temperament among these it is [571] better to look in naming it.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And, having set these three side by side in your mind as standards, as it were, of mixture, consider the drug that is hot, or cold, or dry, or moist without qualification: looking to which of these mixtures [571] is it better to give it that name?

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἀγαθός [αγ], ή, όν, Lacon. ἀγασός Ar. Lys. 1301 , Cypr. ἀζαθός GDI 57 :— good: of persons, well-born, gentle, opp. κακός, δειλός, οἷά τε τοῖς ἀγαθοῖσι παραδρώωσι χέρηες Od. 15.324 , cf. Il. 1.275 ; ἀφνειός τ' ἀ. τε Il. 13.664 , cf. Od. 18.276 ; πατρὸς δ' εἴμ' ἀγαθοῖο, θεὰ δέ με γείνατο μήτηρ Il. 21.109 , cf. Od. 4.611 ; κακὸς ἐξ ἀ. Thgn. 190 , cf. 57 sq.; πραῢς ἀστοῖς, οὐ φθονέων ἀγαθοῖς Pi. P. 3.71 , cf. 2.96 , 4.285 ; τίς ἂν εὔπατρις ὧδε βλάστοι; οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀ. κτλ. S. El. 1082 ; οἵ τ' ἀ. πρὸς τῶν ἀγενῶν κατανικῶνται Id. Fr. 84 ; τοὺς εὐγενεῖς γὰρ κἀγαθοὺς . . φιλεῖ Ἄρης ἐναίρειν ib. 649 , cf. E. Alc. 600 , al.: ἀγαθοὶ καὶ ἐξ ἀγαθῶν Pl. Phdr. 274a :—in political sense, aristocrats, esp. in the phrase καλοὶ κἀγαθοί (v. sub καλοκἀγαθός). brave, valiant, since courage was attributed to Chiefs and Nobles, Il. 1.131 , al.; τῷ κ' ἀγαθὸς μὲν ἔπεφν', ἀγαθὸν δέ κεν ἐξενάριξεν 21.280 ; cf. Hdt. 5.109 , etc. good, capable, in reference to ability, ἀ. βασιλεύς Il. 3.179 ; ἰητήρ 2.732 ; θεράπων 16.165 , 17.388 ; πύκτης Xenoph. 2.15 ; ἰητρός Hp. Prog. 1 ; προβατογνώμων A. Ag. 795 ; ἄρχοντες Democr. 266 : freq. with qualifying words, ἀ. ἐν ὑσμίνῃ Il. 13.314 ; βοὴν ἀ. 2.408 , 563 , al.; πύξ Od. 11.300 ; βίην Il. 6.478 ; γνώμην S. OT 687 ; πᾶσαν ἀρετήν Pl. Lg. 899b , cf. Alc. 1.124e ; τέχνην Id. Prt. 323b ; τὰ πολέμια, τὰ πολιτικά, Hdt. 9.122 , Pl. Grg. 516b , etc.: more rarely c. dat., ἀ. πολέμῳ X. Oec. 4.15 : with Preps., ἄνδρες ἀ. περὶ τὸ πλῆθος Lys. 13.2 ; εἴς τι Pl. Alc. 1.125a ; πρός τι Id. R. 407e : c. inf., ἀ. μάχεσθαι Hdt. 1.136 ; ἱππεύεσθαι 1.79 ; ἀ. ἱστάναι good at weighing, Pl. Prt. 356b . good, in moral sense, first in Thgn. 438 , cf. Heraclit. 104 , S. El. 1082 , X. Mem. 1.7.1 , Pl. Ap. 41d , etc.; ψυχῆς ἀγαθῆς πατρὶς ὁ ξύμπας κόσμος Democr. 247 : freq. with other Adjs., ὁ πιστὸς κἀ. S. Tr. 541 ; δικαίων κἀ. ib. 1050 :—ironical, τὸν ἀ. Κρέοντα Id. Ant. 31 . ὦ ἀγαθέ, my good friend, as a term of gentle remonstrance, Pl. Prt. 311a , etc. ἀ. δαίμων, v. sub δαίμων; ἀ. τύχη, v. sub τύχη; ἀ. θεός = Lat. bona dea, Plu. Caes. 9 , Cic. 19 . of things, good, serviceable, Ἰθάκη . . ἀ. κουροτρόφος Od. 9.27 , etc.; ἀ. τοῖς τοκεῦσι, τῇ πόλει X. Cyn. 13.17 : c. gen., εἴ τι οἶδα πυρετοῦ ἀ. good for it, Id. Mem. 3.8.3 ; ἑλκῶν Thphr. HP 9.11.1 . of outward circumstances, αἰδὼς οὐκ ἀ. κεχρημένῳ ἀνδρὶ παρεῖναι Od. 17.347 ; εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀγαθόν to good purpose, Il. 9.102 ; ὁ δὲ πείσεται εἰς ἀ. περ for his own good end, 11.789 ; οὐκ ἀγαθὸν πολυκοιρανίη 2.204 :—ἀγαθόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it is good to do so and so<*> Il. 7.282 , 24.130 , Od. 3.196 , etc. morally good, πρῆξις Democr. 177 ; ἔργα Emp. 112.2 , cf. Ep.Rom. 2.7 , etc. ἀγαθόν, τό, good, blessing, benefit, of persons or things, ὦ μέγα ἀ. σὺ τοῖς φίλοις X. Cyr. 5.3.20 ; φίλον, ὃ μέγιστον ἀ. εἶναί φασι Id. Mem. 2.4.2 , cf. Ar. Ra. 74 , etc; as term of endearment for a baby, blessing!, treasure!, Men. Sam. 28 :— ἀγαθόν τινα δεδρακέναι, πεποιηκέναι confer a benefit on . . , Th. 3.68 , Lys. 13.92 ; ἐπ' ἀγαθῷ τινος for one's good, Th. 5.27 , X. Cyr. 7.4.3 ; ἐπ' ἀ. τοῖς πολίταις Ar. Ra. 1487 ; οὐκ ἐπ' ἀ. for no good end, Th. 1.131 ; ἐπ' οὐδενὶ ἀ. τῆς Ἑλλάδος X. HG 5.2.35 :—in pl., ἡ ἐπ' ἀγαθοῖς γεναμένη (sic) κατασπορά PFlor. 21.10 (iii A.D.):—τὸ ἀ. or τἀ., the good, Epich. 171.5 , cf. Pl. R. 506b , 508e , Arist. Metaph. 1091a31 , etc.:—in pl., ἀγαθά, τά, goods of fortune, treasures, wealth, Hdt. 2.172 , Lys. 13.91 , X. Mem. 1.2.63 , etc.; ἀγαθὰ πράττειν fare well, Ar. Av. 1706 ; also, good things, dainties, Thgn. 1000 , Ar. Ach. 873 , etc.: good qualities, τοῖς ἀ., οἷς ἔχομεν ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ Isoc. 8.32 , cf. Democr. 37 ; good points, of a horse, εἰ τἄλλα πάντα ἀ. ἔχοι, κακόπους δ' εἴη X. Eq. 1.2 . Comp. and Sup. are usu. supplied from other stems, viz. Comp. ἀμείνων, ἀρείων<*> βελτίων, κρείσσων ʽκάρρωνʼ, λωΐων (λώʽωνʼ), Ep. βέλτερος, λωΐτερος, φέρτερος:— Sup. ἄριστος, βέλτιστος, κράτιστος, λώϊστος (λῷστος), Ep. βέλτατος, κάρτιστος, φέρτατος, φέριστος:— later, reg. Comp. ἀγαθώτερος LXX Jd. 11.25 , 15.2 , D.S. 8 Fr. 12 , Plot. 5.5.9 , Diod.Rh. p.53.9H. : Sup. ἀγαθώτατος D.S. 16.85 , Hld. 5.15 , etc. ( -ότατος POxy. 1757.26 (ii A.D.)). Adv. usually εὖ, q.v.: ἀγαθῶς Hp. Off. 9 , Arist. Rh. 1388b6 , LXX 1 Ki. 20.7 . (Etym. dub. ( ὅτι ἄγει ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸν ὀρθὸν βίον Stoic. 3.49 ); perh. cognate with ἄγαμαι, hence admirable.)
