term_table.greek_sentence: ὥστε ἐν τῷ ψαύειν τῆς γλώττης ἐνεργεῖν μὲν ἅπαντα κατὰ τὸ διαφέρον ἕκαστον αὐτῶν μόριον, ᾧπερ ἂν ὁμιλῆσαν τύχῃ, διαδίδοσθαι δὲ τὴν διάθεσιν ἐκ τοῦ πρώτου παθόντος εἰς ὅλην αὐτὴν, ὥσπερ ὅταν εἰς ὕδωρ ψυχρὸν ἕνα δάκτυλον ἀθρόως καθέντες ἐν ψύχει σφοδρῷ φρίξομεν ὅλην τὴν χεῖρα, πολλάκις δὲ καὶ σύμπαν τὸ σῶμα· ταχεῖα γὰρ ἡ διάδοσις ἐν τοῖς αἰσθητικοῖς σώμασιν ἐκ τοῦ πρώτου παθόντος εἰς ὅλον γίνεται τὸ ζῶον, ὥστε καὶ θερμαινομένῳ συνθερμαίνεσθαι καὶ ψυχομένῳ συμψύχεσθαι καὶ ξηραινομένῳ ﻿ [585] συγξηραίνεσθαι καὶ ὑγραινομένῳ συνυγραίνεσθαι, καὶ πολλάκις τἀναντία πάσχειν ὅλον ὑφ’ ἕνα καιρόν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: so that, in the contact with the tongue, all of them act, each part of them according to its own distinct character, upon whatever part it happens to have come into contact with, and the disposition is transmitted from the part first affected to the whole tongue—just as when, in severe cold, we plunge a single finger all at once into cold water and shiver with the whole hand, and often with the entire body as well. For the transmission in sensitive bodies from the part first affected to the whole animal takes place swiftly, so that when a part is heated the whole is heated along with it, when it is cooled the whole is cooled along with it, when it is dried [585] the whole is dried along with it, and when it is moistened the whole is moistened along with it, and often the whole undergoes contrary affections at one and the same time.
term_table.english_sentence_B: so that, in touching the tongue, all of them act, each of them on whatever different part of it it happens to come into contact with, while the affection is transmitted from the part first affected to the whole tongue; just as, when in severe cold we plunge one finger suddenly into cold water, we shiver over the whole hand, and often over the entire body as well. For in sensitive bodies the transmission from the part first affected to the whole animal takes place quickly, so that the whole is heated together with what is being heated, cooled together with what is being cooled, dried [585] together with what is being dried, and moistened together with what is being moistened, and often the whole suffers contrary things at one and the same time.

Prt. 356b . good, in moral sense, first in Thgn. 438 , cf. Heraclit. 104 , S. El. 1082 , X. Mem. 1.7.1 , Pl. Ap. 41d , etc.; ψυχῆς ἀγαθῆς πατρὶς ὁ ξύμπας κόσμος Democr. 247 : freq. with other Adjs., ὁ πιστὸς κἀ. S. Tr. 541 ; δικαίων κἀ. ib. 1050 :—ironical, τὸν ἀ. Κρέοντα Id. Ant. 31 . ὦ ἀγαθέ, my good friend, as a term of gentle remonstrance, Pl. Prt. 311a , etc. ἀ. δαίμων, v. sub δαίμων; ἀ. τύχη, v. sub τύχη; ἀ. θεός = Lat. bona dea, Plu. Mem. 3.8.3 ; ἑλκῶν Thphr. HP 9.11.1 . of outward circumstances, αἰδὼς οὐκ ἀ. κεχρημένῳ ἀνδρὶ παρεῖναι Od. 17.347 ; εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀγαθόν to good purpose, Il. 9.102 ; ὁ δὲ πείσεται εἰς ἀ. περ for his own good end, 11.789 ; οὐκ ἀγαθὸν πολυκοιρανίη 2.204 :—ἀγαθόν [ἐστι], c. inf., it is good to do so and so<*> Il. 7.282 , 24.130 , Od. 3.196 , etc. morally good, πρῆξις Democr. 177 ; ἔργα Emp. 112.2 , cf. Ep.Rom. 2.7 , etc. ἀγαθόν, τό, good, blessing, benefit, of persons or things, ὦ μέγα ἀ. σὺ τοῖς φίλοις X. Cyr. 5.3.20 ; φίλον, ὃ μέγιστον ἀ. εἶναί φασι Id. Mem. 2.4.2 , cf. Ar. Ra. 74 , etc; as term of endearment for a baby, blessing!, treasure!, Men. Sam. 28 :— ἀγαθόν τινα δεδρακέναι, πεποιηκέναι confer a benefit on . . , Th. 3.68 , Lys. 13.92 ; ἐπ' ἀγαθῷ τινος for one's good, Th. 5.27 , X. Cyr. 7.4.3 ; ἐπ' ἀ. τοῖς πολίταις Ar. Ra. 1487 ; οὐκ ἐπ' ἀ. for no good end, Th. 1.131 ; ἐπ' οὐδενὶ ἀ. τῆς Ἑλλάδος X. HG 5.2.35 :—in pl., ἡ ἐπ' ἀγαθοῖς γεναμένη (sic) κατασπορά PFlor. 21.10 (iii A.D.):—τὸ ἀ. or τἀ., the good, Epich. 171.5 , cf. Pl. R. 506b , 508e , Arist. Metaph. 1091a31 , etc.:—in pl., ἀγαθά, τά, goods of fortune, treasures, wealth, Hdt. 2.172 , Lys. 13.91 , X. Mem. 1.2.63 , etc.; ἀγαθὰ πράττειν fare well, Ar. term_table.lsj_entry_text: κέντρον, τό, (κεντέω) any sharp point: horse-goad, [ ἵπποι] ἄνευ κέντροιο θέοντες Il. 23.387 , cf. 430 , Ar. Nu. 1297 , X. Cyr. 7.1.29 , etc.; διπλοῖς κέντροισι S. term_table.english_sentence_A: You have seen, I think, at some time, when a stone has been thrown into still water, that the water begins to move from that point and extends the movement in a circle, with the thing that struck it as if at a centre.
term_table.english_sentence_B: You have seen, I suppose, at some time, when a stone was thrown into still water, the water beginning to move from it and extending its movement in a circle, the thing that struck it being, as it were, the centre.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὅταν οὖν ὑφ’ ἕνα καιρὸν εἰς διαφέροντας τόπους ἀτρεμίζοντος ὕδατος ἐμβληθέντες δύο λίθοι γεννήσωσι δύο κύκλους δι’ ἀλλήλων φερομένους, ἐναντίας ὄψει κινήσεις ἐν ἅπαντι μορίῳ τοῦ ὕδατος, ὅθεν καὶ ἀπορίαν παρέσχε τὸ φαινόμενον τοῦτο καὶ αὐτοῖς τοῖς φυσικοῖς ἀνδράσιν, εἴθ’ ἕτερα μόρια πρὸς ἑκατέρας τῶν κινήσεων, εἴτε καὶ ταὐτὰ κινεῖται πρὸς ἀμφοτέρων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So when, at one and the same time, two stones thrown into different places in still water generate two circles passing through one another, you will see contrary movements in every part of the water; whence this phenomenon has presented a difficulty even to the natural philosophers themselves, whether it is different parts that move in respect of each of the two movements, or the same parts that are moved by both.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Now when, at one and the same time, two stones thrown into different places of still water generate two circles that travel through one another, you will see contrary movements in every part of the water; whence this phenomenon has also caused perplexity to the natural philosophers themselves, whether different parts are moved for each of the two movements, or the same parts are moved by both.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ γὰρ πάσχει σαφῶς καὶ ὑπ’ ἀμφοῖν πάσχει θερμαινόμενόν τε ἅμα καὶ ψυχόμενον, ὥσπερ, οἶμαι, κᾀν ταῖς λειπυρίαις καὶ τοῖς ἠπιάλοις συμπίπτει πυρετοῖς, πλὴν οὐκ ἔξωθέν γε ἐν ἐκείνοις, ἀλλ’ ἐξ αὐτοῦ τοῦ σώματος ἥ τε τῆς ψύξεως καὶ ἡ τῆς θέρμης ὁρμᾶται διάθεσις.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For it is clearly affected, and it is affected by both, being heated and cooled at the same time, just as, I think, happens also in the leipyriai and the epialos fevers, except that in those the condition of cooling and that of heat does not set out from outside, but from the body itself.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For it is plainly affected, and affected by both, being heated and cooled at the same time, just as, I think, also happens in the leipyriae and in the epialoi fevers; except that in those cases it is not from outside, but from the body itself, that both the condition of cooling and that of heat take their start.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ῥᾴδιος (ῥαιδ- correctly in early texts, PCair.Zen. 367.20 (iii B.C.), etc., later ῥαδ-, Diog.Oen. 10 , etc.), α, ον: Ep. and Ion. ῥηΐδιος [ιδ], η, ον , as always in Hom. ; ῥῄδιος, η, ον, Thgn. 574 , 577 (v. infr. B):—Degrees of Comparison: ῥᾳδιώτερος is cited from Hyp. by Poll. 5.107 , perhaps by error for ῥᾳδιέστερος, which occurs in Hyp. Fr. 86 , Arist. Pr. 870b37 (as Adv.), Plb. 11.1.1 , 16.20.4 . Adv. -έστατα Ph. Bel. 96.33 :—but the form ῥᾴων, ῥᾷον is more common, Th. 5.36 , etc.; Ion. ῥηΐων, ῥήϊον, (v. infr. B); Ep. ῥηΐτερος Il. 18.258 , 24.243 , etc.; contr. ῥῄτερος Thgn. 1370 ; Dor. ῥᾴτερος Pi. O. 8.60 (ῥαΐτερον codd.); a form ῥᾴσσων in EM 158.15 : ῥᾳότερον, gloss on εὐπετέστερον , Erot. p.35 N.: Sup. , Att. ῥᾷστος, η, ον ; Dor. ῥάϊστος Theoc. 11.7 (Adv.); Ion. and Ep. ῥήϊστος Od. 4.565 ; contr. ῥῇστος Timo 67.2 (Adv.); Ep. ῥηΐτατος, v. infr. B. 111 fin.: (v. ῥᾶ, ῥέα, ῥεῖα):—easy, ready, and so easy to make or do, opp. χαλεπός ( Arist. Rh. 1363a23 ); ῥηΐδιόν τι ἔπος a word easy to understand and follow, Od. 11.146 , cf. h.Ap. 534 ; οἶμος ῥηϊδίη an easy road, Hes. Op. 292 ; ταχὺς γὰρ Ἅιδης ῥᾷστος ἀνδρὶ δυστυχεῖ, i. e. least painful, E. Hipp. 1047 : c. inf., τάφρος περῆσαι ῥηϊδίη easy to pass over, Il. 12.54 ; ῥηΐτεροι πολεμίζειν ἦσαν Ἀχαιοί easier to fight with, 18.258 ; ῥηΐτεροι . . Ἀχαιοῖσιν ἐναιρέμεν easier for them to slay, 24.243 ; οὐ ῥηΐδι' ἐστὶ θεῶν ἐρικυδέα δῶρα ἀνδράσι γε θνητοῖσι δαμήμεναι 20.265 ; ῥᾴονι ἂν ἐχρώμεθα τῷ Φιλίππῳ we should have found P. easier to resist, D. 1.9 . ῥᾴδιόν ἐστι it is easy, c. inf., ῥᾴδιον πόλιν σεῖσαι καὶ ἀφαυροτέροις Pi. P. 4.272 ; τοῖς γὰρ δικαίοις ἀντέχειν οὐ ῥᾴδιον S. Fr. 78 , cf. Ph. 1395 , Ar. Th. 68 , Th. 6.21 , etc.: c. acc. et inf., τύραννον εὐσεβεῖν οὐ ῥᾴδιον S. Aj. 1350 , cf. X. HG 6.2.10 ; χαλεπὸν τὸ ποιεῖν, τὸ δὲ κελεῦσαι ῥ. Philem. 27 ; τὸ ἐπιτιμᾶν ῥ. καὶ παντὸς εἶναι D. 1.16 ; ῥᾷον παραινεῖν ἢ παθόντα καρτερεῖν Men. Mon. 471 , etc.: ῥᾷστοί εἰσιν ἀμύνεσθαι,= ῥᾴδιόν ἐστιν αὐτοὺς ἀμύνεσθαι, Th. 4.10 ; ῥᾷσται ἐς τὸ βλάπτεσθαι (sc. αἱ νῆες) Id. 7.67 . also ῥᾴδιόν ἐστι it is a light matter, you think little of doing, παρ' ὑμῖν ῥ. ξενοκτονεῖν E. Hec. 1247 . Adv. phrase, ἐκ ῥᾳδίας easily, Plot. 4.8.1 . easy-going, adaptable, ῥ. ἤθεα E. Hipp. 1116 (lyr.); in bad sense, reckless, unscrupulous, ῥ. τὸν τρόπον Luc. Merc.Cond. 40 , cf. Alex. 4 ; ῥ. τὼ ὀφθαλμώ having a roving eye, Alciphr. 1.6 ; cf. B. 1.2 , ῥᾳδιουργός. ῥᾴων γενέσθαι to be easier, get better, of a sick person, Hp. Loc.Hom. 34 ; ὡσπερεὶ ῥ. ἔσομαι shall feel easier, better, D. 45.57 ; ταῦτ' ἢν ποιῇς, ῥ. ἔσει Theopomp.Com. 62 ; Εὐριπίδου μνήσθητι, καὶ ῥ. ἔσει Philippid. 18 . Adv. ῥᾳδίως, Aeol. βραϊδίως Theoc. 30.27 ; Ep. and Ion. ῥηϊδίως, as always in Hom. ; ῥηδίως Herod. 7.69 :—easily, readily, Il. 4.390 , al., Hes. Op. 43 , Hdt. 9.2 , etc.; in Trag. and Att. freq. ῥᾳδίως φέρειν bear lightly or with equanimity, make light of a thing, E. Andr. 744 , etc.; ῥ. προσίσταται ib. 232 ; ῥ. ἀπολείπειν to leave not unwillingly, Th. 1.2 ; ῥᾳδίως ἀπαλλάττοιντο αὐτῶν Pl. Phd. 63a . in bad sense, lightly, recklessly, ῥ. περὶ μεγάλων βουλεύεσθαι Th. 1.73 , cf. Pl. Lg. 917b ; ῥᾳδίως οὕτως in this easy, thoughtless way, Id. R. 377b , 378a ; ῥ. τολμῶσι λέγειν Lys. 19.49 . of things, ταλάντου ῥᾳδίως ἄξιος easily, fully worth a talent, Is. 8.35 ; οὐ ῥ. hardly, scarcely, Plu. Lyc. 31 , cf. 2.39b . Comp. , ῥᾷον φέρειν Th. 8.89 ; ῥ. ὀμνύναι κἀπιορκεῖν ἢ ὁτιοῦν nothing so easy, D. 54.39 ; Ion. ῥήϊον Hp. Int. 12 ; also ῥηϊτέρως, Id. Mul. 1.1 , 26 . Sup. ῥᾷστα, esp. in phrases, ῥᾷστα φέρειν S. OT 983 ; ὡς ῥᾷστα φέρειν A. Pr. 104 , E. Hel. 254 , cf. Supp. 954 , etc.; ῥ. τε καὶ ἥδιστα βιοτεύειν X. Mem. 2.1.9 ; later, ἐκ τοῦ ῥᾴστου D.H. Comp. 25 , Plu. Fab. 11 : Ep. ῥηΐτατα Od. 19.577 .

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ γὰρ ἀναμίξας ἀκριβῶς ἶσον ἀψινθίου καὶ μέλιτος ὄγκον ἐπιθείης τῇ γλώττῃ, γλυκύπικρον, ὥσπερ οἱ ποιηταὶ τὸν ἔρωτα προσαγορεύουσι, φανεῖταί σοι τὸ μικτὸν ἐξ ἀμφοῖν, οὐκ ἐν ἄλλῳ μέν τινι χρόνῳ μέλιτος αἰσθανομένης τῆς γλώττης, ἐν ἄλλῳ δὲ ἀψινθίου, οὔτε θατέρου μόνον, ἀλλὰ διὰ παντὸς ἀμφοῖν ἀήθη τινὰ μίξιν μεμιγμένην.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For if, having thoroughly mixed an equal bulk of wormwood and of honey, you apply it to the tongue, the mixture of both will appear to you sweet-bitter, as the poets call love, the tongue not perceiving honey at one time and wormwood at another, nor only one of the two, but throughout perceiving both, mixed in a certain unaccustomed mixture.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For if, having mixed precisely equal bulks of wormwood and honey, you place it on the tongue, the mixture of the two will appear to you bittersweet, as the poets call love; the tongue does not perceive the honey at one time and the wormwood at another, nor only one of them, but perceives both throughout, mixed in a certain unaccustomed mixture.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ γὰρ ἀναμίξας ἀκριβῶς ἶσον ἀψινθίου καὶ μέλιτος ὄγκον ἐπιθείης τῇ γλώττῃ, γλυκύπικρον, ὥσπερ οἱ ποιηταὶ τὸν ἔρωτα προσαγορεύουσι, φανεῖταί σοι τὸ μικτὸν ἐξ ἀμφοῖν, οὐκ ἐν ἄλλῳ μέν τινι χρόνῳ μέλιτος αἰσθανομένης τῆς γλώττης, ἐν ἄλλῳ δὲ ἀψινθίου, οὔτε θατέρου μόνον, ἀλλὰ διὰ παντὸς ἀμφοῖν ἀήθη τινὰ μίξιν μεμιγμένην.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For if, having thoroughly mixed an equal bulk of wormwood and of honey, you apply it to the tongue, the mixture of both will appear to you sweet-bitter, as the poets call love, the tongue not perceiving honey at one time and wormwood at another, nor only one of the two, but throughout perceiving both, mixed in a certain unaccustomed mixture.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For if, having mixed precisely equal bulks of wormwood and honey, you place it on the tongue, the mixture of the two will appear to you bittersweet, as the poets call love; the tongue does not perceive the honey at one time and the wormwood at another, nor only one of them, but perceives both throughout, mixed in a certain unaccustomed mixture.

term_table.greek_sentence: τοιόνδε [587] τι γίγνεται κᾀν τῷ συνελθεῖν εἰς ἕνα χυμὸν αὐστηρὸν καὶ νιτρώδη δύναμιν, ἤτοι τῆς φύσεως αὐτῆς ἀναμιξάσης ἤ τινος ἰατροῦ συνθέντος.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Something of this kind [587] also comes about when a harsh and a nitrous power come together into a single juice, whether nature herself has mixed them or some physician has compounded them.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Something of this sort [587] happens also when a harsh and a nitrous power come together into a single flavour, whether nature itself has mixed them or some physician has compounded them. For the tongue perceives the quality of each of the two flavours at one and the same time; and if it perceives them, it is clearly also disposed according to their proper powers.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἥ τε γὰρ γλῶττα τῆς ἑκατέρου τῶν χυμῶν ποιότητος ὑφ’ ἕνα χρόνον αἰσθάνεται, καὶ εἴπερ αἰσθάνεται, δηλονότι καὶ διατίθεται κατὰ τὰς οἰκείας αὐτῶν δυνάμεις, ἕκαστόν τε τῶν ἄλλων τοῦ σώματος μορίων ἀνάγκη πάσχειν ὡσαύτως, εἰ καὶ μὴ τῶν ποιοτήτων αἰσθάνηται· οὐ γὰρ δὴ τῷ γε πάσχειν ἢ μὴ διαφέρειν τῶν ἄλλων ὑποληπτέον τὴν γλῶτταν, ἀλλὰ τῷ μὴ λανθάνειν αὐτὴν μηδὲν τῶν οἰκείων παθῶν ἀκριβείᾳ δυνάμεως αἰσθητικῆς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For the tongue perceives the quality of each of the two juices at one and the same time, and if it perceives them, clearly it is also disposed according to their proper powers; and each of the other parts of the body must necessarily be affected in the same way, even if it does not perceive the qualities. For one must not suppose that the tongue differs from the other parts in being affected or not, but in the fact that none of its proper affections escapes its notice, owing to the precision of its perceptive power.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Each of the other parts of the body must likewise be affected in the same way, even if it does not perceive the qualities. For one must not suppose that the tongue differs from the other parts in being affected or not being affected, but in that none of its own affections escapes it, owing to the precision of its perceptive faculty.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἥ τε γὰρ γλῶττα τῆς ἑκατέρου τῶν χυμῶν ποιότητος ὑφ’ ἕνα χρόνον αἰσθάνεται, καὶ εἴπερ αἰσθάνεται, δηλονότι καὶ διατίθεται κατὰ τὰς οἰκείας αὐτῶν δυνάμεις, ἕκαστόν τε τῶν ἄλλων τοῦ σώματος μορίων ἀνάγκη πάσχειν ὡσαύτως, εἰ καὶ μὴ τῶν ποιοτήτων αἰσθάνηται· οὐ γὰρ δὴ τῷ γε πάσχειν ἢ μὴ διαφέρειν τῶν ἄλλων ὑποληπτέον τὴν γλῶτταν, ἀλλὰ τῷ μὴ λανθάνειν αὐτὴν μηδὲν τῶν οἰκείων παθῶν ἀκριβείᾳ δυνάμεως αἰσθητικῆς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For the tongue perceives the quality of each of the two juices at one and the same time, and if it perceives them, clearly it is also disposed according to their proper powers; and each of the other parts of the body must necessarily be affected in the same way, even if it does not perceive the qualities. For one must not suppose that the tongue differs from the other parts in being affected or not, but in the fact that none of its proper affections escapes its notice, owing to the precision of its perceptive power.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Each of the other parts of the body must likewise be affected in the same way, even if it does not perceive the qualities. For one must not suppose that the tongue differs from the other parts in being affected or not being affected, but in that none of its own affections escapes it, owing to the precision of its perceptive faculty.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μανότης, ητος, ἡ, opp. πυκνότης, looseness of texture, porousness, σπληνός, ὀστῶν, Pl. Ti. 72c , 86d ; σαρκός Arist. EN 1129a22 , cf. Thphr. HP 1.5.4 , al. rarity, separateness, Pl. Lg. 812d ; τῶν φυτευομένων Thphr. CP 3.7.1 .

term_table.english_sentence_A: Its looseness of texture also contributes to this; for the juices, descending more easily into the depth and acting upon the soft parts, produce a disposition that is strong and a perception of it that is more evident.

term_table.greek_sentence: ῥᾷον γὰρ εἰς τὸ βάθος οἱ χυλοὶ κατιόντες ἐνεργοῦντές τε περὶ τὰ μαλακὰ τῶν μορίων ἰσχυρὰν μὲν τὴν διάθεσιν, ἐναργεστέραν δὲ καὶ τὴν αἴσθησιν αὐτῆς ἀπεργάζονται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Its looseness of texture also contributes to this; for the juices, descending more easily into the depth and acting upon the soft parts, produce a disposition that is strong and a perception of it that is more evident.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For the juices, descending more easily into its depth and acting upon its soft parts, produce a strong condition, and also a more evident perception of that condition.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ γὰρ ἐπιθείης φλεγμαίνοντι μορίῳ στρύχνου χυλὸν, ὄψει πυκνούμενον αὐτὸ καὶ πιλούμενον καὶ τὰς διαπνοὰς ἐπεχομένας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: [588] Yet it is possible, both in those parts and even before them, while the skin is not yet ulcerated, to infer by reasoning the mixed activity that arises in bodies from the opposite powers at the same time.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For if you apply the juice of strychnos to an inflamed part, you will see it being condensed and compacted, and its transpirations being checked.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πελιδν-ός, ή, όν, = πελιός , livid, Hp. Aph. 4.47 , Arist. Pr. 887b10 , HA 523a9 ( Comp. ), Nic. Th. 272 , al. ; of the mask worn by Tyro in Sophocles' play, Poll. 4.141 ; Att. πελιτνός acc. to Ael. Dion. Fr. 278 , Moer. p.325 P. , which shd. be read in Th. 2.49 , Alex. 110.17 , Com.Adesp. 342 .
term_table.greek_sentence: ὥστ’ εἰ καὶ μέχρι πλείονος οὕτω ποιήσαις, οὐδ’ ἐρυθρὸν ἔτι φυλάξαις τὸ μόριον, ἀλλ’ ἤτοι πελιδνὸν ἢ μέλαν ἐργάσῃ, ὁποῖόν τι κᾀν τοῖς ἐρυσιπέλασι ποιοῦσι συνεχῶς οἱ πλεῖστοι τῶν ἰατρῶν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For if you apply the juice of strychnos to an inflamed part, you will see it being condensed and compacted and the transpirations being held back; so that, if you were to do this for a longer time, you would no longer even preserve the part red, but you would make it either livid or black, just the sort of thing that most physicians continually do in cases of erysipelas as well; for these too they blacken and harden in the course of time by chilling them immoderately.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So that, if you do this for a longer time, you will no longer even keep the part red, but will make it either livid or black, which is just the sort of thing that most physicians continually do in erysipelases as well.

term_table.greek_sentence: οὐ γὰρ δὴ μερισάμενά γε τοὺς χρόνους ἐνήργησεν, ὥστε εἰ τύχοι δι’ ὅλης ἡμέρας ἐπιτεθέντων ἀμφοῖν ἕξ μὲν ταῖς πρώταις ὥραις θάτερον τῶν φαρμάκων, ἓξ δὲ ταῖς ὑπολοίποις θάτερον ἐνεργῆσαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For surely they did not act by dividing up the times between them, so that, say, when both had been applied for a whole day, one of the drugs acted during the first six hours and the other during the remaining six.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For they certainly did not act by dividing the times between them, so that, for instance, when both had been applied for a whole day, one of the drugs acted during the first six hours and the other during the remaining six.

Smp. 186b ; τὸ δὲ ταὐτὸν ἕ. ἀποφαίνειν καὶ τὸ θάτερον ταὐτόν Id. Sph. 259d ; ἕ. ἤδη ἦν καὶ οὐχ ὁ αὐτός D. 34.12 ; ἑτέραν ἔδωκεν παντὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ὄψιν OGI 458.7 (i B. C.); ἕ. εὐαγγέλιον Ep.Gal. 1.6 : coupled with ἄλλος, χἀτέρους ἄλλους πόνους and other different toils, E. Supp. 573 (s.v.l.), cf. Or. 345 (dub.l.); Ῥόδον καὶ ἄλλας ἑτέρας πόλεις D. 15.27 ; ἕτερον τό τ' ἀλγεῖν καὶ θεωρεῖν ἐστ' ἴσως Philem. 75.7 ; ἕτερα φρονῶν καὶ δημηγορῶν Din. 1.17 : c.gen., other than, different from, φίλους . . ἑτέρους τῶν νῦν ὄντων Th. 1.28 , cf. Pl. Prt. 333a , D. 10.44 , etc.; ἕτερον, ἕτερα ἢ . . , E. Or. 345 , X. Cyr. 1.6.2 ; παρὰ ταῦτα πάντα ἕτερόν τι Pl. Phd. 74a ; ἕτερα πολιτείας εἴδη παρὰ μοναρχίαν Arist. Pol. 1294a25 , cf. 1286b21 . other than should be, euphem. for κακός, παθεῖν μὲν εὖ, παθεῖν δὲ θάτερα S. Ph. 503 ; ἀγάθ' ἢ θάτερα, ἵνα μηδὲν εἴπω φλαῦρον D. 22.12 : abs., δαίμων ἕ. Pi. P. 3.34 ; λέκτρα, συμφοραί, E. Med. 639 (lyr.), HF 1238 ; ἐὰν τὰ ἕ. ψηφίσωνται οἱ δικασταί D. 48.30 ; πλέον θάτερον ἐποίησαν did more harm (than good), Isoc. 19.25 , cf. Pl. Phd. 114e , Euthd. 280e , Aristid. 2.117 J. Special Phrases: elliptical, mostly in dat. fem., τῇ ἑτέρᾳ (sc. χειρί), Ep. ἑτέρῃ or ἑτέρηφι, with one hand (v. sub init.); with the left hand, Od. 3.441 , Il. 22.80 , Theoc. 24.45 : hence prov., οὐ τῇ ἑτέρᾳ ληπτός not to be caught with one hand, Pl. Sph. 226a ; ἐκ δ' ἑτέρης A.R. 1.1115 , AP 9.650 ( Leont. ). θατέρᾳ (sc. ἡμέρᾳ) on the morrow, S. OT 782 , E. Rh. 449 ; τῆς ἑτέρας Pl. Cri. 44a ; but τῇ ἑτέρᾳ on the following (i.e. the third) day, X. Cyr. 4.6.10 . (sc. ὁδῷ) in another or a different way, καὶ τῇδε φῦναι χἀτέρᾳ S. OC 1444 ; another way, τρέπεσθαι Ar. Nu. 812 ; ἑτέρᾳ πῃ Id. Eq. 35 ; τότ' ἄλλοσ' . . , θατέρᾳ δὲ . . S. Tr. 272 ; θατέρᾳ . . , θατέρᾳ . . in one way . . , in the other . . , Henioch. 5.16 ; ἑτέρηφι Hes. Op. 216 : acc. ἑτέραν ἐκτρέπεσθαι Luc. Tim. 5 . adverb. with Preps.: ἐπὶ θάτερα to the one or the other side, one or the other way, ἐπὶ μὲν θάτερα . . , ἐπὶ θ. δὲ . . Hp. Art. 7 ; τότε μὲν ἐπὶ θάτερα, τότε δ' ἐπὶ θ. Pl. Sph. 259c : also with another Prep., ἐς τὰ ἐπὶ θάτερα to or on the other side, Th. 1.87 ; ἐκ τοῦ ἐπὶ θάτερα from the other side, Id. 7.37 ; ἐκ μὲν τοῦ ἐπὶ θ., ἐκ δὲ τοῦ ἐπὶ θ. Pl. Prt. 314e : c. gen., ἐς τὰ ἐπὶ θ. τοῦ ποταμοῦ Th. 7.84 ; εἰς τἀπὶ θ. τῆς πόλεως X. HG 6.2.7 ; τὸ ἐπὶ θάτερον τῆς ῥινός Hp. Art. 35 . κατὰ θάτερα on the one or other side, κατὰ θ. ἀστός D. 57.30 ; ψόφου κατὰ θ. προσπεσόντος Plu. Brut. 51 , etc.; but καθ' ἕτερα at other points, Th. 7.42 . Adv. ἑτέρως in one or the other way, opp. ἀμφοτέρως, Pl. Tht. 181e ; ἑ. τε καὶ ἑ., = ἀμφοτέρως , Id. Phdr. 235a ; τοῦ σκέλους ἑ. ἔχειν, = ἑτεροσκελὴς εἶναι , Philostr. VA 3.39 . differently, rarely in Poetry, οὐχ ἑ. τις ἐρεῖ Theoc. Ep. 10.3 ; ἑ. ἔχειν to be different, Ar. Pl. 371 : freq. in Prose, ὡς ἑ. in the other way (cf. ὡς) , ἢν ἡ ἑτέρη γνάθος ἐκστῇ ὡς ἑ. χρὴ τὴν ἐπίδεσιν ἄγειν Hp. Art. 34 , cf. Pl. Sph. 266a , etc.; ἐάν τε καλῶς, ἐάν θ' ὡς ἑ. D. 18.85 , cf. 212 : c. gen., differently from, ἑ. πως τῶν εἰωθότων Pl. Plt. 295d ; ἑ. ἤπερ . . Ael. NA 12.28 . otherwise than should be, badly, wrongly, once in Hom. , ἑ. ἐβόλοντο Od. 1.234 ; εἰ καὶ ἑ. τοῦτο ἀπέβη SIG 851.10 (Marc.Aur.); εἴ τι ἑ. φρονεῖτε Ep.Phil. 3.15 .
term_table.greek_sentence: οὐ γὰρ δὴ μερισάμενά γε τοὺς χρόνους ἐνήργησεν, ὥστε εἰ τύχοι δι’ ὅλης ἡμέρας ἐπιτεθέντων ἀμφοῖν ἕξ μὲν ταῖς πρώταις ὥραις θάτερον τῶν φαρμάκων, ἓξ δὲ ταῖς ὑπολοίποις θάτερον ἐνεργῆσαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For surely they did not act by dividing up the times between them, so that, say, when both had been applied for a whole day, one of the drugs acted during the first six hours and the other during the remaining six.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For they certainly did not act by dividing the times between them, so that, for instance, when both had been applied for a whole day, one of the drugs acted during the first six hours and the other during the remaining six.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἐρῆμος, ον, fem. ἐρήμη Od. 3.270 , S. OC 1719 (lyr.), Ant. 739 , Tr. 530 (lyr.), and in the phrase δίκη ἐρήμη (v. infr. III) : Att. ἔρημος, ον, acc. to Hdn.Gr. 2.938 : Comp. -ότερος Th. 3.11 , Lys. 29.1 , etc. : Sup. -ότατος Hdt. 9.118 :—desolate, lonely, solitary, of places, ἐς νῆσον ἐρήμην Od. 3.270 ; χῶρος Il. 10.520 ; τὰ ἐ. τῆς Λιβύης the desert parts.., Hdt. 2.32 , cf. Th. 2.17 ; ἡ ἐρῆμος (sc.χώρα) Hdt. 4.18 ; ἡ ἐρήμη Ael. NA 7.48 : pl., ib. 3.26 ; empty, πνύξ Ar. Ach. 20 . of personsor animals, τὰ δ' ἐρῆμα φοβεῖται (i.e. the sheep), Il. 5.140 ; ξέρξην ἔ. μολεῖν A. Pers. 734 (troch.) ; ἧσθαι δόμοις ἔ. Id. Ag. 862 ; πόρτις ἐρήμα S. Tr. 530 (lyr.) ; ἔ. κἄφιλος Id. Ph. 228 ; τὸν θεὸν ἔ. ἀπολιπόντε Ar. Pl. 447 ; freq. of poor, friendless persons, And. 4.15 , etc.; ἐρημότεροι, opp. δυνατώτεροι, Th. 3.11 ; οὐκ ὢν οὔτε τῶν ἐρημοτάτων οὔτε τῶν ἀπόρων κομιδῇ D. 21.111 ; εἰς ὀρφανὰ καὶ ἔ. ὑβρίζειν Pl. Ep. 1.3 ; θεῶν ἔρημα εἶναι πάντα Pl. Lg. 908c . of persons, bereft of, συμμάχων Hdt. 7.160 ; πατρός S. OC 1719 (lyr.); πατρὸς ἢ μητρός Pl. Lg. 927d ; πρὸς φίλων S. Lg. 862e . ἐρήμη, rarely ἔρημος (with or more commonly without γραφή, δίκη, δίαιτα), ἡ, an undefended action, in which one party does not appear, and judgement goes against him by default, ἤλπιζε.. τὴν γραφὴν..ἐρήμην ἔσεσθαι would be undefended, Antipho 2.1.7 ; ἐρήμῃ δίκῃ θάνατον καταγιγνώσκειν τινός Th. 6.61 ; δίκην εἷλον ἐρήμην I got judgement by default, D. 21.81 ; ἐρήμην αὐτὸν λαβόντες..εἷλον Lys. 20.18 ; τὴν ἔρημον δεδωκότα having given it by default in one's favour, D. 21.85 ; ἔρημον ὦφλε δίκην he let it go by default, ib. 87 , cf. term_table.lsj_entry_text: βαλαν-εῖον, τό, bath, bathing-room, Ar. Nu. 837 , 1054 , etc.; β. δημόσιον BGU 1130.9 (i B. C.): more freq. in pl., Ar. Nu. 991 , Eq. 1401 , etc. bath taken, Aristo Stoic. 1.88 , Gal. 11.46 .—Prose word for poet. λουτρά.
term_table.greek_sentence: οὔκουν οὐχ οὕτως συνέβη χυθῆναί τε καὶ συναχθῆναι τὴν ὑποκειμένην οὐσίαν, ὡς τοῖς λουσαμένοις μὲν ἐν βαλανείῳ, μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ εἰς ψυχρὸν ὕδωρ ἐμβᾶσιν, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον ὡς εἰ τῷ λουομένῳ προσραίνοις ὕδατος ψυχροῦ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Therefore the underlying substance did not come to be diffused and contracted in the way that happens to those who have washed in a bath and afterwards stepped into cold water, but rather as if you were to sprinkle cold water on someone while he is bathing.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Therefore the underlying substance was not diffused and drawn together in the way it is for those who have washed in a bath and afterwards stepped into cold water, but rather as if you were to sprinkle cold water on someone while he is bathing.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: αἴσθ-ησις, εως, ἡ, sense-perception, sensation, Philol. 13 , Archyt. 1 , Arist. APo. 99b35 ; τοῦ σώματος ἡ αἴ. Hp. VM 9 ; πρὸς αἴσθησιν perceptibly, Ptol. Alm. 1.10 , etc.: in pl., the senses, Democr. 9 , al.; δι' ἑπτὰ σχημάτων αἱ αἰ. Hp. Vict. 1.23 , cf. Pl. Tht. 156b , etc.: in sg. of the several senses, ἡ τοῦ ὁρᾶν αἴ. Id. R. 507e ; ἀπ' ὄψεως ἤ τινος ἄλλῃς αἰ. Id. Phlb. 39b ; organ or seat of sensation, X. Mem. 1.4.6 ; πάσα, τὰς αἰ. ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ εἶναι Arist. Fr. 95 , cf. Pr. 958b16 ; αἴ. πημάτων perception, sense of . . , E. El. 290 ; esp. of pain, Vett. Val. 113.10. al.; also of the mind, perception, knowledge of a thing, ἐν αἰ. γενέσθαι τινός Plu. Luc. 11 , etc.; αἴ. ἔχειν τινός, = αἰσθάνεσθαί τινος , have a perception of a thing, Pl. Ap. 40c ; περὶ ὑμῶν Tht. 192b ; πᾶσαν αἴσθησιν αἰσθάνεσθαι Phdr. 240d ; λαμβάνειν Isoc. 1.47 ; ἐν αἰ. εἶναι Plot. 4.7.15 :—also of things, αἴσθησιν ἔχειν give a perception, i.e. become perceptible, serving as Pass. to αἰσθάνομαι, Th. 2.61 ; more freq. αἴσθησιν παρέχειν Id. 3.22 , X. An. 4.6.13 , etc.; αἴ. ποιῆσαί τινι Antipho 5.44 , cf. D. 10.7 ; αἴ. παρέχειν τινός furnish the means of observing, Th. 2.50 ; αἴ. ἐγένετο περί τινος D. 48.16 . in object. sense, impressions of sense, Arist. term_table.greek_sentence: ὡς οὖν ἐπὶ τῶν συνθέτων φαρμάκων οὐδὲν ἐστι θαυμαστὸν ἐναντίας ἅμα διαθέσεις ἐγγίγνεσθαι τοῖς σώμασιν, οὕτως οὐδ’ ἐπὶ τῶν ἁπλῶν, ὅταν καὶ ταῦτα πρὸς μὲν τὴν ἄλλην αἴσθησίν τε καὶ διάγνωσιν ἁπλᾶ φαίνεται, πρὸς δὲ τὴν φύσιν αὐτὴν ὑπάρχῃ σύνθετα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: As, then, in the case of compound drugs it is nothing to wonder at that opposite dispositions arise simultaneously in bodies, so neither is it in the case of simple ones, when these too appear simple with respect to sensation in general and diagnosis, but are in respect of their very nature compound.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Just as, then, in the case of compound drugs there is nothing surprising in contrary conditions arising in bodies at the same time, so neither is there in the case of simple drugs, when these too appear simple to perception and diagnosis in other respects, but are compound with respect to their nature itself.

term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ μὲν δὴ καὶ ὡς ἐφ’ ὧν ἡμεῖς αὐτοὶ συντίθεμέν τι καὶ μίγνυμεν, ἐνίοτε μὲν εἰ οὕτως ἔτυχε πλέονα μὲν τὸν [591] στύφοντα χυλὸν ἐμβάλλοντες, ἐνίοτε δὲ τὸν γλυκὺν, ἢ πικρὸν, ἢ ἁλυκὸν, ἢ δριμὺ, ἤ τινα ἕτερον τῶν ἐναντίων, ἐνίοτε δ’ ἴσους ἀμφοτέρους, οὕτως ἐγχωρεῖ καὶ τὴν φύσιν ἐν δένδροις καὶ θάμνοις καὶ πόαις καὶ ζώοις καὶ κατ’ αὐτὴν τὴν γῆν μιγνύναι τοὺς ἐναντίους χυμοὺς ἢ τοῖς ὄγκοις ἢ ταῖς δυνάμεσιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And indeed, just as in the cases where we ourselves compound and mix something, sometimes, as it may happen, putting in more of the [591] astringent juice, sometimes the sweet, or bitter, or salty, or pungent, or some other of the opposites, and sometimes both in equal amounts, so it is possible also for nature, in trees and shrubs and herbs and animals and in the earth itself, to mix the opposite juices either in their bulks or in their powers, and sometimes also one of the two as predominant, so that their activities are alike in the equal mixtures, but different in the unequal ones.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Moreover, just as with the things that we ourselves compound and mix, putting in, as it may happen, sometimes more of the [591] astringent juice, sometimes more of the sweet, or bitter, or salty, or pungent, or some other of the opposites, and sometimes both in equal amounts, so too it is possible for nature, in trees and shrubs and herbs and animals and in the earth itself, to mix the opposite flavours, either in their bulks or in their powers.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ὀλίγ-ιστος, v. ὀλίγος.
term_table.greek_sentence: ὀλίγιστον γὰρ τὸ στῦφον ἐν πολλαπλασίῳ τῷ μὴ τοιούτῳ μέμικται κατὰ τὸ ῥόδον, ὥστε καὶ τῆς στύψεως ἔργα βραχέα κατὰ λόγον ἐστὶν, ἄχρι τοῦ μὴ διαλύεσθαι τῶν ὁμιλούντων αὐτῷ σωμάτων τὸν τόνον, ὑπὸ τῆς ἐν τῷ ῥόδῳ χαλαστικῆς δυνάμεως.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For in the rose a very small amount of what is astringent is mixed with a many-times-greater amount of what is not of that kind, so that the effects of its astringency too are proportionately slight, extending only so far that the tone of the bodies which come into contact with it is not dissolved by the relaxing power in the rose.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For in the rose a very small amount of the astringent is mixed with a many times greater amount of what is not such, so that the effects of its astringency are, reasonably enough, slight. They go only so far as to keep the tone of the bodies in contact with it from being dissolved by the relaxing power in the rose.

term_table.greek_sentence: οὐδὲν οὖν θαυμαστὸν ἄκος αὐτὸ φλεγμονῶν ὑπάρχειν καὶ μάλιστα ἐν ἐπιδόσει τε καὶ αὐξήσει, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἀρχομένων ἔτι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: It is therefore no wonder that it is a remedy for inflammations, and especially those in their increase and growth, or rather also those still beginning.
term_table.english_sentence_B: It is therefore no wonder that it is a remedy for inflammations, especially in their progression and increase, or rather even while they are still beginning.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἀθρόως γὰρ ἀπὸ τῶν στυφόντων καὶ συναγόντων τὴν οὐσίαν ἐπὶ τὰ χαλῶντα καὶ χέοντα μεταβαίνειν ἄτοπον, ἔν τε τῷ μεταξὺ τῆς ἀκμῆς τε καὶ ἀρχῆς αὐξανομένων ἔτι τῶν νοσημάτων οὔθ’ ἁπλῶς ἀποκρούεσθαι δίκαιον, ὡς ἐν ἀρχαῖς;
term_table.english_sentence_A: For to pass all at once from things that are astringent and contract the substance to those that relax and diffuse it is absurd, and in the interval between the peak and the beginning, when the diseases are still increasing, it is right neither simply to repel, as at the beginnings, nor yet to disperse, as at the peaks; but just as the condition of the affection is intermediate between the opposites, so too the cure must be intermediate, neither astringent, as at the beginnings, nor dispersing, as at the peaks.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For to pass all at once from things that are astringent and that draw the substance together to things that relax and diffuse it is absurd; and in the interval between the peak and the beginning, while the diseases are still increasing, it is right neither simply to repel, as at the beginnings, nor already to disperse, as at the peaks; but just as the condition of the affection is intermediate between the contraries, so the cure too must be intermediate, neither astringent, as at the beginnings, nor dispersing, as at the peaks.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: μικτός, ή, όν, mixed, blended, Ar. Th. 1114 , Pl. Phlb. 22d , etc.; opp. ἁπλοῦς, Id. R. 547e ; μ. ἐκ τούτων compounded of these, Id. Lg. 837b , cf. D.H. Dem. 41 . Adv. - τῶς Str. 1.2.27 , Gal. 9.703 . motley, POxy. 1153.14 (i A. D.). (In early texts μεικτός (which is written in PCair.Zen. 292.25 , al. (iii B. C.)) shd. prob. be restored, v. μείγνυμι. )
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ δὴ ἅπαν τὸ μέσον ἐκ τῶν ἐναντίων μικτόν ἐστιν, ἤτοι δι’ ὅλων ἀλλήλοις κεραννυμένων αὐτῶν, ἢ κατὰ σμικρὰ μόρια, καὶ τὴν αἴσθησιν ἐκφεύγοντα τῶν παρακειμένων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And indeed everything intermediate is mixed from the opposites, either by their being blended with one another throughout, or in small particles, the parts lying side by side also escaping perception.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And indeed every intermediate is mixed from the contraries, either with these blended with one another through and through, or in small particles of the things lying side by side, which escape perception.

term_table.english_sentence_A: Whether, then, you wish rose oil to have been blended from the opposites in this way or in that, to me it makes no difference, for the point at issue is demonstrated either way.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Whether, then, you would have rose oil blended from the contraries in this way or in that, it makes no difference to me; for the proposition is demonstrated either way.

term_table.greek_sentence: οἶδα δὲ ὅτι τοῖς περὶ τούτων λογισμοῖς ἅπασιν, οἷς τε ὁ Θεόφραστος [594] ἔγραψε καὶ οἷς ἡμεῖς ἐν ὅλῃ τῇδε τῇ πραγματείᾳ λέγομεν, ἐπὶ πλέον ὁμιλήσας, εὑρήσεις τὸν δεύτερον τρόπον τῆς μίξεως.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But I know that, once you have spent more time with all the arguments about these matters, both those which Theophrastus [594] wrote and those which we set forth throughout this whole treatise, you will find the second mode of mixture.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἔλαιον γὰρ καὶ ὑδρέλαιον οὐ τέγγει καλῶς αὐτὰς ἁδρομερέστερον ὑπάρχον ἢ ὡς εἴσω δύεσθαι δύνασθαι· τῷ δὲ ῥοδίνῳ συμβέβηκεν πρὸς τοῖς ἄλλοις οἷς ἔχει καὶ τὴν στύψιν ὀλίγην οὖσαν οὐ σμικρὰ συντελεῖν εἰς τοῦτο.

term_table.greek_sentence: τὰ δ’ ἐπ’ ὀλίγον μὲν στύφοντα, τὸ πλεῖστον δ’ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἔχοντα λεπτομεροῦς τε ἅμα καὶ χλιαρᾶς οὐσίας, οὐχ ὅπως οὐ κωλύεται πρὸς τῆς στύψεως ἐγκαταβαίνειν τῷ βάθει τῶν πλησιαζόντων σωμάτων, ἀλλὰ καὶ συνεργεῖται μᾶλλον ἐπωθούμενα πρὸς αὐτῆς.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But things that are astringent to a slight degree, while having in themselves for the most part a substance that is at once fine-particled and lukewarm, so far from being prevented by the astringency from descending into the depth of the bodies they come into contact with, are rather even assisted, being pushed onward by it.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἐν οἶς δ’ ἐστὶν ὑγρότης χλιαρά τε ἅμα καὶ λεπτομερὴς, ταῦτ’ οὐδὲν κωλύει διὰ μὲν τὸ λεπτομερές τε ἅμα καὶ χλιαρὸν τῆς οὐσίας ἑτοίμως κινούμενα διεξέρχεσθαι τοὺς πόρους τῶν κινουμένων σωμάτων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But those in which there is a moisture that is at once lukewarm and fine-particled — nothing prevents these, on account of the fine-particled and at the same time lukewarm character of their substance, from being readily set in motion and passing through the pores of the bodies that are moved (κινουμένων).
term_table.english_sentence_B: But as for things in which there is a moisture at once lukewarm and fine-particled, nothing prevents these, being readily moved on account of the fine-particled and lukewarm nature of their substance, from passing through the pores of the bodies being moved.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ δὲ πρὸς τῷ τοιαῦτα τυγχάνειν ὄντα καὶ βραχείας τινὸς μετέχει στύψεως, οἵας ἐπωθεῖν τε καὶ πρὸς τὸ βάθος ὅσον ἔφθασεν εἰσδῦναι τοῖς πόροις λεπτομερὲς, σφίγγειν τέ πως καὶ πυκνοῦν τὴν ἔξωθεν ἐπιφάνειαν, πάντων ταῦτα τῶν ὑγραινόντων ἄριστα δραστήρια.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And if, in addition to happening to be such, they also partake of some slight astringency, of such a kind as both to push on toward the depth whatever fine-particled part has already entered the pores, and in some way to constrict and condense the outer surface, these are the most effective of all moistening agents.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And if, besides being of this kind, they also share in some slight astringency, such as both to push onward toward the depth whatever fine-particled matter has already penetrated into the pores, and in some way to constrict and condense the outer surface, these are the most effective of all moistening agents.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: στῦψις, εως, ἡ, contraction, astringency, Thphr. Od. 32 , Diph.Siph. ap. Ath. 3.80f , Dsc. 1.39 , Sor. 1.81 , Phylotim. ap. Orib. 4.10.2 , Aret. SA 2.2 ; of food which has a costive effect, Hp. Acut. 10 , cf. Aen.Gaz. Ep. 20 ; contraction of the skin, Sch. Il. 14.216 . in dyeing, steeping of the fabric in an astringent solution, to prepare it for taking the dye, Arist. Col. 794a29 (pl.). in perfumery, thickening of oil with certain drugs to make it retain the scent longer, Dsc. 1.6 (pl.).
term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ μὲν γὰρ στύψις ἀποκλείειν φθάνουσα τοὺς πόρους, εἰς ἑαυτήν τε συνάγουσα καὶ πιλοῦσα τὴν πλησιάζουσαν οὐσίαν, ἐμποδὼν ἵσταται τοῖς τέγγειν πεφυκόσιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For astringency, when it closes off the pores beforehand, drawing together into itself and compacting the substance it comes near to, stands as an obstacle to those things whose nature is to soak.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For astringency, by closing off the pores before anything else and by drawing together into itself and compacting the substance that comes near it, stands in the way of the things naturally fitted to moisten.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: λεπτός, ή, όν, (λέπω) rare in lit. sense, peeled, husked, ῥίμφα τε λέπτ' ἐγένοντο, of barley being threshed out, Il. 20.497 . fine, small, κονίη 23.506 ; κόνις S. term_table.greek_sentence: ἡ δὲ οὕτως ἀσθενὴς, ὡς ἐν τῷ ῥοδίνῳ νικωμένη μᾶλλον ἢ νικῶσα, φθάσαι μὲν οὐχ οἵα τέ ἐστι τὰ [596] λεπτομερῆ καὶ λεπτὰ τοῦ ῥοδίνου μόρια, δυνόντων δ’ εἰς τὸ βάθος ἐκείνων ἐνεργεῖν ἄρχεται περὶ τὴν ἐκτὸς ἐπιφάνειαν, πιλοῦσα καὶ συνάγουσα καὶ πυκνοῦσα καθ’ ὅσον οἵα τέ ἐστιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But the astringency that is so weak that, in rose oil, it is overcome rather than overcoming, is not able to get ahead of the [596] fine-particled and fine parts of the rose oil; but as those sink into the depth, it begins to act about the outer surface, felting and drawing together and condensing it as far as it is able.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But astringency that is so weak, as in rose oil, where it is overcome rather than overcoming, is not able to get ahead of the [596] fine-particled and fine parts of the rose oil; rather, once those have sunk into the depth, it begins to act on the outer surface, compressing, drawing together and condensing as far as it is able.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πόρος, ὁ, (πείρω, περάω) means of passing a river, ford, ferry, Θρύον Ἀλφειοῖο π. Thryum the ford of the Alphëus, Il. 2.592 , h.Ap. 423 , cf. h.Merc. 398 ; πόρον ἷξον Ξάνθου Il. 14.433 ; Ἀξίου π. A. Pers. 493 ; ἀπικνέεται ἐς τὸν π.τῆς διαβάσιος to the place of the passage, Hdt. 8.115 ; π. διαβὰς Ἅλυος A. Pers. 864 (lyr.); τοῦ κατ' Ὠρωπὸν π. μηδὲν πραττέσθω IG 12.40.22 . narrow part of the sea, strait, διαβὰς πόρον Ὠκεανοῖο Hes. Th. 292 ; παρ' Ὠκεανοῦ . . ἄσβεστον π. A. Pr. 532 (lyr.); π. Ἕλλης ( Dor. Ἕλλας), = Ἑλλήσποντος , Pi. Fr. 189 , A. Pers. 875 (lyr.), Ar. V. 308 (lyr.); Ἰόνιος π. the Ionian Sea which is the passage-way from Greece to Italy, Pi. N. 4.53 ; πέλαγος αἰγαίου πόρου E. Hel. 130 ; Εὔξεινος, ἄξενος π. (cf. πόντος 11 ), Id. Andr. 1262 , IT 253 ; διάραντες τὸν π., i.e. the sea between Sicily and Africa, Plb. 1.37.1 ; ἐν πόρῳ in the passage-way (of ships), in the fair-way, Hdt. 7.183 , Th. 1.120 , 6.48 ; ἐν π. τῆς ναυμαχίης Hdt. 8.76 ; ἕως τοῦ π. τοῦ κατὰ τὸν ὅρμον τὸν Ἀφροδιτοπολίτην PHib. 1.38.5 (iii B.C.). periphr., πόροι ἁλός the paths of the sea, i.e. the sea, Od. 12.259 ; Αἰγαίου πόντοιο πλατὺς π. D.P. 131 ; ἐνάλιοι π. A. Pers. 453 ; π.ἁλίρροθοι ib. 367 , S. Aj. 412 (lyr.); freq. of rivers, π. Ἀλφεοῦ, Σκαμάνδρου, i.e. the Alphëus, Scamander, etc., Pi. O. 1.92 , A. Ch. 366 (lyr.), etc.; ῥυτοὶ π. Id. Eu. 452 , cf. 293 ; Πλούτωνος π. the river Pluto, Id. Pr. 806 : metaph., βίου π. the stream of life, Pi. I. 8(7).15 ; π. ὕμνων Emp. 35.1 . artificial passage over a river, bridge, Hdt. 4.136 , 140 , 7.10 . γ ́; aqueduct, IG 7.93 (Megara, V A.D. , restd.), Epigr.Gr. 1073.4 (Samos). generally, pathway, way, A. Ag. 910 , S. Ph. 705 (lyr.), etc.; track of a wild beast, X. Cyr. 1.6.40 ; αἰθέρα θ' ἁγνὸν πόρον οἰωνῶν their pathway, A. Pr. 284 (anap.); ἐν τῷ π.εἶναι to be in the way, Sammelb. 7356.11 (ii A.D.): metaph., πραπίδων πόροι A. Supp. 94 (lyr.). passage through a porous substance, opening, Epicur. Ep. 1pp.10,18 U.; esp. passage through the skin, οἱ πόροι the pores or passages by which the ἀπορροαί passed, acc. to Empedocles, πόρους λέγετε εἰς οὓς καὶ δι' ὧν αἱ ἀπορροαὶ πορεύονται Pl. Men. 76c , cf. Epicur. Fr. 250 , Metrod. Fr. 7 , Ti.Locr. 100e ; νοητοὶ π. S.E. P. 2.140 ; opp. ὄγκοι, Gal. 10.268 ; so of sponges, Arist. HA 548b31 ; of plants, Id. Pr. 905b8 , Thphr. CP 1.2.4 , HP 1.10.5 . of other ducts or openings of the body, π. πρῶτος, of the womb, Hp. ap. Poll. 2.222 ; πόροι σπερματικοί, θορικοὶ π., Arist. GA 716b17 , 720b13 ; π. ὑστερικοί the ovaries. Id. HA 570a5 , al.; τροφῆς π., of the oesophagus, Id. PA 650a15 , al.; of the rectum, Id. GA 719b29 ; of the urinal duct, ib. 773a21 ; of the arteries and veins, Id. HA 510a14 , etc. passages leading from the organs of sensation to the brain, ψυχὴ παρεσπαρμένη τοῖς π. Pl. Ax. 366a ; οἱ π. τοῦ ὄμματος Arist. Sens. 438b14 , cf. HA 495a11 , PA 656b17 ; ὤτων, μυκτήρων, Id. GA 775a2 , cf. 744a2 ; of the optic nerves, Heroph. ap. Gal. 7.89 . c. gen. rei, way or means of achieving, accomplishing, discovering, etc., οὐκ ἐδύνατο π. οὐδένα τούτου ἀνευρεῖν Hdt. 2.2 ; οὐδεὶς π. ἐφαίνετο τῆς ἁλώσιος Id. 3.156 ; τῶν ἀδοκήτων π. ηὗρε θεός E. Med. 1418 (anap.); π. ὁδοῦ a means of performing the journey, Ar. Pax 124 ; π. ζητήματος Pl. Tht. 191a ; but also π. κακῶν a means of escaping evils, a way out of them, E. Alc. 213 (lyr.): c. inf., πόρος νοῆσαι Emp. 4.12 ; π. εὐθαρσεῖν And. 2.16 ; π. τις μηχανή τε . . ἀντιτείσασθαι E. Med. 260 : with Preps., π. ἀμφί τινος A. Supp. 806 codd. (lyr.); περί τινος dub. in Ar. Ec. 653 ; πόροι πρὸς τὸ πολεμεῖν X. An. 2.5.20 . abs., providing, means of providing, opp. ἀπορία, Pl. Men. 78d sq.; contrivance, device, οἵας τέχνας τε καὶ π. ἐμησάμην A. Pr. 477 ; δεινὸς γὰρ εὑρεῖν κἀξ ἀμηχάνων πόρον ib. 59 , cf. Ar. Eq. 759 ; μέγας π. A. Pr. 111 ; τίνα π. εὕρω πόθεν; E. IA 356 (troch.). π. χρημάτων a way of raising money, financial provision, X. Ath. 3.2 , HG 1.6.12 , D. 1.19 , IG 7.4263.2 (Oropus, iii B.C.), etc.; ὁ π. τῶν χρ. D. 4.29 , IG 12(5).1001.1 (Ios, iv B.C.); without χρημάτων, SIG 284.23 (Erythrae, iv B.C.), etc.; μηχανᾶσθαι προσόδου π. X. Cyr. 1.6.10 , cf. PTeb. 75.6 (ii B.C.): in pl., 'ways and means', resources, revenue, πόροι χρημάτων D. 18.309 : abs., πόρους πορίζειν Hyp. Eux. 37 , cf. X. Cyr. 1.6.9 (sg.), Arist. Rh. 1359b23 ; πόροι ἢ περὶ προσόδων, title of work by X. : sg., source of revenue, endowment, OGI 544.24 (Ancyra, ii A.D.), 509.12 , 14 (Aphrodisias, ii A.D.), etc. assessable income or property, taxable estate, freq. in Pap., as BGU 1189.11 (i A.D.), etc.; liability, PHamb. 23.29 (vi A.D.), etc. journey, voyage, μακρᾶς κελεύθου π. A. Th. 546 ; παρόρνιθας π. τιθέντες Id. Eu. 770 , cf. E. IT 116 , etc.; ἐν τῷ π. πλοῖον ἀνατρέψαι on its passage, Aeschin. 3.158 . Π personified as father of Ἔρως, Pl. Smp. 203b .
term_table.greek_sentence: ἐξ ὧν ἀνάγκη προωθεῖσθαι μὲν εἴσω τὰ φθάσαντα τοῖς πόροις εἰσδῦναι σμικρομερῆ σώματα, κωλύεσθαι δὲ ἔξω παλινδρομεῖν ἀποκλεισθέντων τῶν πόρων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: From this it necessarily follows that the small-particled bodies which have already got in by the pores are pushed forward inward, and are prevented from running back outward, since the pores have been closed off.
term_table.english_sentence_B: From this it necessarily follows that the small-particled bodies which got ahead and entered the pores are pushed further inward, and are prevented from running back outward, since the pores have been closed off.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: δηλ-ητήριος, ον, noxious, φάρμακα SIG 37 (Teos, v B. C.), cf. J. BJ 1.13.10 , Gal. Nat.Fac. 3.7 , Hdn. 3.5.5 . δηλητήριον (sc. φάρμακον), τό, poison, Hp. Ep. 19 ( Hermes 53.69 ), Plu. 2.662c , Hdn. 1.17.10 , Lib. Or. 64.33 ; τὰ ὑγιεινὰ καὶ τὰ νοσερὰ καὶ τὰ δ. Porph. Abst. 3.8 .
term_table.greek_sentence: καὶ γὰρ εἴσω τε πρὸς ἑαυτὴν ἐπισπᾶται καὶ λεπτύνει καταθραύουσα ταύτῃ καὶ τὰ φύσει ψυχρὰ φάρμακα, τὰ δηλητήρια καλούμενα, κώνειον καὶ μήκων καὶ ὑοσκυάμου σπέρμα καὶ μανδραγόρας καὶ ὅσα ἄλλα τοιαῦτα, θᾶττόν τε καὶ μᾶλλον ἐν ταῖς θερμαῖς φύσεσιν ἐνεργεῖ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For it both draws inward toward itself and thins by breaking down; and for this reason even the drugs that are cold by nature, the so-called deleterious ones—hemlock and poppy and henbane seed and mandrake and all the others of this kind—act more quickly and more strongly in hot natures.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For it both draws inward to itself and thins by breaking up; in this way even drugs that are cold by nature, those called deleterious (hemlock and poppy and henbane seed and mandrake and all others of that kind), act faster and more strongly in hot natures.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ταχύς [υ], εῖα, ύ : of motion, swift, fleet, opp. βραδύς, of persons and animals, either abs., Il. 18.69 , etc.; or more fully, πόδας ταχύς 13.249 , 482 , 17.709 , etc.; ταχὺς ἔσκε θέειν Od. 17.308 ; θείειν τ. Il. 16.186 , Od. 3.112 ; κύνες, ἔλαφος, πτώξ, ἵππος, Il. 3.26 , 8.248 , 17.676 , 23.347 , etc.; οἰωνόν, ταχὺν ἄγγελον 24.292 , cf. Od. 15.526 ; τ. βαδιστής a quick walker, E. Med. 1182 ; σφοδροὶ καὶ τ. X. Cyr. 2.1.31 . of things, τ. πόδες Il. 6.514 , cf. Od. 13.261 , etc.; τ. ἰός, ὀϊστοί, Il. 4.94 , Od. 22.3 , etc.; πτερά Ar. Av. 1453 ; -ύτατα ἅρματα Pi. O. 1.77 ; νῆες, τριήρεις, Hdt. 8.23 , Th. 6.43 , etc.; [ ἴχνοσ] τὸ τοῦ ποδὸς μὲν βραδύ, τὸ τοῦ δὲ νοῦ ταχύ E. Ion 742 . of thought and purpose, quick, hasty, φρονεῖν γὰρ οἱ ταχεῖς οὐκ ἀσφαλεῖς S. OT 617 : c. inf., βλάπτειν τ. Ar. Ra. 1428 ; τ. βουλεῦσαί τι ἀνήκεστον Th. 1.132 , cf. 118 , Luc. Dem.Enc. 12 ; also τ. πρὸς ὀργήν Plu. Cat.Mi. 1 ; τὸ ταχύ speed, haste, E. Ph. 452 , X. Eq. 7.18 , etc. of actions, events, etc., rapid, sudden, πήδημα S. Aj. 833 ; ᾅδης, μόρος, E. Hipp. 1047 , Mosch. 3.26 ; πόλεμος Th. 4.55 , 6.45 ; φυγή Id. 4.44 ; μεταβολή Pl. R. 553d ; short, τ. ἐλπίδες fleeting hopes, Pi. P. 1.83 ; ἐπαυρέσεις Th. 2.53 ; ἀτραπός Ar. Ra. 127 ; ταχεῖ σὺν χρόνῳ S. OC 1602 ; τ. διήγησις short, rapid, Arist. Rh. 1416b30 . Adv., regul. ταχέως, quickly, opp. βραδέως, Il. 23.365 , Hes. Th. 103 , etc.:—rarely in sense perhaps (cf. τάχα 11 ), Plb. 16.25.8 . the Adv. is also expressed by periphr., διὰ ταχέων in haste, Th. 1.80 , 3.13 , Pl. Ap. 32d , X. An. 1.5.9 ; ἐκ ταχείας S. Tr. 395 ; cf. τάχος 11 . neut. ταχύ as Adv., Pi. P. 10.51 , N. 1.51 , S. Ph. 349 , E. HF 885 (lyr.), Ar. Eq. 109 , Gal. 16.665 , etc.; ἤδη ἤδη τ. τ. Sammelb. 4321.21 , BGU 956.3 (both iii A.D.); ἄρτι ἄρτι τ. τ. Arch.Pap. 5.393 (ii A.D.); also τάχα (q.v.). the Adj. ταχύς is freq. construed with Verbs, where we should use the Adv., ταχέες δ' ἱππῆες ἄγερθεν Il. 23.287 ; ταχεῖά γ' ἦλθε χρησμῶν πρᾶξις A. Pers. 739 ; ὁρμάσθω ταχύς S. Ph. 526 ; δεῦρ' ἀφίξεται τ. Id. OC 307 ; τ. χάρις διαρρεῖ Id. Aj. 1266 , cf. Th. 2.75 , 5.66 . Degrees of Comparison: Comp. : the form ταχύτερος, α, ον, is used by Hdt. , ἐποίησα ταχύτερα ἢ σοφώτερα 3.65 , cf. 7.194 ; also in Arist. Mu. 394b3 , Arr. Ind. 9.6 , Aret. SD 1.16 , but not in good Att. ; ταχύτερον as Adv., Hdt. 4.127 , 9.101 , Hp. Prog. 17 . the more usual form is θάσσων, neut. θᾶσσον, gen. ονος, Att. θάττων, neut. θᾶττον, Il. 15.570 , 13.819 (elsewh. only neut. in Hom. ), etc.:—neut. as Adv., freq. in Hom. , Od. 2.307 , al.; θᾶσσον ἂν . . κλύοιμι sooner, i.e. rather, would I hear, S. Ph. 631 ; θᾶσσον also often stands for the Positive, Il. 2.440 , Od. 15.201 , 16.130 , Pi. P. 4.181 , Ar. Nu. 506 , V. 187 , Ra. 94 ; οὐ θᾶσσον οἴσεις; i.e. make haste and bring, S. Tr. 1183 , cf. OT 430 ; θᾶττον νοήματος quicker than thought, X. Mem. 4.3.13 , cf. Ar. V. 824 , etc.; with a Conj., ὅτι θᾶσσον, like ὅτι τάχιστα , Theoc. 24.48 ; ἐπειδὴ θᾶττον συνεσκότασεν as soon as . . , D. 54.5 ; ἐπειδὰν θ. συνιῇ τις Pl. Prt. 325c ; ὅταν θ. φθέγγηται ὁ κόκκυξ Arist. HA 563b17 , cf. 611a5 ; ἐὰν or ἢν θ. as soon as . . , X. Cyr. 3.3.20 , An. 6.5.20 , Pl. Alc. 1.105a ; ἂν θ. Men. Pk. 174 ; εἰ θ. Pl. Ep. 324b ; ὡς θ. Plb. 1.66.1 , 3.82.1 ; θ. rarely = sooner than, before, ἐξήλαυνον μεσημβρίας οὐ πολλῷ τινι θ. Aristid. Or. 51 ( 27 ). 13 (cf. τάχιον infr. 3 ). the form ταχίων [ι], neut. ιον, is freq. in late Prose, as LXX Wi. 13.9 , 1 Ma. 2.40 , Ph. Bel. 69.14 , 17 , 73.23 , Gem. 1.20 , D.H. 6.42 , D.S. 20.6 , J. (v. infr.), Plu. 2.240d , Ev.Jo. 20.4 , Alciphr. 3.4 ; also in Hp. Mul. 1.1 , Men. 402.16 ; but condemned by Phryn. 58 , Hdn. Philet. p.436 P.; τὴν ταχίονα τῆς τροφῆς παράθεσιν earlier, sooner, Gal. 19.206 :—Adv. τάχιον earlier, πλέεται . . περὶ τὸν Σεπτέμβριον μῆνα . . , οὐδὲν δὲ κωλύει κἂν τ. Peripl.M.Rubr. 24 ; τ. τῆς ὑποσχέσεως sooner than they had promised, Rev.Ét.Gr. 6.159 (Iasus); τ. τοῦ παραγγέλματος J. BJ 4.4.2 ; εἰς μακρὸν αὐτῶν γῆρας καὶ βίου μῆκος ὅμοιον τοῖς τ. ἐπερχομένων Id. AJ 1.3.7 ; ἀποπαύεται οὔτε τ. ἐτῶν τεσσαράκοντα οὔτε βράδιον ἐτῶν πεντήκοντα Sor. 1.20 , cf. 48 , al.; formerly, ἐπεσκεύασαν τὸ παρόχιον, . . τ. γενόμενον γυμνάσιον IGRom. 3.639 (Lycia, ii A.D.), cf. 4.1517 (Sardis), 1632.14 (Philadelphia), 1665.5 (Tira), Keil-Premerstein Dritter Bericht p.79 (iii A.D.), Hermes 63.229 (Callatis); cf. supr. 2 fin. Sup. : the form ταχύτατος is rare, ταχύτατα ἅρματα Pi. O. 1.77 ; ταχύτατα as Adv., X. HG 5.1.27 codd., Antiph. 87 codd.; but both passages have been corrected. the usual form is τάχιστος, η, ον, used by Hom. only in neut. pl. τάχιστα as Adv., most quickly, most speedily, ὅττι τάχιστα as soon as may be, as soon as possible, Il. 4.193 , 9.659 , al.; ὅτι τάχιστα S. OT 1341 (lyr.), Th. 3.31 , etc.; so ὅσον τ. A. Ch. 772 , S. OT 1436 , etc.; ᾳ (prob.) τ. Pi. O. 13.79 ; ὅπως τ. A. Ag. 605 , S. OT 1410 , Ar. V. 167 ; ὡς τ. IG 12.76.23 , Hdt. 1.210 , Th. 4.15 , E. Rh. 147 , X. An. 1.3.14 : these are ellipt. phrases, as may be seen from the foll. examples, ὡς δυνατόν ἐστι τάχιστα Pl. Lg. 710b , X. Cyr. 5.4.3 ; ᾗ δυνατὸν τ. Id. HG 6.3.6 ; ὡς or ᾗ ἠδύνατο τ. Id. Cyr. 3.2.14 , An. 1.2.4 ; ὡς δύναιτο τ. Hdt. 1.79 ; ὡς or ᾗ ἂν δύνωμαι τ. X. HG 4.1.38 , Cyr. 7.1.9 , cf. IG 12.106.18 . τάχιστα after Particles of Time, as soon as, ἐπεὶ ( Ion. ἐπεί τε) τάχιστα A. Pr. 201 , Hdt. 1.27 , 75 , 7.163 , X. An. 7.2.6 , PCair.Zen. 34.12 (iii B.C.); ἐπειδὴ τ. Pl. Prt. 310d , Is. 9.3 , D. 27.16 , etc.; ἐπεὰν τ. Hdt. 4.134 , 7.129 , 8.144 ; ἐπὰν τ. X. An. 4.6.9 ; ἐπειδὰν τ. Id. Cyr. 1.3.14 , An. 3.1.9 ; ὅταν τ. Id. Cyr. 4.5.33 : also ὡς τ. separated by one or more words, ὡς ἡμέρη τ. ἐγεγόνεε Hdt. 1.11 , cf. 19 , 47 , 65 , al., X. Cyr. 1.3.2 , Mem. 1.2.16 , al.; ὡς δὲ τ. ἐξῆλθε . . κόρον ἔτεκε IG 42(1).121.4 (Epid., iv B.C.); ὡς γὰρ τ. εἰσῆλθον Men. Pk. 287 ; ὡς ἂν τ. λάβῃς τὴν ἐπιστολήν PCair.Zen. 241.1 (iii B.C.); but ὡς τ. γὰρ ἀπεδήμησας ib. 472.7 (iii B.C.); ὅπως τ. A. Pr. 230 :—the same notion is sometimes expressed by the part., ἀπαλλαγεὶς τάχιστα, = ὡς ἀπηλλάγη τ ., Plu. Dem. 8 , cf. 25 . freq. also in Prose, τὴν ταχίστην (in full, τὴν τ. ὁδόν X. An. 1.2.20 , Luc. Rh.Pr. 4 ) as Adv., by the quickest way, i.e. most quickly, Hdt. 1.24 , 73 , 81 , 86 , Hyp. Eux. 7 , Men. Pk. 75 , Plb. 1.33.4 , etc. (Cf. Lith. (dial.) deñgti, Lett. diêgt, both = 'run quickly', Polish dążyć 'hurry'.)

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἄπορος, ον, first in Hdt. and Pi. (v.infr.), without passage, having no way in, out, or through: hence, of places, impassable, πέλαγος, πηλός, Pl. Ti. 25d , Criti. 108e ; ὁδός, ὀρη, X. An. 2.4.4 , 2.5.18 . of states or circumstances, impracticable, difficult, Hdt. 5.3 , etc.; ἄ. ἀλγηδών, πάθη, S. R. 453d ; φόβος Lg. 698b ; βίος Men. Kith.Fr. 1.10 ; νύξ Longin. 9.10 :—ἄπορον, τό, and ἄπορα, τά, as Subst., ἐκ τῶν ἀπόρων in the midst of their difficulties, Hdt. 8.53 , cf. Pl. term_table.greek_sentence: καί σοι καὶ τοῦτο τῶν ἀπόρων ὑποληφθὲν ἓν εἶναι προβλημάτων, εἰ μὴ ῥαθύμως προσέχοις τοῖς λεγομένοις, ἑτοίμως ἕξει τὴν λύσιν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: And this too, though it has been supposed to be one of the insoluble problems, will readily have its solution for you, if you attend to what is being said not carelessly.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: πρόβλημα, ατος, τό, (προβάλλω) anything thrown forward or projecting, πόντου π. ἁλίκλυστον sea-washed promontory, S. Aj. 1219 (lyr.). hindrance, obstacle, Hp. Nat.Mul. 67 , Mul. 1.20 , Ael. NA 2.13 . anything put before one as a defence, bulwark, barrier, προβλήματα ἀντ' ἀσπίδων ἐποιεῦντο γεράνων δοράς Hdt. 7.70 , cf. 4.175 ; τῶν . . π. τὰ μὲν πρὸς τὸν πόλεμον ὁπλίσματα, τὰ δὲ φράγματα Pl. Plt. 279d sq., cf. Sph. 261a ; σώματος π., of a shield, A. Th. 540 ; νεῶν προβλήματα, of a wall, E. Rh. 213 ; χαλκᾶ προβλήματα the brazen armour of horses, X. Cyr. 6.1.51 . c.gen. objecti, defence against a thing, αἰχμῆς καὶ πέτρων A. Th. 676 ; χείματος προβλήματα E. Supp. 208 ; π. χειμώνων Pl. Ti. 74b ; π. κακῶν Ar. V. 615 ; κρύους π. ποιοῦνται τὴν ἐσθῆτα Plu. 2.691d ; but, μηδὲν φόβου π. μηδ' αἰδοῦς ἔχειν to have neither fear nor reverence as a defence, S. term_table.lsj_entry_text: ἁδρο-μερής, ές, of coarse, large grains, opp. λεπτομερής, D.S. 5.26 , Gal. 8.336 ( Sup. ); coarse, of wine, Dsc. 5.6 : Comp. -έστεροι, ὄγκοι Ph. 1.493 . Adv. -ῶς Herasap. Gal. 13.1045 .
term_table.greek_sentence: τοῦτο δ’ ἐκ μὲν τῆς οἰκείας οὐκ ἔχει φύσεως, ἁδρομερῆ τε γάρ ἐστι καὶ δυσκίνητα καὶ τὴν εἰς λεπτὰ τομὴν καὶ πρόσω φορὰν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐκ ἄν ποτε σχόντα, ἐπικτήτου τέ τινος δεῖται θερμότητος, τεμνούσης καὶ λεπτυνούσης καὶ καταθραυούσης εἰς μικρὰ καὶ οἷον ποδηγούσης τε καὶ παραγούσης, εἰς τοὺς κατὰ λεπτὸν πόρους ἁπάντων τῶν μορίων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But this they do not have from their own nature — for they are coarse-grained and hard to move, and would never of themselves have obtained division into fine parts and forward motion — and they need some acquired heat that cuts and thins and breaks them up into small pieces and, as it were, guides and conducts them into the fine pores of all the parts.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But this they do not have from their own nature, for they are coarse-grained and hard to move, and would never of themselves achieve division into fine pieces and forward movement; so they need some acquired heat, which cuts, thins and breaks them down into small pieces and, as it were, guides them on their way and leads them along into the fine pores of all the parts.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: λεπτός, ή, όν, (λέπω) rare in lit. sense, peeled, husked, ῥίμφα τε λέπτ' ἐγένοντο, of barley being threshed out, Il. 20.497 . fine, small, κονίη 23.506 ; κόνις S. Plb. 3.115.6 ; οὔτε εὐρεῖαν οὔτε λεπτὴν . . ὁδόν Plu. 2.964c (ap. Porph. Abst. 1.6 ). generally, small, weak, impotent, λεπτὴ μῆτις Il. 10.226 , 23.590 ; ἐλπίς Ar. Cyn. 5.5 ; λ. οὖας, of a child's ear, tiny, Simon. 37.14 ; τὰ λ. τῶν προβάτων small cattle, i.e. sheep and goats, Hdt. 8.137 ; λ. πλοῖα small craft, Id. 7.36 ; ἄκραι λ. small headlands, Id. 8.107 ; λ. κλιμάκια Ar. Pax 69 ; τὸ -ότατον τοῦ χαλκοῦ νομίσματος Plu. Cic. 29 ; λ. χαλκός OGI 485.12 ( Magn. Mae.): without χαλκός, Inscr.Perg. 374 D 7 ; ἀργύριον Ῥόδιον λ. CIG 2693e5 (Mylasa), cf. Coac. 310 ; λ. οἶνος light wine, Luc. Merc.Cond. 18 ; also of food, λ. δίαιται Hp. Aph. 1.4 ; λ. ὀψάρια OGI 484.16 (Pergam.). Ti. 66e ( Comp. ). of persons, οἱ λ. the poor, Plb. 24.7.3 ; λεπτὴν πλέκειν, prov. of poor people, Hsch. ; λεπτὰ ξαίνεις Suid. Subst. λεπτόν (sc. ἔντερον), τό, the small intestine, Hp. term_table.lsj_entry_text: φορά, Ion. φορή, ἡ: (φέρω):— A. as an act, (from Act. ) carrying, φορᾶς . . φθόνησις οὐ γενήσεται there shall be no refusal to carry thee, S. Fr. 300 . bringing forth, productiveness, καρποῦ Thphr. CP 3.14.5 ; opp. ἀφορία, Pl. R. 546a , cf. Arist. GA 750a23 ; of animals, Ael. NA 17.40 ; πτηνῶν Gp. 1.8.9 . (from Pass. φέρομαι) being borne or carried along, motion, of the universe and heavenly bodies. ἡ . . θεία τοῦ ὄντος φ. Pl. Cra. 421b , cf. Ti. 39b , 81a ; ἡ σύμπασα οὐρανοῦ ὁδὸς καὶ φ. Id. term_table.greek_sentence: τοῦτο δ’ ἐκ μὲν τῆς οἰκείας οὐκ ἔχει φύσεως, ἁδρομερῆ τε γάρ ἐστι καὶ δυσκίνητα καὶ τὴν εἰς λεπτὰ τομὴν καὶ πρόσω φορὰν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐκ ἄν ποτε σχόντα, ἐπικτήτου τέ τινος δεῖται θερμότητος, τεμνούσης καὶ λεπτυνούσης καὶ καταθραυούσης εἰς μικρὰ καὶ οἷον ποδηγούσης τε καὶ παραγούσης, εἰς τοὺς κατὰ λεπτὸν πόρους ἁπάντων τῶν μορίων.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But this they do not have from their own nature — for they are coarse-grained and hard to move, and would never of themselves have obtained division into fine parts and forward motion — and they need some acquired heat that cuts and thins and breaks them up into small pieces and, as it were, guides and conducts them into the fine pores of all the parts.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But this they do not have from their own nature, for they are coarse-grained and hard to move, and would never of themselves achieve division into fine pieces and forward movement; so they need some acquired heat, which cuts, thins and breaks them down into small pieces and, as it were, guides them on their way and leads them along into the fine pores of all the parts.

term_table.greek_sentence: ἔστ’ ἂν οὖν ἀπορῇ τοιαύτης, μέλλει καὶ βραδύνει, τοῖς τε μεγάλοις τῶν πόρων ἰσχόμενα καὶ ταῖς φλεψὶ καὶ ταῖς ἀρτηρίαις οἷον ἐννηχόμενα καί που τί κᾀν τῷ χρόνῳ κατὰ τὴν πολλὴν ἄλην ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν αὐταῖς χυμῶν ἀντιπάσχοντα.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So as long as they lack such heat, they delay and are slow, being held up in the large pores and, as it were, swimming about in the veins and arteries, and presumably also, in the course of time and amid their long wandering, being themselves affected in turn by the humors contained in these vessels.
term_table.english_sentence_B: So long, then, as the drug lacks such heat, it lingers and is slow, being held back in the large pores and, as it were, swimming about in the veins and arteries; and in the course of time, through its long wandering, it is perhaps also acted upon in some degree in return by the humours in them.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: ποιότης, ητος, ἡ, quality, Pl. Tht. 182a (where he apologizes for the use of the word as ἀλλόκοτον ὄνομα), Arist. Cat. 8b26 , EN 1173a15 (pl.), Gal. Nat.Fac. 1.2 , POxy. 2113.16 (iv A.D.), etc.; of size, Babr. 28.10 , Aesop. 84 .
term_table.greek_sentence: δέδεικται γὰρ ἤδη πολλάκις ὡς εἰς ἀλλήλας αἱ ποιότητες πᾶσαι δρῶσι κατά τι καὶ λίθος ἔπαθεν ὑπὸ συνεχοῦς πληγῆς ὕδατος σταλαγμοῦ καὶ ξίφος ἠμβλύνθη τέμνον κηρὸν, ἐπιδέδεικταί τε τὰς ἐν τοῖς ζώοις ἐνεργείας ὑπὸ τῶν στερεῶν σωμάτων ἐν αὐτοῖς γίγνεσθαι, ἐπειδὰν μηδέπω ταῦτ’ ᾖ κατεψυγμένα πρὸς τῶν ψυχόντων φαρμάκων, ἀναγκαῖόν [598] ἐστι περιεῖναι τῷ ζώῳ· οὐ καταψύχεται δὲ πρὶν εἰς τοὺς οἰκείους αὐτῶν πόρους ἐνδῦναι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For it has already been shown many times that all the qualities act upon one another in some respect, and that a stone has been affected by the continuous striking of a drip of water, and a sword has been blunted while cutting wax; and it has further been demonstrated that the activities in animals come about through the solid bodies within them, so that so long as these have not yet been chilled by the cooling drugs, it is necessary [598] that the animal survive; but they are not chilled before the drugs have penetrated into their proper pores.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For it has already been shown many times that all the qualities act upon one another in some respect, and that a stone has been affected by the continual striking of a drip of water, and that a sword has been blunted by cutting wax.

term_table.english_sentence_A: What guides them, as the first cause, is the attraction of the arteries, for these were shown, in dilating, to draw everything that lies near; and, as the second and material cause, the fineness of parts of the substance, which the colder and more coarse-particled drugs, not possessing it of themselves, need others to supply.
term_table.english_sentence_B: And they are not chilled before the drugs have entered into their proper passages.

term_table.greek_sentence: ὅσα τοίνυν ἐστὶ τῶν σωμάτων ψυχρὰ ταῖς κράσεσι, τήν θ’ ὁλκὴν τῶν ἀρτηριῶν ἀσθενεστέραν ἔχει ταῦτα τῶν θερμῶν, ἐδείχθη γὰρ καὶ τοῦτο, καταθραύειν ταχέως εἰς μικρὰ τὰς τῶν φαρμάκων οὐσίας ἀδυνατεῖ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Accordingly, all bodies that are cold in their mixtures both have the attraction of the arteries weaker than hot ones—for this too was shown—and are unable quickly to break down the substances of the drugs into small parts.
term_table.english_sentence_B: What guides them, as the first cause, is the attraction of the arteries, for they were shown to draw everything that is near them when they dilate; and, as the second and material cause, the fine-particledness of the substance, which the colder and more coarse-particled drugs do not have of themselves, and so they require things that will supply it.

term_table.greek_sentence: εἰ [599] γὰρ μὴ δυνηθεῖεν ἐν τάχει διαφθεῖραι, τοὐντεῦθεν ἤδη παντάπασιν ἄπρακτοι καθίστανται.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For [599] if they should not be able to destroy quickly, from that point on they become altogether ineffective.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For if [599] they are unable to destroy quickly, from that point on they become altogether ineffective.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: διά-βρωσις, εως, ἡ, eating through, τινός Plu. 2.967f (pl.); chewing, Dsc. 5.74 . Medic., erosion of the coats of a vessel, Aret. SA 2.2 , SD 2.9 (pl.), J. BJ 7.11.4 , Gal. 8.262 ; of the tissues generally, ib. 81 ; also βλεφάρων Dsc. 1.105 (pl.).
term_table.greek_sentence: τοῖς δὲ κατὰ διάβρωσίν τε καὶ σῆψιν ἀναιροῦσιν ἰσχυροῖς ὑπάρχει γίγνεσθαι χρονίζουσι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But those that kill by erosion and putrefaction have it in them to become strong as they linger.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But those that kill by erosion and putrefaction may become strong by lingering.

term_table.greek_sentence: δεόντως οὖν οἷς μὲν ἐκ τοῦ ψύχειν ἡ βλάβη, τὸ τάχος τῆς ἐνεργείας εἰς ὄλεθρον συντελεῖ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Fittingly, then, for those whose harm comes from cooling, the speed of their action contributes to destruction; for being warmed in time they lose the power by which they had their action.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Fittingly, then, for those whose harm comes from cooling, the speed of their action contributes to destruction.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: δυσ-κρασία, ἡ, bad temperament, of the air, Str. 6.4.1 , Plu. Alex. 58 (pl.); σώματος Stoic. 3.216 ; τῶν ἐν ἡμῖν δυνάμεων Ph. 1.29 . ( δυσκρασίη Man. 4.543 .)
term_table.greek_sentence: ἀπολέσθαι μὲν γὰρ ζῶον οὐκ ἐγχωρεῖ οὐδὲν, ἄνευ τοῦ παύσασθαι τὴν καρδίαν ἐνεργοῦσαν, οὐκ ἐνδέχεται δὲ παύσασθαι ταύτην ἄνευ μεγίστης τινὸς δυσκρασίας.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For no animal can perish without the heart ceasing its activity, and it is not possible for this to cease without some very great dyscrasia.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For no animal can perish without the heart ceasing from its activity, and the heart cannot cease without some very great bad mixture.

term_table.greek_sentence: οὐ γὰρ δὴ ἁπλῶς θερμοτέρα τοῦ δέοντος εἰς ὅσον ἔτυχεν ἢ ψυχροτέρα γεννηθεῖσα παύσεται κινουμένη.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For surely it will not cease moving simply because it has become hotter than is proper, to whatever degree it happens, or colder.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For it will certainly not stop moving simply by becoming hotter than it should to some chance degree, or colder.

term_table.greek_sentence: χεῖρον μὲν γὰρ ἐνεργήσει διὰ τὰς τοιαύτας δυσκρασίας, ἀκίνητος δὲ οὐκ ἔσται, πρὶν ἐξαίσιόν τινα θερμασίαν, ἢ ψύξιν, ἢ τῶν ἄλλων τινὰ τῶν δραστικῶν ποιοτήτων ἀναδέξασθαι.
term_table.english_sentence_A: For it will act worse on account of such dyscrasias, but it will not be motionless until it has received some extraordinary warmth, or cooling, or one of the other active qualities.
term_table.english_sentence_B: For it will act worse because of such bad mixtures, but it will not be motionless until it has taken on some extraordinary warmth, or cooling, or some other of the active qualities.

term_table.greek_sentence: παραπλήσιον δέ τι συμβαίνει τοῖς κατὰ ψύξιν ﻿ [600] ἀναιροῦσι φαρμάκοις, ὅταν ἐν τῷ πρὸς μὲν καρδίαν ἔρχεσθαι βραδύνῃ, τῷ πολλάκις ἐπὶ τῶν ὑγρῶν τε καὶ χλωρῶν ξύλων γιγνομένῳ.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Something similar happens to the drugs that kill by cooling, whenever they are slow in coming to the heart, to what often happens in the case of moist and green pieces of wood.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Something similar happens to the drugs that kill by cooling [600] whenever they are slow in coming to the heart, similar to what often happens with moist and green wood.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: κώνει-ον, τό, hemlock, Conium maculatum, Hp. Steril. 224 , Thphr. HP 1.5.3 , 9.8.3 , Nic. Al. 186 , Dsc. 4.78 , etc. = νάρθηξ , Call. Iamb. 1.122 , Hsch. hemlockjuice, poison by which criminals were put to death at Athens, Ar. Ra. 124 ; κώνειον πεπωκώς Pl. Ly. 219e ; τὸ κώνειον ἔπιεν X. HG 2.3.56 , cf. And. 3.10 ; κώνεια πιεῖν Ar. Ra. 1051 .
term_table.greek_sentence: οὕτως οὖν καὶ τὸ κώνειον ἄνθρωπον μὲν ἀναιρεῖ, τῇ τε τῶν πόρων εὐρύτητι καὶ τῷ πλήθει τῆς θερμότητος καὶ τῇ ῥώμῃ τῆς τῶν ἀρτηριῶν ὁλκῆς, ἰσχυρὸν ἔτι πρὸς τὴν καρδίαν ἀφικνούμενον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So too, then, hemlock kills a human being, arriving at the heart still strong, because of the width of the pores, the abundance of heat, and the strength of the attraction exerted by the arteries; but it does not kill starlings, since, owing to the opposite causes, it is held back and delayed and, in the course of that time, is first concocted beforehand and prepared beforehand, being warmed in advance by the heart as by a kind of hearth, just as the wood is outside [the fire].
term_table.english_sentence_B: In the same way, then, hemlock kills a human being, because of the width of the pores, the abundance of the heat, and the strength of the attraction of the arteries, since it arrives at the heart while still strong.

term_table.greek_sentence: οὕτως οὖν καὶ τὸ κώνειον ἄνθρωπον μὲν ἀναιρεῖ, τῇ τε τῶν πόρων εὐρύτητι καὶ τῷ πλήθει τῆς θερμότητος καὶ τῇ ῥώμῃ τῆς τῶν ἀρτηριῶν ὁλκῆς, ἰσχυρὸν ἔτι πρὸς τὴν καρδίαν ἀφικνούμενον.
term_table.english_sentence_A: So too, then, hemlock kills a human being, arriving at the heart still strong, because of the width of the pores, the abundance of heat, and the strength of the attraction exerted by the arteries; but it does not kill starlings, since, owing to the opposite causes, it is held back and delayed and, in the course of that time, is first concocted beforehand and prepared beforehand, being warmed in advance by the heart as by a kind of hearth, just as the wood is outside [the fire].
term_table.english_sentence_B: In the same way, then, hemlock kills a human being, because of the width of the pores, the abundance of the heat, and the strength of the attraction of the arteries, since it arrives at the heart while still strong.

term_table.greek_sentence: οὐκ ἀναιρεῖ δὲ τοὺς ψάρας, ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐναντίοις αἰτίοις ἐπεχόμενόν τε καὶ βρα δῦνον καὶ φθάνον ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ προπέττεσθαι καὶ προπαρασκευάζεσθαι, καθάπερ ἑστίᾳ τινὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ προθερμαινόμενον, ὡς ἔξω τὸ ξύλον ὥστε οὐδὲ τοῦτο θαυμαστὸν οὐδὲ ἄπορον, ἀλλ’ οἷόν τι καὶ ταῖς θριδακίναις ὑπάρχει.

term_table.english_sentence_B: But it does not kill starlings, since for the opposite causes it is held back and slowed, and has time to be concocted beforehand and prepared beforehand, being warmed beforehand by the heart as by a kind of hearth, as the wood is outside. term_table.english_sentence_A: But if someone should already have drunk the juice of the poppy, which is of such a nature as to kill, and yet still be alive, then reasonably [604] this person too is cured by old wine drunk in quantity, and the more so if it should be one of the noble wines; for it also heats more.

(v. infr. 11.2 ), Polem.Hist. 88 , Polyaen. 8.6.1 ):— poppy, esp. opium poppy, Papaver somniferum, μήκων δ' ἑτέρωσε κάρη βάλεν ἐνὶ κήπῳ Il. 8.306 , cf. Ar. Av. 160 , Thphr. HP 1.12.2 (s. v.l.), Theoc.l.c.; μάκωνσι λευκαῖς IGl.c.; μ. ἥμερος, κηπευτή, Dsc. 4.64 , Gal. 6.548 ; μ. Ἡρακλεία frothy poppy, Silene venosa, Thphr. HP 9.12.5 ; μ. ἀφρώδης Dsc. 4.66 ; μ. κερατῖτις horned poppy, Glaucium flavum, Thphr. HP 9.12.3 , Dsc. 4.65 (but = λεοντοπέταλον , Ps.- Dsc. 3.96 ); μ. μέλαινα corn poppy, Papaver Rhoeas, Thphr. HP 9.12.4 , Dsc. 4.63 ; μ. ἀγρία, = μ. μέλαινα , ib. 64 ; μ. ἀγριωτέρα windrose, Papaver argemone, ibid. a single poppy-seed, Archim. Aren. 2.4 ; collectively, μ. ἁδρά Hp. Mul. 2.192 ; μ. μεμελιτωμένη Th. 4.26 ; ὀπὸς μήκωνος opium, Asclep. ap. Gal. 14.138 , etc. poppy-head, Thphr. HP 4.8.10 : as an architectural ornament, Paus. 5.20.5 . quasiliver of testaceous animals (ὀστρακηρά), Arist. HA 530a15 , 547a16 . ink-bag of the cuttle-fish, Id. Fr. 334 (masc.), Ael. NA ap. Suid. a metallic sand, Poll. 7.100 . the part of the ear at the root under the lobe, Id. 2.86 . μ. ἀφρώδης, = πέπλος , spurge, Dsc. 4.167 ; so μ. alone, as a purgative, freq. in Hp., Mul. 2.124 , 192 , al., Morb. 3.16 ; ὀπὸς μήκωνος Mul. 2.201 ; μ. alone, = τιθυμαλλίς , Dsc. 4.164 . (Etym. dub.; OHG. māgo, Germ. mohn, OSlav.makû are prob. borrowed.)
term_table.greek_sentence: τοιοῦτος οὖν οἶνος τῇ φύσει καὶ παλαιὸς τὴν ἡλικίαν, ἀκρατέστερος ﻿ [605] κεραννύμενος ἰᾶται καὶ τοὺς ἤδη κατεψυγμένους οὐχ ὑπὸ μήκωνος ὀποῦ μόνον, ἤ τινος ἄλλου τῶν τοιούτων ψυχόντων φαρμάκων, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς ἤτοι στομαχικῶς ἢ καρδιακῶς ἐν νόσοις συγκοπτομένους.
term_table.english_sentence_A: Such a wine, then, in its nature, and old in age, when mixed rather strong [605] cures also those who have already been chilled, not only by poppy juice or by some other of such cooling drugs, but also those who in diseases fall into syncope either stomachically or cardiacally.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Such a wine, then, of this kind by nature and old in age, when mixed rather undiluted [605], cures not only those already chilled by poppy juice or by some other of the cooling drugs of this kind, but also those who in diseases suffer syncope, whether of the stomachic or of the cardiac sort.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: φάρμακον [v. sub fin.], τό, drug, whether healing or noxious: in Hom. the sense is freq. determined by an epith., φάρμακα, πολλὰ μὲν ἐσθλὰ . . , πολλὰ δὲ λυγρά Od. 4.230 ; τόδε φ. ἐσθλόν 10.287 , cf. 292 ; φ. ἤπια, ὀδυνήφατα (v. infr. 2 ); κακὰ φ. ib. 213 ; φ. λυγρά ib. 236 ; φ. οὐλόμενον ib. 394 ; ἀνδροφόνον 1.261 ; θυμοφθόρα φ. 2.329 ; so, after Hom. , προσανέα φ. Pi. P. 3.52 ; παιώνια A. Ag. 848 ; χρήσιμον Pl. R. 382c ; θανάσιμα Ph. Bel. 103.31 ; ὀλέθριον Luc. Herm. 62 . healing remedy, medicine, in Hom. mostly of those applied outwardly, ἐπιθήσει φάρμαχ' ἅ κεν παύσῃσι μελαινάων ὀδυνάων Il. 4.191 ; ἐπ' ἄρ' ἤπια φάρμακα πάσσε ib. 218 ; ὀδυνήφατα φ. πάσσων 5.401 , 900 , cf. 11.515 , 830 , 15.394 ; προσάλειφεν ἑκάστῳ φ. Od. 10.392 ; φ. περιαλείφειν Ar. Eq. 906 ; also of potions, πιὼν φάρμακ' Od. 10.326 ; φ. πεπωκώς Hdt. 4.160 , cf. Pi. l. c.; παρὰ τοῦ ἰατροῦ Pl. R. 406d , cf. Grg. 467c ; φ. χριστόν E. Hipp. 516 ; ἔγχριστον Theoc. 11.1 ; ἐπίχριστον Str. 17.1.10 ; ἐπίπαστον Theoc. l. c.; καταπλαστόν Ar. Pl. 716 ; ποτόν E. Hipp. l.c.; freq. in Medic. writers, Sor. 1.4 , Gal. 6.265 , etc.; of medicines for cattle, PFlor. 222.11 (iii A. D.). c. gen. (v. infr. 11 ), φ. νόσου a medicine for it, remedy against it, A. Pr. 251 , 606 (lyr.); βηχός Phryn.Com. 60 : κεφαλῆς for a head-ache, Pl. Chrm. 155b ; στραγγουρίας Arist. HA 612b16 , cf. 624a16 ; μέθης Amphis 37 ; δίψης AP 6.170 ( Thyill. ); but ὑγιείας φ. a medicine to restore or maintain health, Aristid. Or. 37(2).11 . enchanted potion, philtre: hence, charm, spell, Od. 4.220 sq., Ar. Pl. 302 , Theoc. 2.15 , PSI 1.64.20 (i B. C.); φαρμάκοις τὸν ἄνδρ' ἔμηνεν Ar. Th. 561 ; τοιαῦτα ἔχω φ. such charms have I, Hdt. 3.85 , cf. Apoc. 9.21 . poison, S. Tr. 685 , E. Med. 385 ; πιεῖν τὸ φ. Antipho 6.15 , Pl. Phd. 57a , 115a ; φάρμακα ἐσβεβληκέναι ἐς τὰ φρέατα Th. 2.48 ; φ. δηλητήρια SIG 37 A 1 (Teos, v B. C.); τοξικὸν φ. BGU 21 ii 14 (iv A. D.). lye for laundering, Stud.Pal. 22.56.12 (iii A. D.). generally, remedy, cure, Hes. Op. 485 , Alc. 35 , etc.; μεῖζον . . τῆς νόσου τὸ φ. the cure too strong for, i. e. worse than, the disease, S. Fr. 589.4 , cf. Com.Adesp. 455 ; φ. πραΰ, of a bridle, Pi. O. 13.85 ; φ. τινι for a thing, Thgn. 1134 (pl.), Archil. 9 ; πρός τι Arist. Pol. 1321a16 ; ποττὸν ἔρωτα Theoc. 11.1 ; but most freq. φ. τινός remedy against . . χλαῖνα . . φ. ῥίγευς Hippon. 19 ; Ζεὺς πάντων φ. μοῦνος ἔχει Simon. 87 ; τὸ σιγᾶν φ. βλάβης ἔχω A. Ag. 548 ; φ. πόνων, λύπης, E. Ba. 283 , Fr. 1079 ; δόλοι . . χρείας ἀνάνδρου φ. ib. 288 ; φόβου Pl. Lg. 647e ; λήθης φάρμακα (of γράμματα) E. Fr. 578.1 ; v. εὐδιανός. c. gen. also, a means of producing something, φ. σωτηρίας Id. Ph. 893 ; μνήμης καὶ σοφίας φ. Pl. Phdr. 274e ; ὑπομνήσεως ib. 275a , cf. 230d ; ἀθανασίας Antiph. 86.6 ; ἡσυχίας Arist. Pol. 1273b23 ; φ. μανίας, of the oil applied to wrestlers, D.L. 1.104 . ἐπὶ θανάτῳ φ. ἑᾶς ἀρετᾶς εὑρέσθαι a remedy or consolation in his own virtue, Pi. P. 4.187 . dye, paint, colour, Emp. 23.3 , Hdt. 1.98 , A. Fr. 134 , Ar. Ec. 735 , Pl. R. 420c , Plt. 277c , PCair.Zen. 789.13 (iii B. C.), etc. chemical reagent, PLeid.X. 25 , PHolm. 13.46 , 22.10 , Ps.-Democr. ap. Zos.Alch. p.160 B. ; used by tanners, Sch. Ar. Eq. 44 , 368 .—Cf. φαρμάσσω. [μα; but μα in φαρμακός.]
term_table.greek_sentence: ὁ δὲ σὺν αὐτοῖς τοῖς ψύχουσι φαρμάκοις πινόμενος ὑπὲρ τοῦ θᾶττον ἀναιρεῖν, οὔτε πολὺς οὗτός ἐστιν οὔτ’ εὐγενὴς, ἀλλ’ ὅσον εἰς τὸ καταθραῦσαί τε καὶ παραπέμψαι μόνον ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτὰ τῇ ῥύμῃ τῆς ἀναδόσεως.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But the wine that is drunk together with the cooling drugs themselves in order to kill more quickly—this is neither much nor of noble quality, but only so much as suffices to break them up and to convey them to the heart by the impetus of the distribution.
term_table.english_sentence_B: But the wine that is drunk together with the cooling drugs themselves in order to kill more quickly is neither much nor of a noble kind; it is only as much as serves to break them up and to convey them to the heart by the impetus of the distribution.

term_table.lsj_entry_text: σηπεδών, όνος, ἡ, (σήπομαι) decay, putrefaction, in animal bodies or wood, or even stone, Hp. Epid. 3.4 , Antipho Soph. 15 , Pl. Phd. 110e , Thphr. CP 6.1.5 ; σηπεδόνα λαβεῖν Pl. Phd. 96b . of live flesh, mortification, of two kinds, ς. χλωρή (v. σῆψις) when a humour discharges, and ξηρή when it is dry, Hp. Epid. 5.4 . pl., putrid humours, Id. Aph. 3.16 (sg. in 7.20 ), Plb. 1.81.7 , Com.Adesp. 344 , etc. a serpent whose bite causes putrefaction, Nic. Th. 327 , Ael. NA 15.18 .
term_table.greek_sentence: Ἐπεὶ δὲ καὶ περὶ τῶν κατὰ σηπεδόνα καὶ διάβρωσιν ἀναιρούντων φαρμάκων ἐρεῖν ὑπεσχόμην, ὡς ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ χείρω γίγνεται καὶ τῷ γένει φθαρτικὰ τῆς ἡμετέρας ὑπάρχει φύσεως, οὐχ ὡς τὰ ψύχοντα τῷ πλήθει μόνον, ἤδη μοι καιρὸς ἂν εἴη καὶ περὶ τούτων εἰπεῖν.
term_table.english_sentence_A: But since I also promised to speak about the drugs that kill by putrefaction and erosion—that they become worse with time, and that they are destructive of our nature in their kind, not, like the cooling drugs, merely by their quantity—it would now be the time for me to speak about these as well.
term_table.english_sentence_B: Since I also promised to speak about the drugs that kill by way of putrefaction and erosion, explaining how they become worse with time and are by their kind destructive of our nature, and not, like the cooling drugs, by their quantity alone, it would now be time for me to speak about these as well.
